meta.title: Jesus Says Data Catalog
meta.subtitle: A Comprehensive Categorization of His Words as Recorded in the New Testament

teachings.text: Jesus teaches that the Father knows what his children need before they ask. He sees what is done in secret in giving, prayer, and fasting, and rewards openly.
teachings.quote: Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.
teachings.title: The Father Knows What You Need

teachings.text: Jesus teaches that if evil men give good gifts to their children, how much more will the Father in heaven give to those who ask.
teachings.quote: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children, how much more shall your Father which is in heaven give good things to them that ask him?
teachings.title: How Much More Will the Father Give

teachings.text: Jesus says not one sparrow falls to the ground without the Father, and the very hairs of his hearers' heads are all numbered. He tells them not to fear, for they are of more value than many sparrows.
teachings.quote: Are not two sparrows sold for a farthing? and one of them shall not fall on the ground without your Father. But the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear ye not therefore, ye are of more value than many sparrows.
teachings.title: You Are Worth More Than Many Sparrows

teachings.text: Jesus charges his hearers to call no man their father upon the earth, for one is their Father, who is in heaven.
teachings.quote: And call no man your father upon the earth: for one is your Father, which is in heaven.
teachings.title: One Is Your Father Who Is in Heaven

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Samaritan woman the hour comes when worship will not be at this mountain or Jerusalem, for salvation is of the Jews.
teachings.quote: Woman, believe me, the hour cometh, when ye shall neither in this mountain, nor yet at Jerusalem, worship the Father. Ye worship ye know not what: we know what we worship: for salvation is of the Jews.
teachings.title: Worship Will Not Be Bound to One Place

teachings.text: Jesus declares that true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth, for God is a Spirit and the Father seeks such.
teachings.quote: But the hour cometh, and now is, when the true worshippers shall worship the Father in spirit and in truth: for the Father seeketh such to worship him. God is a Spirit: and they that worship him must worship him in spirit and in truth.
teachings.title: True Worshippers Worship in Spirit and Truth

teachings.text: Jesus thanks the Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that he has hidden these things from the wise and revealed them to babes.
teachings.quote: I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes. Even so, Father: for so it seemed good in thy sight.
teachings.title: God Reveals Himself to the Humble

teachings.text: Jesus says that with men it is impossible but with God all things are possible, and that as the Father raises the dead and gives life, so the Son gives life to whom he will.
teachings.quote: With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.
teachings.title: With God All Things Are Possible

teachings.text: Jesus declares that God so loved the world he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have everlasting life.
teachings.quote: ¶ For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.
teachings.title: God So Loved the World He Gave His Son

teachings.text: Jesus says all the Father gives him will come to him, and he will not cast out the one who comes. No one can come unless the Father draws him, and he will raise him up at the last day.
teachings.quote: All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out. No man can come to me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him: and I will raise him up at the last day.
teachings.title: All the Father Gives Will Come to the Son

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples that the Father himself loves them because they have loved him and believed that he came out from God, and that the Father has committed all judgment to the Son.
teachings.quote: For the Father himself loveth you, because ye have loved me, and have believed that I came out from God.
teachings.title: The Father Loves Those Who Love the Son

categories.title: The Identity of Jesus Christ
categories.description: Jesus made explicit claims about his own nature, origin, authority, and mission that form the theological core of his teaching.

teachings.text: Jesus declares that he is the bread of life and the living bread come down from heaven, that whoever comes to him will never hunger and whoever believes will never thirst, and the bread he gives for the world's life is his flesh.
teachings.quote: I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst. I am that bread of life. I am the living bread which came down from heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: and the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world.
teachings.title: I AM the Bread of Life

teachings.text: Jesus declares that he is the light of the world, and whoever follows him will not walk in darkness but have the light of life.
teachings.quote: I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.
teachings.title: I AM the Light of the World

teachings.text: Jesus warns that unless his hearers believe that he is he, they will die in their sins, and declares that he speaks to the world the things he has heard from the Father who sent him, who is true.
teachings.quote: I said therefore unto you, that ye shall die in your sins: for if ye believe not that I am he, ye shall die in your sins. Even the same that I said unto you from the beginning. I have many things to say and to judge of you: but he that sent me is true; and I speak to the world those things which I have heard of him.
teachings.title: I AM He — Believe or Die in Your Sins

teachings.text: Jesus declares that before Abraham was, I am.
teachings.quote: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am.
teachings.title: Before Abraham Was, I AM

teachings.text: Jesus declares that the true shepherd enters by the door and his sheep know his voice. He calls himself the door by which any may enter and be saved, and the good shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep, knows his own as the Father knows him, and has other sheep he must bring, so there will be one flock and one shepherd.
teachings.quote: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that entereth not by the door into the sheepfold, but climbeth up some other way, the same is a thief and a robber. But he that entereth in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep. To him the porter openeth; and the sheep hear his voice: and he calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out. And when he putteth forth his own sheep, he goeth before them, and the sheep follow him: for they know his voice. And a stranger will they not follow, but will flee from him: for they know not the voice of strangers. Verily, verily, I say unto you, I am the door of the sheep. All that ever came before me are thieves and robbers: but the sheep did not hear them. I am the door: by me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, and shall go in and out, and find pasture. I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep. But he that is an hireling, and not the shepherd, whose own the sheep are not, seeth the wolf coming, and leaveth the sheep, and fleeth: and the wolf catcheth them, and scattereth the sheep. The hireling fleeth, because he is an hireling, and careth not for the sheep. I am the good shepherd, and know my sheep, and am known of mine. As the Father knoweth me, even so know I the Father: and I lay down my life for the sheep. And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.
teachings.title: I AM the Good Shepherd

teachings.text: Jesus declares that he is the resurrection and the life, and that whoever believes in him, though he die, will live.
teachings.quote: I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:
teachings.title: I AM the Resurrection and the Life

teachings.text: Jesus declares that he is the way, the truth, and the life, and that no one comes to the Father except through him.
teachings.quote: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
teachings.title: I AM the Way, the Truth, and the Life

teachings.text: Jesus declares that he is the true vine, his Father the vinedresser, and his disciples the branches who apart from him can do nothing.
teachings.quote: I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman. I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
teachings.title: I AM the True Vine

teachings.text: Jesus declares he is Alpha and Omega, the beginning and end, the first and last, the root and offspring of David, the bright morning star.
teachings.quote: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last. I Jesus have sent mine angel to testify unto you these things in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, and the bright and morning star.
teachings.title: I AM the Alpha and Omega, Root of David

teachings.text: As a boy in the temple, Jesus asks his parents why they sought him and did not know he must be about his Father's business.
teachings.quote: How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father’s business?
teachings.title: The Boy Jesus About His Father's Business

teachings.text: Jesus declares that the Father loves the Son and has given all things into his hand. All things are delivered to him, and no one knows the Son but the Father, nor the Father except the Son and those he reveals him to.
teachings.title: The Father Has Given All Things to the Son

teachings.text: Jesus answers his accusers by declaring that his Father works until now, and he works.
teachings.quote: My Father worketh hitherto, and I work.
teachings.title: The Father Works and So Does the Son

teachings.text: Jesus teaches that the Son does nothing but what he sees the Father do, for the Father shows him all his works in love.
teachings.quote: Verily, verily, I say unto you, The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do: for what things soever he doeth, these also doeth the Son likewise. For the Father loveth the Son, and sheweth him all things that himself doeth: and he will shew him greater works than these, that ye may marvel.
teachings.title: The Son Does Only What He Sees the Father Do

teachings.text: Jesus declares his judgment is just because he seeks not his own will but the Father's, and names as witnesses John the Baptist, the works the Father has given him to finish, and the Father himself who has borne witness of him.
teachings.quote: I can of mine own self do nothing: as I hear, I judge: and my judgment is just; because I seek not mine own will, but the will of the Father which hath sent me. If I bear witness of myself, my witness is not true. ¶ There is another that beareth witness of me; and I know that the witness which he witnesseth of me is true. Ye sent unto John, and he bare witness unto the truth. But I receive not testimony from man: but these things I say, that ye might be saved. He was a burning and a shining light: and ye were willing for a season to rejoice in his light. ¶ But I have greater witness than that of John: for the works which the Father hath given me to finish, the same works that I do, bear witness of me, that the Father hath sent me. And the Father himself, which hath sent me, hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen his shape. And ye have not his word abiding in you: for whom he hath sent, him ye believe not.
teachings.title: Jesus Seeks the Father's Will, Not His Own

teachings.text: Jesus declares his doctrine is not his own but his Father's who sent him, and anyone willing to do God's will can know whether the doctrine is from God or whether he speaks of himself, for he who speaks of himself seeks his own glory.
teachings.quote: My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me. If any man will do his will, he shall know of the doctrine, whether it be of God, or whether I speak of myself. He that speaketh of himself seeketh his own glory: but he that seeketh his glory that sent him, the same is true, and no unrighteousness is in him. Did not Moses give you the law, and yet none of you keepeth the law? Why go ye about to kill me?
teachings.title: Christ's Doctrine Comes from the Father

teachings.text: Jesus tells them they judge by the flesh while he judges none, yet his judgment is true, for the Father is with him.
teachings.quote: Ye judge after the flesh; I judge no man. And yet if I judge, my judgment is true: for I am not alone, but I and the Father that sent me.
teachings.title: The Father Is with Jesus in His Judgment

teachings.text: Jesus tells his hearers they neither know him nor his Father, and that if they had known him they would have known his Father also.
teachings.quote: Ye neither know me, nor my Father: if ye had known me, ye should have known my Father also.
teachings.title: To Know Jesus Is to Know the Father

teachings.text: Jesus declares his honor comes from the Father, whom they call God yet do not know, while he knows him and keeps his word.
teachings.quote: If I honour myself, my honour is nothing: it is my Father that honoureth me; of whom ye say, that he is your God: Yet ye have not known him; but I know him: and if I should say, I know him not, I shall be a liar like unto you: but I know him, and keep his saying.
teachings.title: Jesus Knows and Keeps the Father's Word

teachings.text: Jesus declares that he and the Father are one, and bids his hearers, though they do not believe him, to believe the works that they may know the Father is in him and he in the Father.
teachings.quote: I and my Father are one. But if I do, though ye believe not me, believe the works: that ye may know, and believe, that the Father is in me, and I in him.
teachings.title: Jesus and the Father Are One

teachings.text: Jesus asks for which of the many good works he has shown them from the Father they seek to stone him.
teachings.quote: Many good works have I shewed you from my Father; for which of those works do ye stone me?
teachings.title: Which Good Work Merits Stoning

teachings.text: Jesus cites their law that says, you are gods, and asks why they call it blasphemy when he whom the Father has sanctified and sent into the world says he is the Son of God, since the scripture cannot be broken.
teachings.quote: Is it not written in your law, I said, Ye are gods? If he called them gods, unto whom the word of God came, and the scripture cannot be broken; Say ye of him, whom the Father hath sanctified, and sent into the world, Thou blasphemest; because I said, I am the Son of God?
teachings.title: The Father Sanctified and Sent the Son

teachings.text: Jesus declares that whoever believes in him believes in him who sent him, and whoever sees him sees the one who sent him. He came as light into the world so that whoever believes will not abide in darkness, not to judge but to save.
teachings.quote: He that believeth on me, believeth not on me, but on him that sent me. And he that seeth me seeth him that sent me. I am come a light into the world, that whosoever believeth on me should not abide in darkness. And if any man hear my words, and believe not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world.
teachings.title: To See Me Is to See the Father

teachings.text: Jesus declares he has not spoken of himself; the Father who sent him gave him commandment what to say, and his commandment is everlasting life.
teachings.quote: For I have not spoken of myself; but the Father which sent me, he gave me a commandment, what I should say, and what I should speak. And I know that his commandment is life everlasting: whatsoever I speak therefore, even as the Father said unto me, so I speak.
teachings.title: The Father's Commandment Is Everlasting Life

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples that had they known him, they would have known his Father; from now on they know him and have seen him.
teachings.quote: If ye had known me, ye should have known my Father also: and from henceforth ye know him, and have seen him.
teachings.title: To Know Jesus Is to Have Seen the Father

teachings.text: Jesus answers Philip, asking how he has been so long with them and yet not known him, and declares that whoever has seen him has seen the Father, so why does Philip ask, show us the Father.
teachings.quote: Have I been so long time with you, and yet hast thou not known me, Philip? he that hath seen me hath seen the Father; and how sayest thou then, Shew us the Father?
teachings.title: Whoever Has Seen Jesus Has Seen the Father

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples he goes away and comes again; if they loved him they would rejoice he goes to the Father, greater than he.
teachings.quote: Ye have heard how I said unto you, I go away, and come again unto you. If ye loved me, ye would rejoice, because I said, I go unto the Father: for my Father is greater than I.
teachings.title: Jesus Goes to the Father Greater Than He

teachings.text: Jesus declares he has not come to destroy the law or prophets but to fulfill them. He came to call sinners to repentance, seek the lost, and give his life a ransom for many.
teachings.quote: ¶ Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil.
teachings.title: Christ Came to Fulfill, Seek, and Ransom

teachings.text: Jesus declares the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins and tells the paralyzed man to rise and go home. He also names himself Lord of the Sabbath.
teachings.quote: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thine house.
teachings.title: The Son of Man Has Authority to Forgive Sin

teachings.text: Jesus says every kingdom divided against itself cannot stand. He asks how Satan's kingdom can stand if Satan casts out Satan, declares that if he casts out devils by the Spirit of God the kingdom of God has come, and likens his work to binding the strong man before plundering his house. Whoever is not with him is against him.
teachings.quote: Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation; and every city or house divided against itself shall not stand: And if Satan cast out Satan, he is divided against himself; how shall then his kingdom stand? And if I by Beelzebub cast out devils, by whom do your children cast them out? therefore they shall be your judges. But if I cast out devils by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God is come unto you. Or else how can one enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man? and then he will spoil his house. He that is not with me is against me; and he that gathereth not with me scattereth abroad.
teachings.title: Jesus Casts Out Demons by the Spirit of God

teachings.text: Jesus answers the chief priests by saying he will tell them his authority if they first say whether John's baptism was from heaven or men.
teachings.quote: I also will ask you one thing, which if ye tell me, I in like wise will tell you by what authority I do these things. The baptism of John, whence was it? from heaven, or of men?
teachings.title: Jesus Challenges the Source of John's Baptism

teachings.text: Jesus tells the chief priests that neither will he tell them by what authority he does these things.
teachings.quote: Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.
teachings.title: Jesus Declines to Reveal His Authority

teachings.text: Jesus declares that all power is given to him in heaven and on earth.
teachings.quote: All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.
teachings.title: All Power in Heaven and Earth Given to Christ

teachings.text: Jesus asks the Pharisees if they never read how hungry David entered the house of God and ate the showbread lawful only for priests.
teachings.quote: Have ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was an hungred, he, and they that were with him? How he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and did eat the shewbread, which is not lawful to eat but for the priests, and gave also to them which were with him?
teachings.title: David Ate the Showbread — Who Is Lord Here

teachings.text: Jesus calls the man with the withered hand forward and asks whether it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath or evil, to save life or to kill. Then he commands the man to stretch out his hand.
teachings.quote: Stand forth. Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath days, or to do evil? to save life, or to kill? Stretch forth thine hand.
teachings.title: Is It Lawful to Do Good on the Sabbath

teachings.text: Jesus says he has come to send fire on the earth and asks what he wills if it is already kindled.
teachings.quote: ¶ I am come to send fire on the earth; and what will I, if it be already kindled?
teachings.title: Christ Came to Cast Fire on the Earth

teachings.text: Jesus says to his mother at Cana, Woman, what have I to do with you, and tells her his hour has not yet come.
teachings.quote: Woman, what have I to do with thee? mine hour is not yet come.
teachings.title: Christ's Hour Has Not Yet Come

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples he has food to eat that they know nothing of.
teachings.quote: I have meat to eat that ye know not of.
teachings.title: Jesus Has Food the Disciples Know Nothing Of

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples this man's blindness is not from sin but so the works of God can be displayed in him.
teachings.quote: Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him. I must work the works of him that sent me, while it is day: the night cometh, when no man can work.
teachings.title: Blindness Displayed for the Works of God

teachings.text: Jesus says this sickness is not unto death but for the glory of God, that the Son of God might be glorified by it.
teachings.quote: This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that the Son of God might be glorified thereby.
teachings.title: This Sickness Is for the Glory of God

teachings.text: Jesus asks whether there are not twelve hours in the day, saying one who walks by day does not stumble while one who walks by night stumbles. Then he tells the disciples their friend Lazarus sleeps and he goes to wake him.
teachings.quote: Are there not twelve hours in the day? If any man walk in the day, he stumbleth not, because he seeth the light of this world. But if a man walk in the night, he stumbleth, because there is no light in him. Our friend Lazarus sleepeth; but I go, that I may awake him out of sleep.
teachings.title: Jesus Goes to Wake Lazarus from Sleep

teachings.text: Jesus assures Martha that her brother will rise again.
teachings.quote: Thy brother shall rise again.
teachings.title: Martha's Brother Will Rise Again

teachings.text: Jesus declares that no one has ascended to heaven but he who came down from heaven, the Son of Man who is in heaven.
teachings.quote: And no man hath ascended up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven, even the Son of man which is in heaven.
teachings.title: The Son of Man Descended from Heaven

teachings.text: Jesus says he came from heaven to do the Father's will — to lose none given him but raise them up at the last day.
teachings.quote: For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me. And this is the Father’s will which hath sent me, that of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing, but should raise it up again at the last day.
teachings.title: Christ Came from Heaven to Do the Father's Will

teachings.text: Jesus tells the crowd not to grumble among themselves.
teachings.quote: Murmur not among yourselves.
teachings.title: Do Not Grumble Among Yourselves

teachings.text: Jesus asks the murmuring disciples whether his saying offends them, and what if they see the Son of Man ascend where he was before.
teachings.quote: Doth this offend you? What and if ye shall see the Son of man ascend up where he was before?
teachings.title: What If They See the Son Ascend as Before

teachings.text: Jesus tells his brothers his time has not yet come while theirs is always ready. The world cannot hate them but hates him because he testifies its works are evil. He bids them go up to the feast though he does not yet go.
teachings.quote: My time is not yet come: but your time is alway ready. The world cannot hate you; but me it hateth, because I testify of it, that the works thereof are evil. Go ye up unto this feast: I go not up yet unto this feast; for my time is not yet full come.
teachings.title: The World Hates Christ Because He Tells the Truth

teachings.text: Jesus cries in the temple that he did not come of himself but is sent by one who is true, whom they do not know.
teachings.quote: Ye both know me, and ye know whence I am: and I am not come of myself, but he that sent me is true, whom ye know not. But I know him: for I am from him, and he hath sent me.
teachings.title: Jesus Is Sent by One Whom They Do Not Know

teachings.text: Jesus says he is with them a little while longer, then goes to him who sent him. They will seek but not find him.
teachings.quote: Yet a little while am I with you, and then I go unto him that sent me. Ye shall seek me, and shall not find me: and where I am, thither ye cannot come.
teachings.title: Jesus Goes Where They Cannot Follow

teachings.text: Jesus says he came from the Father into the world, and now leaves the world to go to the Father.
teachings.quote: I came forth from the Father, and am come into the world: again, I leave the world, and go to the Father.
teachings.title: Jesus Came from the Father and Returns to Him

subcategories.title: Predictions of His Suffering, Death, and Resurrection

teachings.text: Jesus declares that as Jonah was three days in the whale’s belly, so will the Son of Man be in the heart of the earth.
teachings.quote: For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
teachings.title: The Sign of Jonah Foretells the Resurrection

teachings.text: Jesus foretells that the Son of Man must go to Jerusalem, suffer many things from the elders and chief priests and scribes, be killed, and be raised the third day.
teachings.title: The Son of Man Must Suffer and Rise

teachings.text: Jesus rebukes Peter, saying get behind me Satan, for he is an offense and minds the things of men, not of God.
teachings.quote: Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.
teachings.title: Jesus Rebukes Peter: Get Behind Me Satan

teachings.text: Jesus charges Peter, James, and John to tell the vision to no one until the Son of Man has risen from the dead.
teachings.quote: Tell the vision to no man, until the Son of man be risen again from the dead.
teachings.title: Tell the Vision to No One Until He Rises

teachings.text: Jesus affirms that Elijah does come first and restores all things, but says Elijah has already come and they did not know him and did to him whatever they wished, and likewise the Son of Man will suffer.
teachings.quote: Elias truly shall first come, and restore all things. But I say unto you, That Elias is come already, and they knew him not, but have done unto him whatsoever they listed. Likewise shall also the Son of man suffer of them.
teachings.title: Elijah Has Come and They Did Not Know Him

teachings.text: Jesus rebukes Peter, saying get behind me Satan, for he minds the things of men, not of God.
teachings.quote: Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.
teachings.title: Peter Rebuked for Minding the Things of Men

teachings.text: Jesus says he has a baptism to be baptized with, and how distressed he is until it is accomplished.
teachings.quote: But I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straitened till it be accomplished!
teachings.title: Jesus Has a Baptism of Suffering Ahead

teachings.text: Jesus tells the twelve they go up to Jerusalem where all things written by the prophets concerning the Son of Man will be accomplished — he will be delivered to the Gentiles, mocked, scourged, and killed, and the third day rise again.
teachings.quote: Behold, we go up to Jerusalem, and all things that are written by the prophets concerning the Son of man shall be accomplished. For he shall be delivered unto the Gentiles, and shall be mocked, and spitefully entreated, and spitted on: And they shall scourge him, and put him to death: and the third day he shall rise again.
teachings.title: All Written of the Son of Man Will Be Fulfilled

teachings.text: Jesus foretells he will be delivered to the Gentiles, mocked, spat upon, scourged, and put to death, and the third day rise again.
teachings.quote: For he shall be delivered unto the Gentiles, and shall be mocked, and spitefully entreated, and spitted on: And they shall scourge him, and put him to death: and the third day he shall rise again.
teachings.title: Christ Will Be Mocked, Killed, and Raised Again

teachings.text: Jesus declares that as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the Son of Man be lifted up, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.
teachings.quote: ¶ And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
teachings.title: As Moses Lifted the Serpent, So Must the Son

teachings.text: Jesus declares that the Father loves him because he lays down his life to take it again. No one takes it from him; he lays it down of himself, with power to lay it down and to take it again, as commanded by the Father.
teachings.quote: Therefore doth my Father love me, because I lay down my life, that I might take it again. No man taketh it from me, but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This commandment have I received of my Father.
teachings.title: Christ Lays Down His Life and Takes It Again

teachings.text: Jesus defends Mary — let her alone, she has kept this for his burial; the poor are always with them, but he will not be.
teachings.quote: Let her alone: against the day of my burying hath she kept this. For the poor always ye have with you; but me ye have not always.
teachings.title: Mary Anoints Jesus for His Burial

teachings.text: Jesus announces that the hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
teachings.quote: The hour is come, that the Son of man should be glorified.
teachings.title: The Hour Has Come for the Son to Be Glorified

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples beforehand so that when it comes to pass they may believe. The prince of this world is coming and has nothing in him, but so the world may know he loves the Father, he does as the Father commanded.
teachings.quote: And now I have told you before it come to pass, that, when it is come to pass, ye might believe. Hereafter I will not talk much with you: for the prince of this world cometh, and hath nothing in me. But that the world may know that I love the Father; and as the Father gave me commandment, even so I do. Arise, let us go hence.
teachings.title: The Prince of This World Has Nothing in Christ

teachings.text: Jesus tells John to permit it for now, for so it is fitting for them to fulfill all righteousness.
teachings.quote: Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness.
teachings.title: Jesus Baptized to Fulfill All Righteousness

teachings.text: Jesus tells John’s disciples to report what they hear and see: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor receive the gospel; blessed is whoever is not offended in him.
teachings.quote: Go and shew John again those things which ye do hear and see: The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them. And blessed is he, whosoever shall not be offended in me.
teachings.title: The Works of the Messiah Confirm His Identity

teachings.text: Jesus says that if his hearers will receive it, John is the Elijah who was to come.
teachings.quote: And if ye will receive it, this is Elias, which was for to come.
teachings.title: John the Baptist Is the Elijah Who Was to Come

teachings.text: Jesus defends his disciples by recalling how David and his men ate the showbread that was not lawful, and how the priests profane the Sabbath in the temple and are blameless, declaring that one greater than the temple is here.
teachings.quote: Have ye not read what David did, when he was an hungred, and they that were with him; How he entered into the house of God, and did eat the shewbread, which was not lawful for him to eat, neither for them which were with him, but only for the priests? Or have ye not read in the law, how that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple profane the sabbath, and are blameless? But I say unto you, That in this place is one greater than the temple.
teachings.title: One Greater Than the Temple Is Here

teachings.text: Jesus declares that he is sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
teachings.quote: I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
teachings.title: Christ Sent Only to the Lost Sheep of Israel

teachings.text: Jesus asks his disciples at Caesarea Philippi who men say that he, the Son of Man, is.
teachings.quote: Whom do men say that I the Son of man am?
teachings.title: Who Do Men Say the Son of Man Is

teachings.text: Jesus presses the disciples, asking who they themselves say that he is.
teachings.quote: But whom say ye that I am?
teachings.title: Who Do You Say That I Am

teachings.text: Jesus blesses Simon Bar-Jonah, declaring that flesh and blood has not revealed it to him, but the Father in heaven.
teachings.quote: Blessed art thou, Simon Bar-jona: for flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.
teachings.title: The Father Revealed My Identity to Peter

teachings.text: Jesus reassures the disciples after the Transfiguration, telling them to arise and not be afraid.
teachings.quote: Arise, and be not afraid.
teachings.title: Rise and Do Not Be Afraid

teachings.text: Jesus teaches Peter that kings take tribute from strangers, not their own children, so the children are free; but lest they offend, he sends Peter to cast a hook and find a coin in the first fish’s mouth for the two of them.
teachings.quote: What thinkest thou, Simon? of whom do the kings of the earth take custom or tribute? of their own children, or of strangers? Then are the children free. Notwithstanding, lest we should offend them, go thou to the sea, and cast an hook, and take up the fish that first cometh up; and when thou hast opened his mouth, thou shalt find a piece of money: that take, and give unto them for me and thee.
teachings.title: The Sons Are Free from the Temple Tax

teachings.text: Jesus declares that the Son of Man has come to save that which was lost.
teachings.quote: For the Son of man is come to save that which was lost.
teachings.title: The Son of Man Came to Save the Lost

teachings.text: Jesus sends two disciples into the village to find a donkey tied with a colt, loose them and bring them, and if anyone questions them, to say the Lord has need of them and he will send them at once.
teachings.quote: Go into the village over against you, and straightway ye shall find an ass tied, and a colt with her: loose them, and bring them unto me. And if any man say ought unto you, ye shall say, The Lord hath need of them; and straightway he will send them.
teachings.title: The Lord Has Need of the Colt

teachings.text: Jesus asks the Pharisees what they think of the Christ and whose son he is, then citing David who in the Spirit calls him Lord — saying the LORD said to my Lord, sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool — he asks how, if David then calls him Lord, he is his son.
teachings.quote: What think ye of Christ? whose son is he? How then doth David in spirit call him Lord, saying, The LORD said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footstool? If David then call him Lord, how is he his son?
teachings.title: How Can David's Son Also Be David's Lord

teachings.text: Jesus affirms that Elijah comes first and restores all things, and as written, the Son of Man must suffer and be despised; but Elijah has already come and they did to him whatever they wished, as it is written of him.
teachings.quote: Elias verily cometh first, and restoreth all things; and how it is written of the Son of man, that he must suffer many things, and be set at nought. But I say unto you, That Elias is indeed come, and they have done unto him whatsoever they listed, as it is written of him.
teachings.title: Elijah Has Come and the Son of Man Must Suffer

teachings.text: Jesus reads from Isaiah in the Nazareth synagogue and declares to the hearers that today this scripture is fulfilled in their ears.
teachings.quote: This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears.
teachings.title: Today This Scripture Is Fulfilled in Your Ears

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Pharisees that if his disciples were silent, the stones would immediately cry out.
teachings.quote: I tell you that, if these should hold their peace, the stones would immediately cry out.
teachings.title: The Stones Would Cry Out If They Were Silent

teachings.text: Jesus greets Nathanael as an Israelite in whom is no deceit, and tells him he saw him under the fig tree before Philip called.
teachings.quote: Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile! Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee.
teachings.title: An Israelite in Whom There Is No Deceit

teachings.text: Jesus promises Nathanael he will see greater things — heaven open and the angels of God ascending and descending on the Son of Man.
teachings.quote: Because I said unto thee, I saw thee under the fig tree, believest thou? thou shalt see greater things than these. Verily, verily, I say unto you, Hereafter ye shall see heaven open, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of man.
teachings.title: Angels Ascending and Descending on the Son of Man

teachings.text: Jesus asks the Samaritan woman at the well to give him a drink.
teachings.quote: Give me to drink.
teachings.title: Jesus Asks a Samaritan Woman for a Drink

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Samaritan woman to call her husband, then says she has spoken well in saying she has none, for she has had five husbands and the man she now has is not her husband.
teachings.quote: Go, call thy husband, and come hither. Thou hast well said, I have no husband: For thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband: in that saidst thou truly.
teachings.title: You Have Had Five Husbands

teachings.text: Jesus declares to the Samaritan woman that he who speaks to her is the Messiah.
teachings.quote: I that speak unto thee am he.
teachings.title: I Who Speak to You Am the Messiah

teachings.text: Jesus reveals himself to the healed man, telling him that he has seen him and that the one who speaks with him is he.
teachings.quote: Thou hast both seen him, and it is he that talketh with thee.
teachings.title: You Have Seen the Son of God

teachings.text: Jesus says the works he does in his Father’s name bear witness of him; if he does not the Father’s works, do not believe, but if he does, believe the works, that they may know the Father is in him and he in the Father.
teachings.quote: I told you, and ye believed not: the works that I do in my Father’s name, they bear witness of me. If I do not the works of my Father, believe me not. But if I do, though ye believe not me, believe the works: that ye may know, and believe, that the Father is in me, and I in him.
teachings.title: The Father's Works Bear Witness of the Son

teachings.text: Jesus announces that now the Son of Man is glorified and God is glorified in him, and warns his little children that he is with them only a little while longer; where he goes they cannot come.
teachings.quote: Now is the Son of man glorified, and God is glorified in him. If God be glorified in him, God shall also glorify him in himself, and shall straightway glorify him. Little children, yet a little while I am with you. Ye shall seek me: and as I said unto the Jews, Whither I go, ye cannot come; so now I say to you.
teachings.title: The Son of Man Is Glorified — and Going Away

teachings.text: Jesus tells the kneeling leper that he is willing and commands him to be clean, then charges him to tell no one but to show himself to the priest and offer the gift Moses commanded as a testimony to them.
teachings.quote: I will; be thou clean. See thou tell no man; but go thy way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.
teachings.title: Jesus Heals the Leper and Sends Him to the Priest

teachings.text: Jesus answers the centurion's plea for his stricken servant by declaring that he will come and heal him.
teachings.quote: I will come and heal him.
teachings.title: Jesus Declares He Will Heal the Centurion's Servant

teachings.text: Jesus answers the legion of demons begging to enter the swine with a single word, and bids them go.
teachings.quote: Go.
teachings.title: Jesus Commands the Demons to Enter the Swine

teachings.text: Jesus, having opened the eyes of the two blind men, sternly charges them to see that no one knows of it.
teachings.quote: See that no man know it.
teachings.title: Two Blind Men Healed and Charged to Tell No One

teachings.text: Jesus calls the man with the withered hand to stretch it out, and it is restored whole as the other on the Sabbath.
teachings.quote: Stretch forth thine hand.
teachings.title: The Withered Hand Restored on the Sabbath

teachings.text: Jesus calls for the five loaves and two fish to be brought to him before he feeds the five thousand.
teachings.quote: Bring them hither to me.
teachings.title: Jesus Calls for the Loaves Before the Miracle

teachings.text: Jesus asks the disciples how many loaves they have before he feeds the four thousand.
teachings.quote: How many loaves have ye?
teachings.title: How Many Loaves Do You Have

teachings.text: Jesus rebukes the unclean spirit in the Capernaum synagogue, charging it to be silent and come out of the man.
teachings.quote: Hold thy peace, and come out of him.
teachings.title: Silencing the Unclean Spirit in the Synagogue

teachings.text: Jesus rebukes the wind and commands the raging sea to be at peace and be still, and there is a great calm.
teachings.quote: Peace, be still.
teachings.title: Jesus Rebukes the Wind and the Sea

teachings.text: Jesus charges the unclean spirit to come out of the Gerasene man and demands its name, which answers Legion, for they are many.
teachings.quote: Come out of the man, thou unclean spirit. What is thy name?
teachings.title: Come Out of the Man, You Unclean Spirit

teachings.text: Jesus, perceiving that power has gone out of him, turns in the press of the crowd and asks who touched his clothes.
teachings.quote: Who touched my clothes?
teachings.title: Who Touched My Clothes

teachings.text: Jesus silences the weeping mourners at Jairus's house, declaring that the girl is not dead but sleeping, then takes her by the hand and raises her with the words Talitha cumi.
teachings.quote: Why make ye this ado, and weep? the damsel is not dead, but sleepeth. ... Talitha cumi;
teachings.title: The Girl Is Not Dead but Sleeping — Talitha Cumi

teachings.text: Jesus charges the disciples to give the crowd something to eat themselves and bids them go and see how many loaves they have, before the feeding of the five thousand.
teachings.quote: Give ye them to eat. How many loaves have ye? go and see.
teachings.title: Give the Crowd Something to Eat Yourselves

teachings.text: Jesus looks up to heaven, sighs, and says Ephphatha, that is, Be opened, and the deaf man's ears and tongue are loosed.
teachings.quote: Ephphatha,
teachings.title: Ephphatha — Be Opened

teachings.text: Jesus declares his compassion on the crowd that has been with him three days with nothing to eat, and will not send them away hungry lest they faint on the way, for some have come from far.
teachings.quote: I have compassion on the multitude, because they have now been with me three days, and have nothing to eat: And if I send them away fasting to their own houses, they will faint by the way: for divers of them came from far.
teachings.title: Jesus Has Compassion on the Hungry Crowd

teachings.text: Jesus charges the mute and deaf spirit to come out of the boy and to enter him no more.
teachings.quote: Thou dumb and deaf spirit, I charge thee, come out of him, and enter no more into him.
teachings.title: Come Out of Him and Enter No More

teachings.text: Jesus asks blind Bartimaeus what he wants done for him, and at his plea to receive his sight bids him go his way, declaring that his faith has made him whole.
teachings.quote: What wilt thou that I should do unto thee? Go thy way; thy faith hath made thee whole.
teachings.title: Your Faith Has Made You Whole, Go Your Way

teachings.text: Jesus tells the weeping widow of Nain not to weep, then touches the bier and calls her dead son to arise.
teachings.quote: Weep not. Young man, I say unto thee, Arise.
teachings.title: Jesus Raises the Widow's Son at Nain

teachings.text: Jesus tells the servants at Cana to fill the jars with water and bear it to the master of the feast, turning water into wine.
teachings.quote: Fill the waterpots with water. Draw out now, and bear unto the governor of the feast.
teachings.title: Jesus Turns Water into Wine at Cana

teachings.text: Jesus sends the nobleman on his way with the word that his son lives, healing the boy at a distance.
teachings.quote: Go thy way; thy son liveth.
teachings.title: Go, Your Son Lives

teachings.text: Jesus asks the man sick thirty-eight years at Bethesda whether he wants to be made well, then commands him to rise, take up his bed, and walk.
teachings.quote: Rise, take up thy bed, and walk.
teachings.title: Rise, Take Up Your Bed, and Walk

teachings.text: Jesus asks Philip where they will buy bread so that the great crowd coming to him may eat.
teachings.quote: Whence shall we buy bread, that these may eat?
teachings.title: Where Shall We Buy Bread for This Crowd

teachings.text: Jesus instructs the disciples to make the men sit down before the feeding of the five thousand.
teachings.quote: Make the men sit down.
teachings.title: Make the People Sit Down

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples to gather up the fragments that remain so that nothing is lost.
teachings.quote: Gather up the fragments that remain, that nothing be lost.
teachings.title: Gather Up the Fragments — Let Nothing Be Lost

teachings.text: Jesus sends the man born blind to go and wash in the pool of Siloam, and the man returns seeing.
teachings.quote: Go, wash in the pool of Siloam,
teachings.title: Go Wash in the Pool of Siloam

teachings.text: At Lazarus's tomb Jesus commands the stone be taken away, reminds Martha that if she would believe she should see the glory of God, lifts his eyes to thank the Father for hearing him so that the people standing by may believe the Father has sent him, then cries with a loud voice for Lazarus to come out and bids them loose him and let him go.
teachings.quote: Take ye away the stone. Said I not unto thee, that, if thou wouldest believe, thou shouldest see the glory of God? Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me. And I knew that thou hearest me always: but because of the people which stand by I said it, that they may believe that thou hast sent me. Lazarus, come forth. Loose him, and let him go.
teachings.title: Lazarus, Come Out

subcategories.title: The Promise and Coming of the Spirit

teachings.text: Jesus cries out on the last great day of the feast that if anyone thirsts, let him come to him and drink.
teachings.quote: If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink.
teachings.title: If Anyone Thirsts, Let Him Come and Drink

teachings.text: Jesus says he will pray the Father to give another Helper, the Spirit of truth, who dwells with them and will be in them forever.
teachings.quote: And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever; Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.
teachings.title: The Father Will Send Another Helper, the Spirit

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples he will not leave them comfortless but will come to them. Because he lives, they will live also; whoever has his commandments and keeps them loves him and will be loved by his Father, to whom he will show himself.
teachings.quote: I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you. Yet a little while, and the world seeth me no more; but ye see me: because I live, ye shall live also. At that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me, and I in you. He that hath my commandments, and keepeth them, he it is that loveth me: and he that loveth me shall be loved of my Father, and I will love him, and will manifest myself to him.
teachings.title: I Will Not Leave You Comfortless

teachings.text: Jesus says the Holy Spirit whom the Father sends in his name will teach them all things and bring to remembrance all he has said.
teachings.quote: But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.
teachings.title: The Holy Spirit Will Teach You All Things

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples it is to their advantage that he go away, for if he does not depart the Helper will not come, but when the Spirit of truth comes he will guide them into all truth and glorify Jesus.
teachings.quote: Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you. Howbeit when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth: for he shall not speak of himself; but whatsoever he shall hear, that shall he speak: and he will shew you things to come. He shall glorify me: for he shall receive of mine, and shall shew it unto you.
teachings.title: The Spirit of Truth Will Guide You into All Truth

teachings.text: Jesus charges his disciples to wait for the promise of the Father, declaring that John baptized with water but they will be baptized with the Holy Spirit, and that they will receive power and be his witnesses to the ends of the earth.
teachings.quote: but wait for the promise of the Father, which, ye have heard of me. For John truly baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost not many days hence.
teachings.title: Wait for the Promise — You Will Receive Power

teachings.text: Jesus says that John indeed baptized with water but they will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.
teachings.quote: John indeed baptized with water; but ye shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost.
teachings.title: John Baptized with Water, You with the Holy Spirit

subcategories.title: The Spirit's Work in the World

teachings.text: Jesus says if evil men give good gifts to their children, the Father will much more give the Holy Spirit to those who ask.
teachings.quote: If ye then, being evil, know how to give good gifts unto your children: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Holy Spirit to them that ask him?
teachings.title: The Father Gives the Holy Spirit to Those Who Ask

teachings.text: Jesus declares that it is the Spirit that gives life and the flesh profits nothing, and that the words he speaks are spirit and are life.
teachings.quote: It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.
teachings.title: The Spirit Gives Life; the Flesh Profits Nothing

teachings.text: Jesus says that when the Helper comes he will convict the world of sin because they do not believe in him, of righteousness because he goes to the Father, and of judgment because the ruler of this world is judged.
teachings.quote: And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment: Of sin, because they believe not on me; Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more; Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged.
teachings.title: The Spirit Will Convict the World of Sin

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples he has yet many things to say to them, but they cannot bear them now.
teachings.quote: I have yet many things to say unto you, but ye cannot bear them now.
teachings.title: The Spirit Will Guide You Into All Truth

teachings.text: Jesus says all the Father has is his, so the Spirit will reveal it; soon they will not see him, then will see him again.
teachings.quote: All things that the Father hath are mine: therefore said I, that he shall take of mine, and shall shew it unto you. A little while, and ye shall not see me: and again, a little while, and ye shall see me, because I go to the Father.
teachings.title: The Spirit Will Reveal What Is the Father's

teachings.text: Jesus says all manner of sin and blasphemy will be forgiven, but blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, neither in this world nor the world to come.
teachings.quote: ¶ Wherefore I say unto you, All manner of sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men: but the blasphemy against the Holy Ghost shall not be forgiven unto men. And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Holy Ghost, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.
teachings.title: Blasphemy Against the Holy Spirit Will Not Be Forgiven

categories.title: The Kingdom of God
categories.description: The Kingdom of God (or Kingdom of Heaven) is the organizing center of Jesus’s teaching. He describes its nature, how one enters it, its ethics, and its ultimate completion.

subcategories.title: Nature and Character of the Kingdom

teachings.text: Jesus declares that many will come from east and west to sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven, while the children of the kingdom will be cast into outer darkness.
teachings.quote: And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.title: Many Will Come from Afar to the Kingdom's Feast

teachings.text: Jesus says that since the days of John the Baptist the kingdom of heaven suffers violence and the violent take it by force. He warns it will be taken from those who do not bear its fruit and given to a nation that will.
teachings.quote: And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent take it by force.
teachings.title: The Kingdom Suffers Violence and Demands Fruitfulness

teachings.text: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to a mustard seed which, though least of all seeds, grows into a tree where the birds of the air come and lodge in its branches.
teachings.quote: The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof.
teachings.title: The Mustard Seed

teachings.text: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to leaven which a woman hides in three measures of meal until the whole is leavened.
teachings.quote: The kingdom of heaven is like unto leaven, which a woman took, and hid in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.
teachings.title: The Leaven

teachings.text: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to treasure hidden in a field which a man finds and for joy sells all to buy that field, and to a merchant who finds one pearl of great price and sells all to buy it.
teachings.quote: ¶ Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man hath found, he hideth, and for joy thereof goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field. ¶ Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls: Who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.
teachings.title: The Hidden Treasure

teachings.text: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to a net cast into the sea that gathers every kind; the good are kept and the bad cast away. At the end of the age angels will sever the wicked from the just.
teachings.quote: ¶ Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a net, that was cast into the sea, and gathered of every kind: Which, when it was full, they drew to shore, and sat down, and gathered the good into vessels, but cast the bad away. So shall it be at the end of the world: the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just, And shall cast them into the furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.
teachings.title: The Net

teachings.text: Jesus likens every scribe instructed for the kingdom of heaven to a householder who brings out of his treasure things new and old.
teachings.quote: Have ye understood all these things? Therefore every scribe which is instructed unto the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which bringeth forth out of his treasure things new and old.
teachings.title: The Trained Scribe

teachings.text: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to a king who makes a wedding for his son and sends servants to call the invited, but they refuse and kill the servants. The king destroys them, burns their city, and sends servants into the highways to gather all they find. One found without a wedding garment is cast into outer darkness, for many are called but few chosen.
teachings.quote: The kingdom of heaven is like unto a certain king, which made a marriage for his son, And sent forth his servants to call them that were bidden to the wedding: and they would not come. Again, he sent forth other servants, saying, Tell them which are bidden, Behold, I have prepared my dinner: my oxen and my fatlings are killed, and all things are ready: come unto the marriage. But they made light of it, and went their ways, one to his farm, another to his merchandise: And the remnant took his servants, and entreated them spitefully, and slew them. But when the king heard thereof, he was wroth: and he sent forth his armies, and destroyed those murderers, and burned up their city. Then saith he to his servants, The wedding is ready, but they which were bidden were not worthy. Go ye therefore into the highways, and as many as ye shall find, bid to the marriage. So those servants went out into the highways, and gathered together all as many as they found, both bad and good: and the wedding was furnished with guests. ¶ And when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man which had not on a wedding garment: And he saith unto him, Friend, how camest thou in hither not having a wedding garment? And he was speechless. Then said the king to the servants, Bind him hand and foot, and take him away, and cast him into outer darkness; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth. For many are called, but few are chosen.
teachings.title: The Wedding Banquet

teachings.text: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to ten virgins going to meet the bridegroom — five wise with oil and five foolish without. While he tarries all sleep; at midnight a cry sounds, the wise enter the marriage while the foolish find a shut door and hear, I do not know you. He charges them to watch, for they know neither the day nor the hour.
teachings.quote: Then shall the kingdom of heaven be likened unto ten virgins, which took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom. And five of them were wise, and five were foolish. They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them: But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps. While the bridegroom tarried, they all slumbered and slept. And at midnight there was a cry made, Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him. Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps. And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out. But the wise answered, saying, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves. And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut. Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us. But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not. Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh.
teachings.title: The Ten Virgins

teachings.text: Jesus proclaims that the time is fulfilled and the kingdom of God is at hand, and calls his hearers to repent and believe the gospel.
teachings.quote: The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.
teachings.title: The Kingdom Is at Hand — Repent and Believe

teachings.text: Jesus says the kingdom of God does not come with observation, nor will they say, Look here or there, for it is within you.
teachings.quote: The kingdom of God cometh not with observation: Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, the kingdom of God is within you.
teachings.title: The Kingdom of God Is Within You

subcategories.title: Growth and Presence of the Kingdom

teachings.text: Jesus tells of a sower whose seed falls by the wayside and is devoured, on stony ground where it withers, among thorns that choke it, and on good ground where it bears a hundredfold. He explains the seed as the word of the kingdom and the soils as hearers — wayside, stony, thorny, and good who hear and bear fruit.
teachings.quote: Behold, a sower went forth to sow; And when he sowed, some seeds fell by the way side, and the fowls came and devoured them up: Some fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth: and forthwith they sprung up, because they had no deepness of earth: And when the sun was up, they were scorched; and because they had no root, they withered away. And some fell among thorns; and the thorns sprung up, and choked them: But other fell into good ground, and brought forth fruit, some an hundredfold, some sixtyfold, some thirtyfold. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear. ¶ Hear ye therefore the parable of the sower. When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, then cometh the wicked one, and catcheth away that which was sown in his heart. This is he which received seed by the way side. But he that received the seed into stony places, the same is he that heareth the word, and anon with joy receiveth it; Yet hath he not root in himself, but dureth for a while: for when tribulation or persecution ariseth because of the word, by and by he is offended. He also that received seed among the thorns is he that heareth the word; and the care of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, choke the word, and he becometh unfruitful. But he that received seed into the good ground is he that heareth the word, and understandeth it; which also beareth fruit, and bringeth forth, some an hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.
teachings.title: The Sower

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples it is given to them to know the mysteries of the kingdom, but not to others, and that he speaks to the multitude in parables because seeing they do not see and hearing they do not understand.
teachings.quote: Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given. For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath. Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.
teachings.title: The Mysteries of the Kingdom Are Given to You

teachings.text: Jesus likens the kingdom to a man who sows good seed while his enemy sows tares among the wheat. He tells the servants to let both grow until the harvest, when reapers will burn the tares and gather the wheat. He explains the harvest as the end of the age, when angels gather out all that offends and the righteous shine as the sun.
teachings.quote: The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field: But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way. But when the blade was sprung up, and brought forth fruit, then appeared the tares also. So the servants of the householder came and said unto him, Sir, didst not thou sow good seed in thy field? from whence then hath it tares? He said unto them, An enemy hath done this. The servants said unto him, Wilt thou then that we go and gather them up? But he said, Nay; lest while ye gather up the tares, ye root up also the wheat with them. Let both grow together until the harvest: and in the time of harvest I will say to the reapers, Gather ye together first the tares, and bind them in bundles to burn them: but gather the wheat into my barn. He that soweth the good seed is the Son of man; The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one; The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels. As therefore the tares are gathered and burned in the fire; so shall it be in the end of this world. The Son of man shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend, and them which do iniquity; And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth. Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.
teachings.title: The Wheat and Tares

teachings.text: Jesus asks the disciples whether they understand this parable, saying that if not, how then will they know all parables.
teachings.quote: Know ye not this parable? and how then will ye know all parables?
teachings.title: The Meaning of the Sower

teachings.text: Jesus likens the kingdom of God to a man who scatters seed and sleeps while it springs up he knows not how. The earth bears fruit of itself — first blade, then ear, then full grain. When it is ripe he puts in the sickle.
teachings.quote: So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the ground; And should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knoweth not how. For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear. But when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come.
teachings.title: The Seed Growing Secretly

teachings.text: Jesus says that unless his hearers' righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, they will by no means enter the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.quote: For I say unto you, That except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.title: Your Righteousness Must Exceed the Pharisees'

teachings.text: Jesus charges his hearers to seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, with the promise that all these things will be added to them.
teachings.quote: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
teachings.title: Seek First the Kingdom and All Shall Be Added

teachings.text: Jesus charges his hearers to enter by the narrow gate, for wide is the gate and broad the way leading to destruction and many go in there, but narrow is the gate and the way that leads to life, and few find it.
teachings.quote: ¶ Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.
teachings.title: Enter Through the Narrow Gate

teachings.text: Jesus declares that not everyone who says, Lord, Lord, will enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of his Father, and to many who plead their works in his name he will say, I never knew you.
teachings.quote: ¶ Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven. Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works? And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.
teachings.title: Not Everyone Who Says Lord, Lord Enters the Kingdom

teachings.text: Jesus says Isaiah's prophecy is fulfilled in them: hearing they understand not and seeing they perceive not, for their heart has grown dull.
teachings.quote: And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Esaias, which saith, By hearing ye shall hear, and shall not understand; and seeing ye shall see, and shall not perceive: For this people’s heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed; lest at any time they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and should understand with their heart, and should be converted, and I should heal them.
teachings.title: Isaiah's Prophecy Fulfilled in Hard Hearts

teachings.text: Jesus declares that unless his hearers are converted and become as little children, they will not enter the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.quote: Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.title: Unless You Become as a Little Child

teachings.text: Jesus says a rich man will hardly enter the kingdom of heaven, and that it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.
teachings.quote: Verily I say unto you, That a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven. And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God.
teachings.title: A Rich Man Hardly Enters the Kingdom of God

teachings.text: Jesus declares to the chief priests that tax collectors and harlots enter the kingdom of God before them, for they did not believe John.
teachings.quote: Whether of them twain did the will of his father? Verily I say unto you, That the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you. For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye had seen it, repented not afterward, that ye might believe him.
teachings.title: Sinners Enter the Kingdom Before the Self-Righteous

teachings.text: Jesus tells Nicodemus that unless one is born again he cannot see the kingdom of God, and unless born of water and Spirit he cannot enter it. The Spirit is like the wind, blowing where it wishes.
teachings.quote: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God. Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit. Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again. The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.
teachings.title: You Must Be Born of Water and Spirit

subcategories.title: Citizens of the Kingdom — The Beatitudes

teachings.text: Jesus blesses the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.quote: Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.title: Blessed Are the Poor in Spirit

teachings.text: Jesus blesses those who mourn, for they will be comforted.
teachings.quote: Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.
teachings.title: Blessed Are Those Who Mourn

teachings.text: Jesus blesses the meek, for they will inherit the earth.
teachings.quote: Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth.
teachings.title: Blessed Are the Meek

teachings.text: Jesus blesses those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they will be filled.
teachings.quote: Blessed are they which do hunger and thirst after righteousness: for they shall be filled.
teachings.title: Blessed Are Those Who Hunger for Righteousness

teachings.text: Jesus blesses the merciful, for they will obtain mercy.
teachings.quote: Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.
teachings.title: Blessed Are the Merciful

teachings.text: Jesus blesses the pure in heart, for they will see God.
teachings.quote: Blessed are the pure in heart: for they shall see God.
teachings.title: Blessed Are the Pure in Heart

teachings.text: Jesus blesses the peacemakers, for they will be called the children of God.
teachings.quote: Blessed are the peacemakers: for they shall be called the children of God.
teachings.title: Blessed Are the Peacemakers

teachings.text: Jesus blesses those persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven, and tells his hearers to rejoice and be exceedingly glad when they are reviled and falsely accused for his sake, for great is their reward in heaven.
teachings.quote: Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake. Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.
teachings.title: Blessed Are the Persecuted — Great Is Your Reward

teachings.text: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to a householder who hires laborers throughout the day for a denarius. At evening he pays each one a denarius beginning with the last; when those hired first murmur, he answers that he does no wrong. He declares that the last will be first and the first last, for many are called but few chosen.
teachings.quote: For the kingdom of heaven is like unto a man that is an householder, which went out early in the morning to hire labourers into his vineyard. And when he had agreed with the labourers for a penny a day, he sent them into his vineyard. And he went out about the third hour, and saw others standing idle in the marketplace, And said unto them; Go ye also into the vineyard, and whatsoever is right I will give you. And they went their way. Again he went out about the sixth and ninth hour, and did likewise. And about the eleventh hour he went out, and found others standing idle, and saith unto them, Why stand ye here all the day idle? They say unto him, Because no man hath hired us. He saith unto them, Go ye also into the vineyard; and whatsoever is right, that shall ye receive. So when even was come, the lord of the vineyard saith unto his steward, Call the labourers, and give them their hire, beginning from the last unto the first. And when they came that were hired about the eleventh hour, they received every man a penny. But when the first came, they supposed that they should have received more; and they likewise received every man a penny. And when they had received it, they murmured against the goodman of the house, Saying, These last have wrought but one hour, and thou hast made them equal unto us, which have borne the burden and heat of the day. But he answered one of them, and said, Friend, I do thee no wrong: didst not thou agree with me for a penny? Take that thine is, and go thy way: I will give unto this last, even as unto thee. Is it not lawful for me to do what I will with mine own? Is thine eye evil, because I am good? So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.
teachings.title: The Workers in the Vineyard

teachings.text: Jesus tells of a man with two sons: the first refuses to work in the vineyard but later repents and goes, while the second agrees but does not go. Tax collectors and harlots enter the kingdom of God before those who only profess obedience.
teachings.quote: ¶ But what think ye? A certain man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said, Son, go work to day in my vineyard. He answered and said, I will not: but afterward he repented, and went. And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I go, sir: and went not. Whether of them twain did the will of his father? Verily I say unto you, That the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you.
teachings.title: The Two Sons

teachings.text: Jesus tells of a householder who plants a vineyard, leases it to tenants, and goes away. The tenants beat and kill the servants he sends, and finally kill his son to seize the inheritance — so the lord will destroy them and give the vineyard to others. He declares that the kingdom of God will be taken from them and given to a nation bearing its fruits.
teachings.quote: ¶ Hear another parable: There was a certain householder, which planted a vineyard, and hedged it round about, and digged a winepress in it, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into a far country: And when the time of the fruit drew near, he sent his servants to the husbandmen, that they might receive the fruits of it. And the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another. Again, he sent other servants more than the first: and they did unto them likewise. But last of all he sent unto them his son, saying, They will reverence my son. But when the husbandmen saw the son, they said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and let us seize on his inheritance. And they caught him, and cast him out of the vineyard, and slew him. When the lord therefore of the vineyard cometh, what will he do unto those husbandmen?
