Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, the same is become the head of the corner: this is the Lord’s doing, and it is marvellous in our eyes? Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of God shall be taken from you, and given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof. And whosoever shall fall on this stone shall be broken: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.
teachings.title: The Wicked Tenants

teachings.text: Jesus proclaims that the time is fulfilled and the kingdom of heaven is at hand, calling his hearers to repent and believe the gospel.
teachings.quote: Repent: for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.
teachings.title: The Kingdom Is at Hand — Repent and Believe

teachings.text: Jesus says the healthy need no physician but the sick, and he has come to call sinners to repentance, not the righteous.
teachings.quote: They that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick. But go ye and learn what that meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice: for I am not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.
teachings.title: Christ Came to Call Sinners, Not the Righteous

teachings.text: Jesus pronounces woe on Chorazin and Bethsaida, saying Tyre and Sidon would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
teachings.quote: Woe unto thee, Chorazin! woe unto thee, Bethsaida! for if the mighty works, which were done in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
teachings.title: Woe to Chorazin — Tyre Would Have Repented

teachings.text: Jesus warns that an unclean spirit returns with seven worse spirits to the swept and empty house, so the last state of that person is worse than the first.
teachings.quote: When the unclean spirit is gone out of a man, he walketh through dry places, seeking rest, and findeth none. Then he saith, I will return into my house from whence I came out; and when he is come, he findeth it empty, swept, and garnished. Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this wicked generation.
teachings.title: The Unclean Spirit Returns Sevenfold

teachings.text: Jesus asks whether the Galileans whose blood Pilate mingled with their sacrifices were greater sinners than other Galileans.
teachings.quote: Suppose ye that these Galilæans were sinners above all the Galilæans, because they suffered such things?
teachings.title: Were the Galileans Greater Sinners Than Others

teachings.text: Jesus asks whether the eighteen on whom the tower in Siloam fell were greater sinners than all who lived in Jerusalem.
teachings.quote: Or those eighteen, upon whom the tower in Siloam fell, and slew them, think ye that they were sinners above all men that dwelt in Jerusalem?
teachings.title: Were Those Killed at Siloam Greater Sinners

teachings.text: Jesus tells of a man whose fig tree bore no fruit for three years and is to be cut down, but the vinedresser asks one more year to dig and fertilize it before judgment.
teachings.quote: A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard; and he came and sought fruit thereon, and found none. Then said he unto the dresser of his vineyard, Behold, these three years I come seeking fruit on this fig tree, and find none: cut it down; why cumbereth it the ground? And he answering said unto him, Lord, let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it: And if it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.
teachings.title: The Barren Fig Tree

teachings.text: Jesus says there will be joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, more than over ninety-nine just persons who need no repentance.
teachings.quote: I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance. Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.
teachings.title: More Joy in Heaven over One Repentant Sinner

teachings.text: Jesus calls Zacchaeus to hurry and come down from the sycamore tree, for he must stay at his house today.
teachings.quote: Zacchæus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.
teachings.title: Jesus Calls Zacchaeus Down from the Tree

teachings.text: Jesus declares that salvation has come this day to the house of Zacchaeus, since he too is a son of Abraham.
teachings.quote: This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham.
teachings.title: Salvation Has Come to Zacchaeus Today

teachings.text: Jesus finds the healed man in the temple and tells him, you are made well; sin no more, lest a worse thing come upon you.
teachings.quote: Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.
teachings.title: You Are Well — Sin No More

teachings.text: Jesus asks the woman where her accusers are, then tells her neither does he condemn her; go and sin no more.
teachings.quote: Woman, where are those thine accusers? hath no man condemned thee? Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more.
teachings.title: Go and Sin No More

teachings.text: Jesus tells of a shepherd with a hundred sheep who leaves the ninety-nine to seek the one that is lost, then lays it on his shoulders rejoicing and calls his friends to celebrate, for there is more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents.
teachings.quote: What man of you, having an hundred sheep, if he lose one of them, doth not leave the ninety and nine in the wilderness, and go after that which is lost, until he find it? And when he hath found it, he layeth it on his shoulders, rejoicing. And when he cometh home, he calleth together his friends and neighbours, saying unto them, Rejoice with me; for I have found my sheep which was lost. I say unto you, that likewise joy shall be in heaven over one sinner that repenteth, more than over ninety and nine just persons, which need no repentance.
teachings.title: The Lost Sheep

teachings.text: Jesus tells of a woman with ten silver coins who, losing one, lights a lamp and sweeps the house until she finds it, then calls her neighbors to rejoice with her, saying there is joy among the angels over one sinner who repents.
teachings.quote: ¶ Either what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it? And when she hath found it, she calleth her friends and her neighbours together, saying, Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost. Likewise, I say unto you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.
teachings.title: The Lost Coin

teachings.text: Jesus tells of a younger son who takes his inheritance to a far country, squanders it in reckless living, and in famine resolves to return confessing he has sinned. His father runs to meet him with compassion and restores him with the best robe and the fatted calf, rebuking the older son's anger and declaring this son was dead and is alive again, was lost and is found.
teachings.quote: A certain man had two sons: And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living. And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living. And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want. And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine. And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him. And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger! I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee, And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants. And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him. And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son. But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry. Now his elder son was in the field: and as he came and drew nigh to the house, he heard musick and dancing. And he called one of the servants, and asked what these things meant. And he said unto him, Thy brother is come; and thy father hath killed the fatted calf, because he hath received him safe and sound. And he was angry, and would not go in: therefore came his father out, and intreated him. And he answering said to his father, Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends: But as soon as this thy son was come, which hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf. And he said unto him, Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine. It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.
teachings.title: The Prodigal Son

teachings.text: Jesus calls all who labor and are heavy laden to come to him for rest, bidding them take his yoke and learn from him, for he is gentle and lowly, and his yoke is easy and his burden light.
teachings.quote: ¶ Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.
teachings.title: Come to Me, All Who Labor and Are Heavy Laden

teachings.text: Jesus promises that all the Father gives him will come to him, and the one who comes to him he will never cast out.
teachings.quote: All that the Father giveth me shall come to me; and him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out.
teachings.title: All Who Come to Christ He Will Never Cast Out

teachings.text: Jesus tells Nicodemus that unless one is born again he cannot see the kingdom of God, and unless he is born of water and the Spirit he cannot enter it, for flesh births flesh and Spirit births spirit.
teachings.quote: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God. Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. That which is born of the flesh is flesh; and that which is born of the Spirit is spirit.
teachings.title: You Must Be Born of Water and the Spirit

teachings.text: Jesus tells Nicodemus not to marvel that he must be born again, for the wind blows where it wills—so is everyone born of the Spirit.
teachings.quote: Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again. The wind bloweth where it listeth, and thou hearest the sound thereof, but canst not tell whence it cometh, and whither it goeth: so is every one that is born of the Spirit.
teachings.title: Do Not Marvel — You Must Be Born Again

teachings.text: Jesus rebukes Nicodemus as a teacher of Israel who does not know these things, and asks how they will believe heavenly things if they do not believe the earthly things he tells them.
teachings.quote: Art thou a master of Israel, and knowest not these things? Verily, verily, I say unto thee, We speak that we do know, and testify that we have seen; and ye receive not our witness. If I have told you earthly things, and ye believe not, how shall ye believe, if I tell you of heavenly things?
teachings.title: If You Disbelieve Earthly Things, What of Heavenly

teachings.text: Jesus says some among his hearers do not believe, and that no one can come to him unless it is given by the Father.
teachings.quote: But there are some of you that believe not. Therefore said I unto you, that no man can come unto me, except it were given unto him of my Father.
teachings.title: None Can Come Unless the Father Grants It

subcategories.title: Faith as the Condition of Salvation

teachings.text: Jesus declares that God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten Son, that whoever believes in him will not perish but have everlasting life, and that whoever does not believe is condemned already.
teachings.quote: ¶ For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life. For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved. ¶ He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.
teachings.title: Whoever Believes in the Son Has Eternal Life

teachings.text: Jesus tells Martha he is the resurrection and the life: whoever believes in him will live though he die, and whoever believes will never die.
teachings.quote: I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this?
teachings.title: I Am the Resurrection and the Life

teachings.text: Jesus urges his hearers to walk while they have the light and to believe in it, that they may become children of light.
teachings.quote: Yet a little while is the light with you. Walk while ye have the light, lest darkness come upon you: for he that walketh in darkness knoweth not whither he goeth. While ye have light, believe in the light, that ye may be the children of light.
teachings.title: Believe in the Light and Become Children of Light

subcategories.title: Eternal Life — Its Nature and Assurance

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Samaritan woman that whoever drinks the water he gives will never thirst—it becomes a well springing up to everlasting life.
teachings.quote: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.
teachings.title: Living Water Springs Up to Everlasting Life

teachings.text: Jesus rebukes the crowd for seeking him over the loaves, charging them to labor not for perishable food but for food enduring to everlasting life.
teachings.quote: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Ye seek me, not because ye saw the miracles, but because ye did eat of the loaves, and were filled. Labour not for the meat which perisheth, but for that meat which endureth unto everlasting life, which the Son of man shall give unto you: for him hath God the Father sealed.
teachings.title: Labor for Food That Endures to Eternal Life

teachings.text: Jesus says it is written that they will all be taught of God, that everyone who hears and learns from the Father comes to him, and that whoever believes has everlasting life.
teachings.quote: It is written in the prophets, And they shall be all taught of God. Every man therefore that hath heard, and hath learned of the Father, cometh unto me. Not that any man hath seen the Father, save he which is of God, he hath seen the Father. Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me hath everlasting life.
teachings.title: Everyone Taught of God Comes to the Son

teachings.text: Jesus declares that whoever commits sin is a servant of sin; the servant does not abide in the house forever, but the Son abides forever.
teachings.quote: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin. And the servant abideth not in the house for ever: but the Son abideth ever.
teachings.title: The Servant of Sin Does Not Abide Forever

teachings.text: Jesus says he has no devil but honors his Father while they dishonor him, that he does not seek his own glory but One does, and that whoever keeps his word will never see death.
teachings.quote: I have not a devil; but I honour my Father, and ye do dishonour me. And I seek not mine own glory: there is one that seeketh and judgeth. Verily, verily, I say unto you, If a man keep my saying, he shall never see death.
teachings.title: Whoever Keeps Christ's Word Will Never See Death

teachings.text: Jesus says the thief comes only to steal, kill, and destroy, but he came that they may have life and have it abundantly.
teachings.quote: The thief cometh not, but for to steal, and to kill, and to destroy: I am come that they might have life, and that they might have it more abundantly.
teachings.title: Christ Came to Give Life, and Life Abundantly

teachings.text: Jesus declares that his sheep hear his voice and follow him; he gives them eternal life, and none can pluck them from his hand.
teachings.quote: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.
teachings.title: His Sheep Hear His Voice and He Gives Eternal Life

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples that in his Father's house are many mansions, and he goes to prepare a place and will return for them.
teachings.quote: In my Father’s house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you. And if I go and prepare a place for you, I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.
teachings.title: In the Father's House Are Many Dwelling Places

teachings.text: Jesus charges his hearers to enter through the narrow gate, for wide is the gate and broad the way to destruction, but narrow is the gate and the way that leads to life, and few find it.
teachings.quote: ¶ Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat: Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.
teachings.title: The Narrow Way That Leads to Life

teachings.text: Jesus declares that not everyone who says Lord, Lord will enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the Father's will. Many will claim mighty works in his name, and he will profess: I never knew you, depart from me.
teachings.quote: ¶ Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven. Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name? and in thy name have cast out devils? and in thy name done many wonderful works? And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.
teachings.title: Obedience Enters the Kingdom, Not Words Alone

teachings.text: Jesus warns that once the master shuts the door, those who knock saying Lord, Lord will hear him answer that he does not know them; though they protest they ate with him and he taught in their streets, he will tell them to depart.
teachings.quote: When once the master of the house is risen up, and hath shut to the door, and ye begin to stand without, and to knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open unto us; and he shall answer and say unto you, I know you not whence ye are: Then shall ye begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets. But he shall say, I tell you, I know you not whence ye are; depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.
teachings.title: The Door Shut to Those He Does Not Know

teachings.text: Jesus calls Herod that fox and says he will continue his work until perfected on the third day. He laments over Jerusalem that kills its prophets, saying how often he longed to gather her children as a hen gathers her brood, but they refused.
teachings.quote: Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils, and I do cures to day and to morrow, and the third day I shall be perfected. Nevertheless I must walk to day, and to morrow, and the day following: for it cannot be that a prophet perish out of Jerusalem. O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, which killest the prophets, and stonest them that are sent unto thee; how often would I have gathered thy children together, as a hen doth gather her brood under her wings, and ye would not! Behold, your house is left unto you desolate: and verily I say unto you, Ye shall not see me, until the time come when ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
teachings.title: Jesus Laments over Jerusalem's Refusal

subcategories.title: The Nature and Power of Faith

teachings.text: Jesus marvels at the Roman centurion, saying he has not found so great a faith, not even in Israel.
teachings.quote: Verily I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
teachings.title: Great Faith Not Found Even in Israel

teachings.text: Jesus tells the centurion to go his way, and as he has believed, so be it done to him.
teachings.quote: Go thy way; and as thou hast believed, so be it done unto thee.
teachings.title: As You Have Believed, So Be It Done to You

teachings.text: Jesus asks the two blind men whether they believe he is able to do this.
teachings.quote: Believe ye that I am able to do this?
teachings.title: Do You Believe I Am Able to Do This

teachings.text: Jesus declares that according to their faith it will be done, telling the bleeding woman and others their faith has made them whole and to go in peace.
teachings.quote: According to your faith be it unto you.
teachings.title: Your Faith Has Made You Whole

teachings.text: Jesus calls Peter out of the boat onto the water with a single word: come.
teachings.quote: Come.
teachings.title: Peter Called to Walk on Water — Come

teachings.text: Jesus says to the Canaanite woman that it is not right to take the children's bread and toss it to dogs.
teachings.quote: It is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it to dogs.
teachings.title: The Children's Bread Must Not Go to Dogs

teachings.text: Jesus praises the Canaanite woman, declaring great is her faith and that it will be done for her as she wishes.
teachings.quote: O woman, great is thy faith: be it unto thee even as thou wilt.
teachings.title: Great Is Your Faith — Your Wish Is Granted

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples that with faith like a mustard seed they will move mountains and nothing will be impossible to them, and whatever they ask in prayer believing they will receive.
teachings.quote: Because of your unbelief: for verily I say unto you, If ye have faith as a grain of mustard seed, ye shall say unto this mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it shall remove; and nothing shall be impossible unto you. Howbeit this kind goeth not out but by prayer and fasting.
teachings.title: Faith Like a Mustard Seed Moves Mountains

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Syrophoenician woman that for her saying she may go her way, for the demon has gone out of her daughter.
teachings.quote: For this saying go thy way; the devil is gone out of thy daughter.
teachings.title: For Your Saying the Demon Has Gone Out

teachings.text: Jesus laments a faithless generation and asks how long he will bear with them, calls the boy to him, and declares that all things are possible to one who believes.
teachings.quote: O faithless generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you? bring him unto me. \u2026 If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth.
teachings.title: All Things Are Possible to One Who Believes

teachings.text: Jesus marvels at the centurion and declares he has not found so great a faith, not even in Israel.
teachings.quote: I say unto you, I have not found so great faith, no, not in Israel.
teachings.title: The Centurion's Faith Surpasses All in Israel

teachings.text: Jesus tells the woman to take comfort, that her faith has made her whole, and bids her go in peace.
teachings.quote: Daughter, be of good comfort: thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace.
teachings.title: Your Faith Has Made You Whole — Go in Peace

teachings.text: Jesus cries out against a faithless and perverse generation, asking how long he will bear with them, and bids the father bring his son.
teachings.quote: O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you, and suffer you? Bring thy son hither.
teachings.title: A Faithless Generation — Bring the Boy to Me

teachings.text: Jesus asks whether, when the Son of Man comes, he will find faith on earth, and blesses those who have not seen and yet believed.
teachings.quote: I tell you that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?
teachings.title: Will the Son of Man Find Faith on Earth

teachings.text: Jesus declares that the work of God is to believe in the one whom he has sent.
teachings.quote: This is the work of God, that ye believe on him whom he hath sent.
teachings.title: Believe in the One God Has Sent

teachings.text: Jesus tells the crowd that they have seen him and yet do not believe.
teachings.quote: But I said unto you, That ye also have seen me, and believe not.
teachings.title: You Have Seen Me and Still Do Not Believe

teachings.text: Jesus seeks out the man cast out by the Pharisees and asks whether he believes in the Son of God.
teachings.quote: Dost thou believe on the Son of God?
teachings.title: Do You Believe in the Son of God

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Jews that they do not believe because they are not of his sheep.
teachings.quote: But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep, as I said unto you.
teachings.title: You Do Not Believe Because You Are Not My Sheep

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples plainly that Lazarus is dead, and is glad for their sakes that they may believe, then bids them go to him.
teachings.quote: Lazarus is dead. And I am glad for your sakes that I was not there, to the intent ye may believe; nevertheless let us go unto him.
teachings.title: Lazarus Is Dead; Come That You May Believe

teachings.text: Jesus declares that whoever believes in him will do the works he does, and greater works, because he goes to the Father.
teachings.quote: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do; because I go unto my Father.
teachings.title: Believers Will Do Greater Works Through Christ

teachings.text: Jesus calls out to the disciples on the storm-tossed sea, telling them to take heart, that it is he, and not to be afraid.
teachings.quote: Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.
teachings.title: Take Heart — It Is I, Do Not Be Afraid

teachings.text: Jesus rebukes the disciples as of little faith for worrying they have no bread, asking whether they remember the loaves of the five thousand and the four thousand and the baskets they took up.
teachings.quote: O ye of little faith, why reason ye among yourselves, because ye have brought no bread? Do ye not yet understand, neither remember the five loaves of the five thousand, and how many baskets ye took up? Neither the seven loaves of the four thousand, and how many baskets ye took up?
teachings.title: Why Do You Doubt — Remember the Loaves

teachings.text: Jesus cries out against a faithless and perverse generation, asking how long he will bear with them, and bids the boy be brought to him.
teachings.quote: O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? how long shall I suffer you? bring him hither to me.
teachings.title: A Faithless Generation — Bring Him to Me

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples, let us cross over to the other side of the sea.
teachings.quote: Let us pass over unto the other side.
teachings.title: Let Us Cross to the Other Side

teachings.text: Jesus asks his disciples why they are so fearful and have no faith, calls Peter of little faith asking why he doubted, and tells the synagogue ruler not to be afraid but only believe.
teachings.quote: Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?
teachings.title: Why Are You Fearful — Have You No Faith

teachings.text: Jesus calls out as he walks on the sea, telling the disciples to take heart, it is he, do not be afraid.
teachings.quote: Be of good cheer: it is I; be not afraid.
teachings.title: It Is I on the Water — Do Not Fear

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples, fear not, little flock — it is the Father's good pleasure to give them the kingdom, and charges Thomas to believe.
teachings.quote: Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.
teachings.title: Fear Not, Little Flock — Believe, Do Not Doubt

teachings.text: Jesus says to the nobleman that unless they see signs and wonders, they will not believe.
teachings.quote: Except ye see signs and wonders, ye will not believe.
teachings.title: Unless You See Signs You Will Not Believe

teachings.text: Jesus calls out to the terrified disciples on the sea, telling them it is he and not to be afraid.
teachings.quote: It is I; be not afraid.
teachings.title: Do Not Be Afraid — It Is I

teachings.text: Jesus charges his hearers to take no thought for life, food, drink, or clothing, declaring that life is more than food and the body more than clothing, and that the heavenly Father knows they need all these things.
teachings.quote: Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than meat, and the body than raiment? Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they? Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature? And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin: And yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. Wherefore, if God so clothe the grass of the field, which to day is, and to morrow is cast into the oven, shall he not much more clothe you, O ye of little faith? Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed? (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.
teachings.title: Take No Thought for Life — Your Father Knows

teachings.text: Jesus bids his hearers consider the birds the Father feeds though they neither sow nor reap, and the lilies arrayed beyond Solomon. If God so clothes the grass, he asks, will he not much more clothe you of little faith.
teachings.quote: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they? Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature? And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin: And yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these. Wherefore, if God so clothe the grass of the field, which to day is, and to morrow is cast into the oven, shall he not much more clothe you, O ye of little faith?
teachings.title: Consider the Birds and Lilies — God Clothes You

teachings.text: Jesus charges his hearers to seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to them, taking no thought for tomorrow, for sufficient to the day is its own trouble.
teachings.quote: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.
teachings.title: Seek First the Kingdom and Trust for Tomorrow

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples that when they are handed over they should take no thought how or what to speak, for it will be given them in that hour, since it is not they who speak but the Spirit of their Father.
teachings.quote: But when they deliver you up, take no thought how or what ye shall speak: for it shall be given you in that same hour what ye shall speak. For it is not ye that speak, but the Spirit of your Father which speaketh in you.
teachings.title: The Spirit Will Speak When You Are Handed Over

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples not to let their hearts be troubled, leaves his peace not as the world gives, and declares that in the world they will have tribulation but take heart, for he has overcome the world.
teachings.quote: Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me. Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
teachings.title: Peace I Leave You — I Have Overcome the World

teachings.text: Jesus declares he has not come to destroy the law or the prophets but to fulfill them. Not one jot or tittle will pass till all is fulfilled, and whoever breaks the least commandment will be called least in the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.quote: ¶ Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil. For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled. Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.title: Christ Came to Fulfill, Not Abolish, the Law

teachings.text: Jesus answers the lawyer's question with a question, asking what is written in the law and how he reads it.
teachings.quote: What is written in the law? how readest thou?
teachings.title: What Does the Law Say — How Do You Read?

teachings.text: Jesus declares that the law and the prophets were until John, and that since then the kingdom of God is preached and every man presses into it.
teachings.quote: The law and the prophets were until John: since that time the kingdom of God is preached, and every man presseth into it.
teachings.title: The Law Stood Until John — Now the Kingdom Comes

teachings.text: Jesus declares that it is easier for heaven and earth to pass than for one tittle of the law to fail.
teachings.quote: And it is easier for heaven and earth to pass, than one tittle of the law to fail.
teachings.title: Not One Tittle of the Law Shall Fail

subcategories.title: Moses and the Scriptures Pointing to Jesus

teachings.text: Jesus says that if his hearers had believed Moses they would have believed him, for Moses wrote of him, and asks how they will believe his words if they do not believe his writings.
teachings.quote: For had ye believed Moses, ye would have believed me: for he wrote of me. But if ye believe not his writings, how shall ye believe my words?
teachings.title: Moses Wrote of Christ — Do You Believe His Words

teachings.text: Jesus declares that their father Abraham rejoiced to see his day, and that he saw it and was glad.
teachings.quote: Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day: and he saw it, and was glad.
teachings.title: Abraham Rejoiced to See the Day of Christ

teachings.text: At the Last Supper Jesus gives the disciples bread and the cup as his body and his blood of the new covenant poured out for many for the remission of sins, charging them to do this in remembrance of him.
teachings.quote: Take, eat; this is my body. Drink ye all of it;
teachings.title: The Lord's Supper — Do This in Remembrance of Me

teachings.text: Jesus declares that the cup is his blood of the new covenant, poured out for many for the remission of sins.
teachings.quote: For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.
teachings.title: This Cup Is My Blood of the New Covenant

teachings.text: Jesus pledges he will not drink of the fruit of the vine again until the day he drinks it new with his disciples in his Father's kingdom.
teachings.quote: But I say unto you, I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.
teachings.title: I Will Not Drink Again Until the Father's Kingdom

subcategories.title: The Bread of Life — A Connected Teaching

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Samaritan woman that if she knew the gift of God and who was speaking, she would have asked him for living water.
teachings.quote: If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.
teachings.title: If You Knew the Gift of God — Living Water

teachings.text: Jesus says whoever drinks of this well water will thirst again.
teachings.quote: Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again:
teachings.title: Whoever Drinks This Water Will Thirst Again

teachings.text: Jesus corrects the crowd that not Moses but his Father gives the true bread from heaven, which comes down and gives life to the world.
teachings.quote: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Moses gave you not that bread from heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven. For the bread of God is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world.
teachings.title: The Father Gives the True Bread from Heaven

teachings.text: Jesus declares he is the bread of life — the living bread from heaven whose flesh he will give for the life of the world.
teachings.quote: I am the bread of life: he that cometh to me shall never hunger; and he that believeth on me shall never thirst. I am the living bread which came down from heaven: if any man eat of this bread, he shall live for ever: and the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world.
teachings.title: I Am the Bread of Life from Heaven

teachings.text: Jesus says their fathers ate manna in the wilderness and died, but the bread that comes down from heaven lets one eat and not die.
teachings.quote: Your fathers did eat manna in the wilderness, and are dead. This is the bread which cometh down from heaven, that a man may eat thereof, and not die.
teachings.title: The Fathers Ate Manna and Died

teachings.text: Jesus declares that unless they eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, they have no life in them.
teachings.quote: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of man, and drink his blood, ye have no life in you.
teachings.title: Eat My Flesh and Drink My Blood

teachings.text: Jesus says whoever eats his flesh and drinks his blood has eternal life and will be raised up at the last day, for his flesh is true food and his blood true drink; such a one abides in him and he in them.
teachings.quote: Whoso eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, hath eternal life; and I will raise him up at the last day. For my flesh is meat indeed, and my blood is drink indeed. He that eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, dwelleth in me, and I in him.
teachings.title: My Flesh Is True Food, My Blood True Drink

teachings.text: Jesus promises that whoever feeds on him will live by him forever, unlike the fathers who ate manna and died.
teachings.quote: As the living Father hath sent me, and I live by the Father: so he that eateth me, even he shall live by me. This is that bread which came down from heaven: not as your fathers did eat manna, and are dead: he that eateth of this bread shall live for ever.
teachings.title: Feed on Christ and Live by Him Forever

teachings.text: Jesus clarifies that the Spirit gives life and the flesh profits nothing — the words he speaks are spirit and life.
teachings.quote: It is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life.
teachings.title: My Words Are Spirit and Life

subcategories.title: New and Old — The Covenant Transition

teachings.text: Jesus asks whether the wedding guests can mourn while the bridegroom is with them, then teaches that no one sews new cloth on an old garment or the tear is made worse, and no one puts new wine into old wineskins or the skins burst and the wine is spilled — new wine goes into new wineskins so both are preserved.
teachings.quote: Can the children of the bridechamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then shall they fast. No man putteth a piece of new cloth unto an old garment, for that which is put in to fill it up taketh from the garment, and the rent is made worse. Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break, and the wine runneth out, and the bottles perish: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved.
teachings.title: New Wine in Old Wineskins

subcategories.title: The Lord's Prayer — Pattern for Prayer

teachings.text: Jesus teaches his disciples to pray this way, addressing God as their Father in heaven and hallowing his name.
teachings.quote: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.
teachings.title: Pray to Our Father Who Is in Heaven

teachings.text: Jesus prays for the Father's kingdom to come and his will to be done on earth as it is in heaven.
teachings.quote: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.
teachings.title: Thy Kingdom Come, Thy Will Be Done

teachings.text: Jesus asks the Father to give us this day our daily bread.
teachings.quote: Give us this day our daily bread.
teachings.title: Give Us This Day Our Daily Bread

teachings.text: Jesus prays that the Father would forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors.
teachings.quote: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
teachings.title: Forgive Us as We Forgive Our Debtors

teachings.text: Jesus prays that the Father would lead us not into temptation but deliver us from evil, for his is the kingdom, power, and glory forever.
teachings.quote: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
teachings.title: Deliver Us from Evil — Thine Is the Kingdom

teachings.text: Jesus charges his disciples not to pray like hypocrites in public, but to enter their room and pray to the Father in secret.
teachings.quote: ¶ And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward. But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.
teachings.title: Pray to the Father in Secret, Not for Show

teachings.text: Jesus warns against vain repetitions, for the Father knows what his children need before they ask him.
teachings.quote: But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking. Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.
teachings.title: Do Not Use Vain Repetitions — the Father Knows

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples that when they stand praying they must forgive any grievance, that the Father in heaven may forgive their trespasses.
teachings.quote: And when ye stand praying, forgive, if ye have ought against any: that your Father also which is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses.
teachings.title: Forgive When You Stand Praying

teachings.text: Jesus charges his hearers to ask and it will be given, seek and they will find, knock and it will be opened, for everyone who asks receives, and asks what father would give his son a stone for bread or a serpent for a fish.
teachings.quote: ¶ Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you: For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened. Or what man is there of you, whom if his son ask bread, will he give him a stone? Or if he ask a fish, will he give him a serpent?
teachings.title: Ask, Seek, Knock — the Father Gives Good Gifts

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples that this kind can come forth by nothing but by prayer and fasting.
teachings.quote: This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.
teachings.title: This Kind Comes Out Only by Prayer and Fasting

teachings.text: Jesus tells of a man who goes to a friend at midnight for three loaves. Though the friend refuses because his door is shut and his children are in bed, yet because of the man's persistence he rises and gives him what he needs.
teachings.quote: Which of you shall have a friend, and shall go unto him at midnight, and say unto him, Friend, lend me three loaves; For a friend of mine in his journey is come to me, and I have nothing to set before him? And he from within shall answer and say, Trouble me not: the door is now shut, and my children are with me in bed; I cannot rise and give thee. I say unto you, Though he will not rise and give him, because he is his friend, yet because of his importunity he will rise and give him as many as he needeth.
teachings.title: The Persistent Friend at Midnight

teachings.text: Jesus tells of a widow who keeps pressing an unjust judge until he avenges her, and declares God will much more speedily avenge his elect who cry day and night, asking whether the Son of Man will find faith on earth when he comes.
teachings.quote: There was in a city a judge, which feared not God, neither regarded man: And there was a widow in that city; and she came unto him, saying, Avenge me of mine adversary. And he would not for a while: but afterward he said within himself, Though I fear not God, nor regard man; Yet because this widow troubleth me, I will avenge her, lest by her continual coming she weary me. Hear what the unjust judge saith. And shall not God avenge his own elect, which cry day and night unto him, though he bear long with them? I tell you that he will avenge them speedily. Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?
teachings.title: The Persistent Widow and Unjust Judge

teachings.text: Jesus promises that whatever his disciples ask in his name he will do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
teachings.quote: And whatsoever ye shall ask in my name, that will I do, that the Father may be glorified in the Son. If ye shall ask any thing in my name, I will do it.
teachings.title: Ask in My Name and the Father Will Be Glorified

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples he chose them to bear lasting fruit, that whatever they ask the Father in his name he may give them.
teachings.quote: Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain: that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you.
teachings.title: Ask the Father in My Name — Bear Lasting Fruit

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples a time comes when he will speak plainly of the Father, and in that day they will ask in his name.
teachings.quote: These things have I spoken unto you in proverbs: but the time cometh, when I shall no more speak unto you in proverbs, but I shall shew you plainly of the Father. At that day ye shall ask in my name: and I say not unto you, that I will pray the Father for you:
teachings.title: In That Day You Will Ask in My Name

teachings.text: Jesus declares that he is the true vine and his Father the vinedresser, removing every fruitless branch and pruning every fruitful one to bear more.
teachings.quote: I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman. Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away: and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit.
teachings.title: Christ the True Vine, the Father the Vinedresser

teachings.text: Jesus charges his disciples to abide in him as the branch in the vine. He is the vine, they are the branches, and whoever abides in him bears much fruit. Apart from him they can do nothing, and branches that do not abide are burned.
teachings.quote: Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me. I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing. If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned.
teachings.title: Abide in Me or Be Cast Out and Burned

teachings.text: Jesus promises that those abiding in him with his words may ask what they wish; the Father is glorified by their fruit.
teachings.quote: If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you. Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; so shall ye be my disciples.
teachings.title: Ask Whatever You Will Abiding in Him

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples that if they love him they will keep his commandments.
teachings.quote: ¶ If ye love me, keep my commandments.
teachings.title: Love for Christ Expressed Through Obedience

teachings.text: Jesus promises that whoever loves him keeps his word and is loved by the Father; he and the Father will come and make their home with him. The word they hear is not his own but the Father's who sent him.
teachings.quote: If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him. He that loveth me not keepeth not my sayings: and the word which ye hear is not mine, but the Father’s which sent me. These things have I spoken unto you, being yet present with you.
teachings.title: Love and Obedience Bring the Father's Indwelling

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples that they are already clean through the word he has spoken to them.
teachings.quote: Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.
teachings.title: Already Clean Through the Word He Spoke

teachings.text: Jesus says that as the Father has loved him so he has loved them, and bids them abide in his love by keeping his commandments.
teachings.quote: As the Father hath loved me, so have I loved you: continue ye in my love. If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and abide in his love.
teachings.title: Abide in His Love by Keeping His Commandments

teachings.text: Jesus says he has spoken these things to his disciples so that his joy may remain in them and their joy may be full.
teachings.quote: These things have I spoken unto you, that my joy might remain in you, and that your joy might be full.
teachings.title: His Joy Spoken So Their Joy Is Full

categories.title: The High Priestly Prayer
categories.description: This chapter records Jesus praying aloud before his arrest — his intercession for himself, his disciples, and all who will believe.

subcategories.title: Prayer for Himself — The Hour Has Come

teachings.text: Jesus prays the hour has come; he asks the Father to glorify the Son, who has authority to give eternal life to all given him.
teachings.quote: Father, the hour is come; glorify thy Son, that thy Son also may glorify thee: As thou hast given him power over all flesh, that he should give eternal life to as many as thou hast given him.
teachings.title: The Hour Has Come — Glorify the Son

teachings.text: Jesus prays that eternal life is to know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he has sent.
teachings.quote: And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent.
teachings.title: Eternal Life Is Knowing the Father and Son

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Father he has finished his work, and asks to be glorified with the glory he had with him before the world was.
teachings.quote: And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom thou hast sent. I have glorified thee on the earth: I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do. And now, O Father, glorify thou me with thine own self with the glory which I had with thee before the world was.
teachings.title: Work Finished — Restore the Preexistent Glory

teachings.text: Jesus prays not for the world but for those the Father has given him, asking the Holy Father to keep them in his name that they may be one as he and the Father are one, and to keep them from the evil one.
teachings.quote: I have manifested thy name unto the men which thou gavest me out of the world: thine they were, and thou gavest them me; and they have kept thy word. I pray for them: I pray not for the world, but for them which thou hast given me; for they are thine. And now I am no more in the world, but these are in the world, and I come to thee. Holy Father, keep through thine own name those whom thou hast given me, that they may be one, as we are. I pray not that thou shouldest take them out of the world, but that thou shouldest keep them from the evil.
teachings.title: Keep Them in Your Name That They Be One

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Father the disciples have received the words he gave them, knowing he came from the Father and believing the Father sent him.
teachings.quote: Now they have known that all things whatsoever thou hast given me are of thee. For I have given unto them the words which thou gavest me; and they have received them, and have known surely that I came out from thee, and they have believed that thou didst send me.
teachings.title: The Disciples Received and Believed the Father Sent Him

teachings.text: Jesus declares to the Father that all his are the Father's and all the Father's are his, and that he is glorified in them.
teachings.quote: And all mine are thine, and thine are mine; and I am glorified in them.
teachings.title: All Mine Are Yours and I Am Glorified in Them

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Father that he kept the disciples in his name and none was lost but the son of perdition. He speaks these things so they may have his joy, though the world hates them since they are not of the world.
teachings.quote: While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name: those that thou gavest me I have kept, and none of them is lost, but the son of perdition; that the scripture might be fulfilled. And now come I to thee; and these things I speak in the world, that they might have my joy fulfilled in themselves. I have given them thy word; and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.
teachings.title: None Lost but the Son of Perdition

teachings.text: Jesus says that his disciples are not of the world, even as he is not of the world.
teachings.quote: They are not of the world, even as I am not of the world.
teachings.title: His Disciples Are Not of This World

teachings.text: Jesus prays that the Father sanctify the disciples through his truth, his word being truth. As the Father sent him into the world he sends them, and for their sakes he sanctifies himself that they also may be sanctified through the truth.
teachings.quote: Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth. As thou hast sent me into the world, even so have I also sent them into the world. And for their sakes I sanctify myself, that they also might be sanctified through the truth.
teachings.title: Sanctify Them in the Truth of Your Word

teachings.text: Jesus prays for all who will believe on him through their word, that they all may be one as the Father is in him and he in the Father, so the world may believe the Father sent him and loved them as he loved him.
teachings.quote: Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word; That they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us: that the world may believe that thou hast sent me. I in them, and thou in me, that they may be made perfect in one; and that the world may know that thou hast sent me, and hast loved them, as thou hast loved me.
teachings.title: That All Believers May Be One as We Are

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Father he has given the disciples the glory given him. He wills that they be with him to behold his glory given before the foundation of the world, so the Father's love for him may be in them, and he in them.
teachings.quote: And the glory which thou gavest me I have given them; that they may be one, even as we are one: Father, I will that they also, whom thou hast given me, be with me where I am; that they may behold my glory, which thou hast given me: for thou lovedst me before the foundation of the world. And I have declared unto them thy name, and will declare it: that the love wherewith thou hast loved me may be in them, and I in them.
teachings.title: Father, Let Them Behold My Glory With You

teachings.text: Jesus calls on the righteous Father, saying the world has not known him. But he has, and these know the Father sent him.
teachings.quote: O righteous Father, the world hath not known thee: but I have known thee, and these have known that thou hast sent me.
teachings.title: The World Did Not Know You, but I Did

teachings.text: Jesus names the first and great commandment as to love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and mind, names love of neighbor as the second like it, and declares that on these two hang all the Law and the Prophets.
teachings.quote: Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind. This is the first and great commandment. And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.
teachings.title: The Two Greatest Commandments — Love God and Neighbor

teachings.text: Jesus tells of a man left half dead by thieves, passed by a priest and Levite but tended by a Samaritan who binds his wounds and pays for his care at an inn, and charges his hearer to go and do likewise.
teachings.quote: A certain man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho, and fell among thieves, which stripped him of his raiment, and wounded him, and departed, leaving him half dead. And by chance there came down a certain priest that way: and when he saw him, he passed by on the other side. And likewise a Levite, when he was at the place, came and looked on him, and passed by on the other side. But a certain Samaritan, as he journeyed, came where he was: and when he saw him, he had compassion on him, And went to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring in oil and wine, and set him on his own beast, and brought him to an inn, and took care of him. And on the morrow when he departed, he took out two pence, and gave them to the host, and said unto him, Take care of him; and whatsoever thou spendest more, when I come again, I will repay thee. Which now of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour unto him that fell among the thieves? Go, and do thou likewise.
teachings.title: The Good Samaritan

teachings.text: Jesus says to love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat and persecute you, calling his hearers to be merciful as their Father is merciful.
teachings.quote: But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you;
teachings.title: Love Your Enemies and Pray for Persecutors

teachings.text: Jesus asks what reward there is in loving only those who love you or greeting only your brothers, since even tax collectors do the same, and charges his hearers to lend hoping for nothing in return.
teachings.quote: For if ye love them which love you, what reward have ye? do not even the publicans the same? And if ye salute your brethren only, what do ye more than others? do not even the publicans so?
teachings.title: No Reward in Loving Only Those Who Love You

teachings.text: Jesus gives a new commandment, that his disciples love one another as he has loved them, and says by this all will know they are his disciples, if they have love for one another.
teachings.quote: A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another. By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.
teachings.title: Love One Another as I Have Loved You

teachings.text: Jesus declares no greater love exists than to lay down his life for his friends, and calls them friends if they do what he commands.
teachings.quote: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends. Ye are my friends, if ye do whatsoever I command you.
teachings.title: Greater Love Has No One Than to Lay Down Life

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples he no longer calls them servants but friends, having made known all he heard from his Father.
teachings.quote: Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends; for all things that I have heard of my Father I have made known unto you.
teachings.title: No Longer Servants but Friends Who Know His Mind

categories.title: Righteousness and Ethics
categories.description: This category covers the ethical teachings of the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 5–7) and Sermon on the Plain (Luke 6), including Jesus’s radical internalization of righteousness.

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples they are the salt of the earth, and that if the salt loses its savor it is good for nothing but to be cast out and trampled under foot.
teachings.quote: ¶ Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men.
teachings.title: You Are the Salt of the Earth

teachings.text: Jesus tells his hearers they are the light of the world, that a city set on a hill cannot be hidden, and charges them to let their light shine before men so others may glorify their Father in heaven.
teachings.quote: Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid. Neither do men light a candle, and put it under a bushel, but on a candlestick; and it giveth light unto all that are in the house. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
teachings.title: You Are the Light of the World

teachings.text: Jesus declares he has not come to destroy the law but to fulfill it. Not one jot or tittle will pass till all is fulfilled; whoever breaks the least commandment will be called least, while whoever keeps and teaches them will be great.
teachings.quote: ¶ Think not that I am come to destroy the law, or the prophets: I am not come to destroy, but to fulfil. For verily I say unto you, Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law, till all be fulfilled. Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.title: Christ Came to Fulfill the Law, Not Abolish It

teachings.text: Jesus says that unless his hearers' righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, they will in no way enter the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.quote: For I say unto you, That except your righteousness shall exceed the righteousness of the scribes and Pharisees, ye shall in no case enter into the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.title: Righteousness Must Exceed That of the Pharisees

subcategories.title: The Antitheses — “You Have Heard… But I Say to You”

teachings.text: Jesus teaches that whoever is angry with his brother without cause is in danger of judgment, and contempt brings one into hell fire.
teachings.quote: ¶ Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment: But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment: and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council: but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.
teachings.title: Anger Toward a Brother Brings Judgment

teachings.text: Jesus teaches that whoever looks at a woman to lust has already committed adultery with her in his heart, and if the right eye or hand causes sin, it is better to lose it than have the whole body cast into hell.
teachings.quote: ¶ Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not commit adultery: But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart. And if thy right eye offend thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell. And if thy right hand offend thee, cut it off, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.
teachings.title: Lust in the Heart Is Adultery

teachings.text: Jesus says that whoever puts away his wife, except for the cause of fornication, causes her to commit adultery, and whoever marries her who is divorced commits adultery.
teachings.quote: It hath been said, Whosoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorcement: But I say unto you, That whosoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, causeth her to commit adultery: and whosoever shall marry her that is divorced committeth adultery.
teachings.title: Divorce Except for Fornication Causes Adultery

teachings.text: Jesus charges his hearers not to swear at all, neither by heaven nor earth nor Jerusalem nor their head. Let their yes be yes and their no be no, for whatever is more comes of evil.
teachings.quote: ¶ Again, ye have heard that it hath been said by them of old time, Thou shalt not forswear thyself, but shalt perform unto the Lord thine oaths: But I say unto you, Swear not at all; neither by heaven; for it is God’s throne: Nor by the earth; for it is his footstool: neither by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great King. Neither shalt thou swear by thy head, because thou canst not make one hair white or black. But let your communication be, Yea, yea; Nay, nay: for whatsoever is more than these cometh of evil.
teachings.title: Do Not Swear — Let Your Yes Be Yes

teachings.text: Jesus teaches his hearers not to resist evil but to turn the other cheek and give their cloak to whoever sues for their coat. He charges them to go two miles with whoever compels them one, and to give to whoever asks.
teachings.quote: ¶ Ye have heard that it hath been said, An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth: But I say unto you, That ye resist not evil: but whosoever shall smite thee on thy right cheek, turn to him the other also. And if any man will sue thee at the law, and take away thy coat, let him have thy cloke also. And whosoever shall compel thee to go a mile, go with him twain. Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.
teachings.title: Turn the Other Cheek and Give to Those Who Ask

teachings.text: Jesus warns his hearers not to do their alms before men like the hypocrites who sound a trumpet and already have their reward. Give so secretly the left hand knows not what the right does, and the Father who sees in secret will reward you.
teachings.quote: Take heed that ye do not your alms before men, to be seen of them: otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven. Therefore when thou doest thine alms, do not sound a trumpet before thee, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may have glory of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward. But when thou doest alms, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth: That thine alms may be in secret: and thy Father which seeth in secret himself shall reward thee openly.
teachings.title: Give in Secret, Not to Be Seen by Men

teachings.text: Jesus charges his hearers, when they fast, not to look sad like the hypocrites who disfigure their faces to be seen by men. Let them anoint the head and wash the face so the fast is seen only by the Father, who will reward them.
teachings.quote: ¶ Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward. But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face; That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret: and thy Father, which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly.
teachings.title: Fast in Private, Not Like the Hypocrites

teachings.text: Jesus says, Judge not, that you be not judged, for the measure you use will be measured back. He asks why they see the speck in their brother's eye but not the beam in their own, charging them first to cast out their own beam.
teachings.quote: Judge not, that ye be not judged. For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again. And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me pull out the mote out of thine eye; and, behold, a beam is in thine own eye? Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother’s eye.
teachings.title: Judge Not and Remove the Beam From Your Eye

teachings.text: Jesus charges his hearers not to give what is holy to dogs nor cast pearls before swine, lest they be trampled and turned upon.
teachings.quote: ¶ Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.
teachings.title: Do Not Cast Pearls Before Swine

teachings.text: Jesus tells the accusers of the woman caught in adultery that he who is without sin among them should cast the first stone at her.
teachings.quote: He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her.
teachings.title: Let the Sinless One Cast the First Stone

subcategories.title: The Golden Rule and Two Ways

teachings.text: Jesus teaches that whatever his hearers would have men do to them, they should do likewise, for this is the law and the prophets.
teachings.quote: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them: for this is the law and the prophets.
teachings.title: Do Unto Others as You Would Have Them Do

teachings.text: Jesus likens whoever hears his sayings and does them to a wise man who built on rock, which stood when the storms came. Whoever hears but does them not is like a foolish man who built on sand, and great was its fall.
teachings.quote: ¶ Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell not: for it was founded upon a rock. And every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand: And the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; and it fell: and great was the fall of it.
teachings.title: The Wise and Foolish Builders

subcategories.title: The Nature of Greatness in the Kingdom

teachings.text: Jesus declares that whoever receives one such little child in his name receives him.
teachings.quote: And whoso shall receive one such little child in my name receiveth me.
teachings.title: Receive a Child in My Name and Receive Me

teachings.text: Jesus says that many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.
teachings.quote: But many that are first shall be last; and the last shall be first.
teachings.title: The First Will Be Last and the Last First

teachings.text: Jesus tells the mother of Zebedee's sons and the disciples that they do not know what they ask, that drinking his cup is theirs but sitting at his right or left is the Father's to give. He charges that unlike Gentile rulers who lord it over others, whoever would be great among them must be their servant and whoever would be first must be slave of all.
teachings.quote: What wilt thou? Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father. Ye know that the princes of the Gentiles exercise dominion over them, and they that are great exercise authority upon them. But it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister; And whosoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant:
teachings.title: Whoever Would Be Great Must Become Servant of All

teachings.text: Jesus declares that the greatest among them will be their servant, and that whoever exalts himself will be humbled while whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
teachings.quote: But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant. And whosoever shall exalt himself shall be abased; and he that shall humble himself shall be exalted.
teachings.title: The Humble Will Be Exalted, the Proud Humbled

teachings.text: Jesus says the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.
teachings.quote: Even as the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.
teachings.title: The Son of Man Came to Serve

teachings.text: Jesus tells Peter he does not understand now but will know later, and unless Peter is washed he has no part with him.
teachings.quote: What I do thou knowest not now; but thou shalt know hereafter. If I wash thee not, thou hast no part with me.
teachings.title: Unless I Wash You, You Have No Part With Me

teachings.text: Jesus says one who is washed needs only to wash his feet but is wholly clean, and the disciples are clean, though not all.
teachings.quote: He that is washed needeth not save to wash his feet, but is clean every whit: and ye are clean, but not all.
teachings.title: The Washed Disciple Is Wholly Clean

teachings.text: Jesus asks the disciples if they know what he has done, and affirms they rightly call him Master and Lord, for so he is.
teachings.quote: Know ye what I have done to you? Ye call me Master and Lord: and ye say well; for so I am.
teachings.title: You Rightly Call Me Lord — for So I Am

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples that since he their Lord has washed their feet, they ought to wash one another's feet by his example. The servant is not greater than his lord, and they are blessed if they do these things.
teachings.quote: If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another’s feet. For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you. Verily, verily, I say unto you, The servant is not greater than his lord; neither he that is sent greater than he that sent him. If ye know these things, happy are ye if ye do them.
teachings.title: Wash One Another's Feet as I Have Done

teachings.text: Jesus tells the invited to take the lowest seat lest they be moved down in shame, for whoever exalts himself will be humbled. When they host a feast, they should invite the poor and lame who cannot repay them, and be repaid at the resurrection.
teachings.quote: When thou art bidden of any man to a wedding, sit not down in the highest room; lest a more honourable man than thou be bidden of him; And he that bade thee and him come and say to thee, Give this man place; and thou begin with shame to take the lowest room. But when thou art bidden, go and sit down in the lowest room; that when he that bade thee cometh, he may say unto thee, Friend, go up higher: then shalt thou have worship in the presence of them that sit at meat with thee. For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted. When thou makest a dinner or a supper, call not thy friends, nor thy brethren, neither thy kinsmen, nor thy rich neighbours; lest they also bid thee again, and a recompence be made thee. But when thou makest a feast, call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind: And thou shalt be blessed; for they cannot recompense thee: for thou shalt be recompensed at the resurrection of the just.
teachings.title: The Great Banquet

teachings.text: Jesus tells of a servant who must serve his master's meal before eating, and asks if the master thanks him for what was commanded. So when disciples have done all, they should say they are unworthy servants who only did their duty.
teachings.quote: But which of you, having a servant plowing or feeding cattle, will say unto him by and by, when he is come from the field, Go and sit down to meat? And will not rather say unto him, Make ready wherewith I may sup, and gird thyself, and serve me, till I have eaten and drunken; and afterward thou shalt eat and drink? Doth he thank that servant because he did the things that were commanded him? I trow not. So likewise ye, when ye shall have done all those things which are commanded you, say, We are unprofitable servants: we have done that which was our duty to do.
teachings.title: The Unworthy Servants

teachings.text: Jesus declares that unless his hearers are converted and become as little children they will not enter the kingdom of heaven, and whoever humbles himself as a little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.quote: Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children, ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven. Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, the same is greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.title: Become as a Little Child to Enter the Kingdom

teachings.text: Jesus asks the chief priests and scribes if they have never read that out of the mouth of babes and infants God has perfected praise.
teachings.quote: Yea; have ye never read, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise?
teachings.title: Out of the Mouths of Babes God Perfects Praise

subcategories.title: The Power and Accountability of Words
