teachings.text: Jesus says people will give account for every idle word on judgment day — by their words they will be justified or condemned.
teachings.quote: But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment. For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.
teachings.title: Account for Every Idle Word on Judgment Day

teachings.text: Jesus teaches that what proceeds out of the mouth comes from the heart, and these things defile the person.
teachings.quote: But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man.
teachings.title: What Comes Out of the Mouth Defiles the Person

teachings.text: Jesus declares his testimony of himself is true because he knows where he came from and where he is going. The law accepts the testimony of two witnesses — he bears witness of himself, and the Father who sent him also bears witness.
teachings.quote: Though I bear record of myself, yet my record is true: for I know whence I came, and whither I go; but ye cannot tell whence I come, and whither I go. It is also written in your law, that the testimony of two men is true. I am one that bear witness of myself, and the Father that sent me beareth witness of me.
teachings.title: His Testimony Is True — Father and Son Bear Witness

teachings.text: Jesus says you will know the truth and the truth will make you free; if the Son makes you free, you are free indeed.
teachings.quote: And ye shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free. If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.
teachings.title: The Truth Will Set You Free

teachings.text: Jesus declares that he is the way, the truth, and the life, and no one comes to the Father except through him.
teachings.quote: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.
teachings.title: I Am the Way, the Truth, and the Life

teachings.text: Jesus repeats his summons that he who has ears to hear, let him hear, calling his hearers throughout his ministry to give spiritual attention to his words.
teachings.quote: He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
teachings.title: He Who Has Ears to Hear, Let Him Hear

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples it is given them to know the mysteries of the kingdom, and he speaks to the multitudes in parables because seeing they do not see and hearing they do not hear. He blesses their eyes and ears for what they see.
teachings.quote: Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given. For whosoever hath, to him shall be given, and he shall have more abundance: but whosoever hath not, from him shall be taken away even that he hath. Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand. But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear. For verily I say unto you, That many prophets and righteous men have desired to see those things which ye see, and have not seen them; and to hear those things which ye hear, and have not heard them.
teachings.title: Mysteries of the Kingdom Given to the Disciples

teachings.text: Jesus calls the multitude to him and charges them to hear and understand.
teachings.quote: Hear, and understand:
teachings.title: Hear and Understand What Enters the Mouth

teachings.text: Jesus asks his disciples whether they are also without understanding, that whatever enters the mouth goes into the stomach and is expelled.
teachings.quote: Are ye also yet without understanding? Do not ye yet understand, that whatsoever entereth in at the mouth goeth into the belly, and is cast out into the draught?
teachings.title: Are You Also Without Understanding?

teachings.text: Jesus charges his hearers to take heed what they hear, for the measure they use will be measured to them. To him who has, more will be given; from him who has not, even what he has will be taken.
teachings.quote: Take heed what ye hear: with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you: and unto you that hear shall more be given. For he that hath, to him shall be given: and he that hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he hath.
teachings.title: Take Heed What You Hear

teachings.text: Jesus declares that if any man has ears to hear, let him hear.
teachings.quote: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.
teachings.title: If Any Man Has Ears to Hear, Let Him Hear

teachings.text: Jesus says to let the Pharisees alone, for they are blind leaders of the blind, and if the blind lead the blind both will fall into the ditch.
teachings.quote: Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind. And if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch.
teachings.title: Blind Leaders of the Blind Will Both Fall

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Pharisees and Sadducees that when it is evening they say it will be fair weather, for the sky is red.
teachings.quote: When it is evening, ye say, It will be fair weather: for the sky is red.
teachings.title: You Read the Sky but Miss the Signs

teachings.text: Jesus asks why this generation seeks a sign, and declares that truly no sign will be given to this generation.
teachings.quote: Why doth this generation seek after a sign? verily I say unto you, There shall no sign be given unto this generation.
teachings.title: No Sign Will Be Given to This Generation

teachings.text: Jesus charges his disciples to take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the leaven of Herod.
teachings.quote: Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod.
teachings.title: Beware the Leaven of the Pharisees and Herod

teachings.text: Jesus rebukes the disciples for reasoning that they have no bread, asking whether they still do not perceive or understand. He reminds them of the baskets gathered after the five loaves and the seven, asking how they still do not understand.
teachings.quote: Why reason ye, because ye have no bread? perceive ye not yet, neither understand? have ye your heart yet hardened? Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember? When I brake the five loaves among five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? And when the seven among four thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? How is it that ye do not understand?
teachings.title: Do You Still Not Perceive or Understand?

teachings.text: Jesus says when a cloud rises in the west they predict a shower, and when the south wind blows they predict heat.
teachings.quote: When ye see a cloud rise out of the west, straightway ye say, There cometh a shower; and so it is. And when ye see the south wind blow, ye say, There will be heat; and it cometh to pass.
teachings.title: You Read Weather Signs but Not the Present Time

teachings.text: Jesus declares he came for judgment, that those who do not see may see and those who see may be made blind.
teachings.quote: For judgment I am come into this world, that they which see not might see; and that they which see might be made blind.
teachings.title: I Came for Judgment — the Blind Will See

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Pharisees that if they were blind they would have no sin, but because they say they see, their sin remains.
teachings.quote: If ye were blind, ye should have no sin: but now ye say, We see; therefore your sin remaineth.
teachings.title: Claiming to See Makes Their Sin Remain

teachings.text: Jesus warns of false prophets in sheep's clothing who inwardly are ravening wolves. They will be known by their fruits, for a corrupt tree cannot bear good fruit, and every barren tree is hewn down and burned.
teachings.quote: ¶ Beware of false prophets, which come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly they are ravening wolves. Ye shall know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes of thorns, or figs of thistles? Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit. A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit. Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them.
teachings.title: Beware False Prophets — Known by Their Fruits

teachings.text: Jesus teaches that the tree is known by its fruit. He calls his hearers a generation of vipers, asking how being evil they can speak good, for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
teachings.quote: Either make the tree good, and his fruit good; or else make the tree corrupt, and his fruit corrupt: for the tree is known by his fruit. O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh. A good man out of the good treasure of the heart bringeth forth good things: and an evil man out of the evil treasure bringeth forth evil things.
teachings.title: A Corrupt Tree Cannot Bear Good Fruit

teachings.text: Jesus charges his disciples to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
teachings.quote: Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.
teachings.title: Beware the Leaven of Pharisaic Hypocrisy

teachings.text: Jesus warns that if anyone says here is Christ or there, they are not to believe it. False christs and false prophets will arise and show great signs and wonders to deceive, if possible, even the elect.
teachings.quote: Then if any man shall say unto you, Lo, here is Christ, or there; believe it not. For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect. Behold, I have told you before. Wherefore if they shall say unto you, Behold, he is in the desert; go not forth: behold, he is in the secret chambers; believe it not.
teachings.title: False Christs Will Arise to Deceive if Possible

teachings.text: Jesus declares that this is the condemnation: light has come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light because their deeds were evil. Everyone who does evil hates the light, but he who does truth comes to the light.
teachings.quote: And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil. For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved. But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.
teachings.title: Men Loved Darkness Rather Than Light

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples not to fear, for there is nothing covered that will not be revealed, nothing hidden that will not be known. What he tells them in darkness, speak in light; what they hear in the ear, preach on the housetops.
teachings.quote: Fear them not therefore: for there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; and hid, that shall not be known. What I tell you in darkness, that speak ye in light: and what ye hear in the ear, that preach ye upon the housetops.
teachings.title: Nothing Hidden That Will Not Be Revealed

teachings.text: Jesus asks whether a candle is brought to be put under a bushel or a bed rather than on a candlestick, declaring that nothing is hidden that will not be made manifest, nor kept secret but that it should come abroad.
teachings.quote: Is a candle brought to be put under a bushel, or under a bed? and not to be set on a candlestick? For there is nothing hid, which shall not be manifested; neither was any thing kept secret, but that it should come abroad.
teachings.title: A Lamp Belongs on a Stand, Not Hidden

teachings.text: Jesus declares to a paralytic that his sins are forgiven, and when scribes call it blasphemy he asks whether it is easier to say your sins are forgiven or to say arise and walk, then heals the man so they may know the Son of Man has power on earth to forgive sins.
teachings.quote: Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee. Wherefore think ye evil in your hearts? For whether is easier, to say, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and walk? But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thine house.
teachings.title: Son of Man Has Authority on Earth to Forgive Sins

teachings.text: Jesus tells Simon of a creditor who forgave two debtors, one owing five hundred pence and the other fifty, and asks who will love him most. He contrasts the woman who washed his feet with tears against Simon, who gave no water, kiss, or oil.
teachings.quote: Simon, I have somewhat to say unto thee. There was a certain creditor which had two debtors: the one owed five hundred pence, and the other fifty. And when they had nothing to pay, he frankly forgave them both. Tell me therefore, which of them will love him most? Thou hast rightly judged. Seest thou this woman? I entered into thine house, thou gavest me no water for my feet: but she hath washed my feet with tears, and wiped them with the hairs of her head. Thou gavest me no kiss: but this woman since the time I came in hath not ceased to kiss my feet. My head with oil thou didst not anoint: but this woman hath anointed my feet with ointment.
teachings.title: The Two Debtors

teachings.text: Jesus declares that the woman's many sins are forgiven because she loved much, and the one forgiven little loves little.
teachings.quote: Wherefore I say unto thee, Her sins, which are many, are forgiven; for she loved much: but to whom little is forgiven, the same loveth little.
teachings.title: Forgiven Much Because She Loved Much

teachings.text: Jesus teaches that if you forgive others their trespasses, the heavenly Father will also forgive you, but if you do not forgive, neither will the Father forgive your trespasses.
teachings.quote: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you: But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
teachings.title: Forgive Others or the Father Will Not Forgive You

teachings.text: Jesus answers Peter that he is to forgive a brother not seven times but seventy times seven.
teachings.quote: I say not unto thee, Until seven times: but, Until seventy times seven.
teachings.title: Forgive Not Seven Times but Seventy Times Seven

teachings.text: Jesus likens the kingdom of heaven to a king who, moved with compassion, forgives a servant ten thousand talents. When that servant seizes a fellowservant owing a hundred pence and casts him into prison, the lord delivers him to the tormentors, warning his heavenly Father will do likewise unless they forgive a brother from the heart.
teachings.quote: ¶ Therefore is the kingdom of heaven likened unto a certain king, which would take account of his servants. And when he had begun to reckon, one was brought unto him, which owed him ten thousand talents. But forasmuch as he had not to pay, his lord commanded him to be sold, and his wife, and children, and all that he had, and payment to be made. The servant therefore fell down, and worshipped him, saying, Lord, have patience with me, and I will pay thee all. Then the lord of that servant was moved with compassion, and loosed him, and forgave him the debt. But the same servant went out, and found one of his fellowservants, which owed him an hundred pence: and he laid hands on him, and took him by the throat, saying, Pay me that thou owest. And his fellowservant fell down at his feet, and besought him, saying, Have patience with me, and I will pay thee all. And he would not: but went and cast him into prison, till he should pay the debt. So when his fellowservants saw what was done, they were very sorry, and came and told unto their lord all that was done. Then his lord, after that he had called him, said unto him, O thou wicked servant, I forgave thee all that debt, because thou desiredst me: Shouldest not thou also have had compassion on thy fellowservant, even as I had pity on thee? And his lord was wroth, and delivered him to the tormentors, till he should pay all that was due unto him. So likewise shall my heavenly Father do also unto you, if ye from your hearts forgive not every one his brother their trespasses.
teachings.title: The Unforgiving Servant

teachings.text: Jesus warns that if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive your trespasses.
teachings.quote: But if ye do not forgive, neither will your Father which is in heaven forgive your trespasses.
teachings.title: Unforgiveness Blocks the Father's Forgiveness of You

teachings.text: Jesus charges that if you bring a gift to the altar and remember a brother has something against you, first be reconciled, then offer it.
teachings.quote: Therefore if thou bring thy gift to the altar, and there rememberest that thy brother hath ought against thee; Leave there thy gift before the altar, and go thy way; first be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.
teachings.title: Be Reconciled to Your Brother Before Offering

teachings.text: Jesus counsels his hearers to agree with their adversary quickly while on the way. Otherwise the adversary will deliver them to the judge and the judge to the officer, and they will be cast into prison until they have paid the last farthing.
teachings.quote: Agree with thine adversary quickly, whiles thou art in the way with him; lest at any time the adversary deliver thee to the judge, and the judge deliver thee to the officer, and thou be cast into prison. Verily I say unto thee, Thou shalt by no means come out thence, till thou hast paid the uttermost farthing.
teachings.title: Settle Quickly With Your Adversary on the Way

teachings.text: Jesus instructs that if a brother trespasses, go and tell him his fault privately. If he refuses, take one or two witnesses. If he still refuses, tell the church; if he refuses the church, let him be as a heathen and a publican.
teachings.quote: ¶ Moreover if thy brother shall trespass against thee, go and tell him his fault between thee and him alone: if he shall hear thee, thou hast gained thy brother. But if he will not hear thee, then take with thee one or two more, that in the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established. And if he shall neglect to hear them, tell it unto the church: but if he neglect to hear the church, let him be unto thee as an heathen man and a publican.
teachings.title: Go to a Sinning Brother, Then Bring Witnesses

teachings.text: Jesus declares that whoever divorces his wife, except for fornication, causes her to commit adultery, and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
teachings.quote: But I say unto you, That whosoever shall put away his wife, saving for the cause of fornication, causeth her to commit adultery: and whosoever shall marry her that is divorced committeth adultery.
teachings.title: Divorce Except for Fornication Leads to Adultery

teachings.text: Jesus says that God made them male and female, that the two will be one flesh, and what God has joined together let no one separate. Moses permitted divorce only because of hardness of heart, but from the beginning it was not so.
teachings.quote: Have ye not read, that he which made them at the beginning made them male and female, And said, For this cause shall a man leave father and mother, and shall cleave to his wife: and they twain shall be one flesh? Wherefore they are no more twain, but one flesh. What therefore God hath joined together, let not man put asunder. Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so.
teachings.title: God Joined Them as One Flesh — Let None Separate

teachings.text: Jesus says not all can receive this saying, only those to whom it is given. He names eunuchs born so, eunuchs made by men, and those who made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven, and bids him who can receive it to receive it.
teachings.quote: All men cannot receive this saying, save they to whom it is given. For there are some eunuchs, which were so born from their mother’s womb: and there are some eunuchs, which were made eunuchs of men: and there be eunuchs, which have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven’s sake. He that is able to receive it, let him receive it.
teachings.title: Some Are Made Eunuchs for the Kingdom of Heaven

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Sadducees they err, not knowing the scriptures nor the power of God, that in the resurrection people neither marry nor are given in marriage but are as the angels of God in heaven, and that God is not the God of the dead but of the living, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
teachings.quote: Ye do err, not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God. For in the resurrection they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven. But as touching the resurrection of the dead, have ye not read that which was spoken unto you by God, saying, I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob? God is not the God of the dead, but of the living.
teachings.title: In the Resurrection There Is No Marriage

teachings.text: Jesus teaches that out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, and blasphemies.
teachings.quote: For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies:
teachings.title: Evil Thoughts and Immorality Proceed from the Heart

teachings.text: Jesus says he came not to send peace on earth but a sword, to set a man against his father, daughter against mother, and daughter-in-law against mother-in-law, and a man's foes will be those of his own household.
teachings.quote: Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.
teachings.title: Christ Brings Division Even Within Families

teachings.text: Jesus declares that he who loves father or mother more than him is not worthy of him, and he who loves son or daughter more than him is not worthy of him.
teachings.quote: He that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me: and he that loveth son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.
teachings.title: Love for Christ Must Surpass Love for Family

teachings.text: Jesus asks who is his mother and his brothers, then looks at those sitting around him and names them as his mother and his brothers.
teachings.quote: Who is my mother, or my brethren? Behold my mother and my brethren!
teachings.title: His True Family Are Those Around Him in Faith

teachings.text: Jesus names his mother and his brothers as those who hear the word of God and do it.
teachings.quote: My mother and my brethren are these which hear the word of God, and do it. Let us go over unto the other side of the lake.
teachings.title: His Mother and Brothers Are Those Who Obey God

teachings.text: Jesus warns that whoever offends one of these little ones would be better off drowned with a millstone around his neck. He charges his hearers not to despise these little ones, whose angels always behold his Father's face.
teachings.quote: But whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea. ¶ Woe unto the world because of offences! for it must needs be that offences come; but woe to that man by whom the offence cometh! Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven.
teachings.title: Do Not Offend or Despise These Little Ones

teachings.text: Jesus bids his disciples let the little children come to him and not forbid them, for of such is the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.quote: Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.title: Let the Children Come — the Kingdom Belongs to Them

teachings.text: Jesus teaches his hearers not to lay up treasures on earth where moth and rust corrupt and thieves steal, but to lay up treasures in heaven, for where their treasure is there will their heart be also.
teachings.quote: ¶ Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
teachings.title: Store Treasure in Heaven, Not on Earth

teachings.text: Jesus says the eye is the lamp of the body: if your eye is clear your whole body is full of light, but if your eye is bad your body is full of darkness. How great that darkness, if the light in you is dark.
teachings.quote: The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light. But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!
teachings.title: The Eye Is the Lamp of the Body

teachings.text: Jesus declares no one can serve two masters — they will love one and hate the other; you cannot serve God and mammon.
teachings.quote: ¶ No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
teachings.title: You Cannot Serve Both God and Mammon

teachings.text: Jesus refuses to arbitrate an inheritance dispute between two brothers, asking who made him a judge or a divider over them.
teachings.quote: Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?
teachings.title: Jesus Refuses to Arbitrate an Inheritance Dispute

teachings.text: Jesus says a rich man will hardly enter the kingdom of heaven, for it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God. What is impossible with men is possible with God.
teachings.quote: Verily I say unto you, That a rich man shall hardly enter into the kingdom of heaven. And again I say unto you, It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter into the kingdom of God. With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.
teachings.title: A Camel Through a Needle Before a Rich Man Enters

teachings.text: Jesus pronounces woe on the rich who have their consolation, and on those full and laughing now, for they will hunger, mourn, and weep.
teachings.quote: But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation. Woe unto you that are full! for ye shall hunger. Woe unto you that laugh now! for ye shall mourn and weep.
teachings.title: Woe to the Rich Who Have Their Consolation Now

teachings.text: Jesus warns against covetousness and tells of a rich man who planned bigger barns and ease for his soul. God said, You fool, this night your soul will be required of you. So is he who lays up treasure but is not rich toward God.
teachings.quote: Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth. The ground of a certain rich man brought forth plentifully: And he thought within himself, saying, What shall I do, because I have no room where to bestow my fruits? And he said, This will I do: I will pull down my barns, and build greater; and there will I bestow all my fruits and my goods. And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry. But God said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided? So is he that layeth up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.
teachings.title: The Rich Fool

teachings.text: Jesus charges his hearers to give to the one who asks and not to turn away from the one who would borrow.
teachings.quote: Give to him that asketh thee, and from him that would borrow of thee turn not thou away.
teachings.title: Give to the One Who Asks and Do Not Refuse

teachings.text: Jesus tells the rich young ruler that if he would be perfect he should sell what he has and give to the poor, and he will have treasure in heaven, and come and follow him.
teachings.quote: If thou wilt be perfect, go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.
teachings.title: Sell All and Give to the Poor to Follow Christ

teachings.text: Asked whether it is lawful to give tribute to Caesar, Jesus calls his questioners hypocrites and asks for the tribute coin. Seeing Caesar's image and inscription, he tells them to render to Caesar what is Caesar's and to God what is God's.
teachings.quote: Why tempt ye me, ye hypocrites? Shew me the tribute money. Whose is this image and superscription? Render therefore unto Cæsar the things which are Cæsar’s; and unto God the things that are God’s.
teachings.title: Render to Caesar and to God What Is Theirs

teachings.text: Jesus tells of a man who delivers talents to his servants — five, two, and one, each according to ability. On his return he commends those who doubled what they were given, but condemns the one who hid his talent as wicked and slothful, casting him into outer darkness. To everyone who has more will be given; from him who has not even what he has will be taken.
teachings.quote: ¶ For the kingdom of heaven is as a man travelling into a far country, who called his own servants, and delivered unto them his goods. And unto one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one; to every man according to his several ability; and straightway took his journey. Then he that had received the five talents went and traded with the same, and made them other five talents. And likewise he that had received two, he also gained other two. But he that had received one went and digged in the earth, and hid his lord’s money. After a long time the lord of those servants cometh, and reckoneth with them. And so he that had received five talents came and brought other five talents, saying, Lord, thou deliveredst unto me five talents: behold, I have gained beside them five talents more. His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord. He also that had received two talents came and said, Lord, thou deliveredst unto me two talents: behold, I have gained two other talents beside them. His lord said unto him, Well done, good and faithful servant; thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord. Then he which had received the one talent came and said, Lord, I knew thee that thou art an hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown, and gathering where thou hast not strawed: And I was afraid, and went and hid thy talent in the earth: lo, there thou hast that is thine. His lord answered and said unto him, Thou wicked and slothful servant, thou knewest that I reap where I sowed not, and gather where I have not strawed: Thou oughtest therefore to have put my money to the exchangers, and then at my coming I should have received mine own with usury. Take therefore the talent from him, and give it unto him which hath ten talents. For unto every one that hath shall be given, and he shall have abundance: but from him that hath not shall be taken away even that which he hath. And cast ye the unprofitable servant into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
teachings.title: The Parable of the Talents

teachings.text: Jesus says the poor widow has cast more into the treasury than all the others, for they gave out of their abundance but she out of her poverty cast in all she had, even all her living.
teachings.quote: Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury: For all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living.
teachings.title: The Poor Widow's Offering Exceeds All Others

teachings.text: Jesus tells of a steward accused of wasting his lord's goods who, about to be put out, calls in the debtors and reduces their bills to make friends for himself; the lord commends the unjust steward for acting wisely. He charges his hearers to make friends by the mammon of unrighteousness, says one faithful in little is faithful in much, and that no one can serve God and mammon.
teachings.quote: There was a certain rich man, which had a steward; and the same was accused unto him that he had wasted his goods. And he called him, and said unto him, How is it that I hear this of thee? give an account of thy stewardship; for thou mayest be no longer steward. Then the steward said within himself, What shall I do? for my lord taketh away from me the stewardship: I cannot dig; to beg I am ashamed. I am resolved what to do, that, when I am put out of the stewardship, they may receive me into their houses. So he called every one of his lord’s debtors unto him, and said unto the first, How much owest thou unto my lord? And he said, An hundred measures of oil. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and sit down quickly, and write fifty. Then said he to another, And how much owest thou? And he said, An hundred measures of wheat. And he said unto him, Take thy bill, and write fourscore. And the lord commended the unjust steward, because he had done wisely: for the children of this world are in their generation wiser than the children of light. And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations. He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much. If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches? And if ye have not been faithful in that which is another man’s, who shall give you that which is your own? ¶ No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
teachings.title: The Dishonest Manager

subcategories.title: The Blessing on the Poor and Woe to the Rich

teachings.text: Jesus blesses the poor for theirs is the kingdom of God, those who hunger for they will be filled, and those who weep for they will laugh. He pronounces woe when all speak well of you, for so did their fathers to the false prophets.
teachings.quote: Blessed be ye poor: for yours is the kingdom of God. Blessed are ye that hunger now: for ye shall be filled. Blessed are ye that weep now: for ye shall laugh. Woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you! for so did their fathers to the false prophets.
teachings.title: Blessings on the Poor and Warnings to the Proud

teachings.text: Jesus pronounces woe on the rich who have their consolation, the full who will hunger, and those who laugh now who will mourn and weep.
teachings.quote: But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation. Woe unto you that are full! for ye shall hunger. Woe unto you that laugh now! for ye shall mourn and weep.
teachings.title: Woe to the Rich Who Have Their Reward

subcategories.title: The Judgment of the Nations — Sheep and Goats

teachings.text: Jesus describes the Son of Man coming in glory and gathering all nations, separating them as a shepherd divides sheep from goats. The King welcomes those on his right to inherit the kingdom for feeding, clothing, and visiting him in the least of these, and sends those on the left into everlasting fire for failing to do so, the righteous going into life eternal.
teachings.quote: ¶ When the Son of man shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory: And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats: And he shall set the sheep on his right hand, but the goats on the left. Then shall the King say unto them on his right hand, Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me. Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee? or thirsty, and gave thee drink? When saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and clothed thee? Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee? And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me no meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me no drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me not in: naked, and ye clothed me not: sick, and in prison, and ye visited me not. Then shall they also answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, or athirst, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister unto thee? Then shall he answer them, saying, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye did it not to one of the least of these, ye did it not to me. And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal.
teachings.title: The Sheep and Goats: Final Judgment of Nations

teachings.text: Jesus declares that what is done for the least of these is done for him, and what is not done is withheld from him.
teachings.quote: And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me. Then shall he answer them, saying, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye did it not to one of the least of these, ye did it not to me.
teachings.title: Serving Christ in the Least of These

teachings.text: Jesus blesses the merciful, declaring that they will obtain mercy, and elsewhere says he desires mercy and not sacrifice.
teachings.quote: Blessed are the merciful: for they shall obtain mercy.
teachings.title: Blessed Are the Merciful

teachings.text: Jesus says he has compassion on the multitude after three days with nothing to eat, and will not send them away fasting lest they faint.
teachings.quote: I have compassion on the multitude, because they continue with me now three days, and have nothing to eat: and I will not send them away fasting, lest they faint in the way.
teachings.title: Compassion on the Hungry Multitude

teachings.text: Jesus asks the two blind men what they would have him do for them.
teachings.quote: What will ye that I shall do unto you?
teachings.title: What Would You Have Me Do?

teachings.text: Jesus pronounces woe on Pharisees who tithe herbs but neglect judgment and the love of God, saying these should be done without neglecting the others.
teachings.quote: But woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye tithe mint and rue and all manner of herbs, and pass over judgment and the love of God: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.
teachings.title: Justice and Mercy Cannot Be Neglected

teachings.text: Jesus sends the ten lepers to go and show themselves to the priests.
teachings.quote: Go shew yourselves unto the priests.
teachings.title: Ten Lepers Sent to the Priests

teachings.text: Jesus asks where the other nine are, noting that none returned to give glory to God except the one stranger, the Samaritan.
teachings.quote: Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine? There are not found that returned to give glory to God, save this stranger.
teachings.title: Only One Returned to Give Thanks

teachings.text: Jesus calls his first disciples to follow him, promising to make them fishers of men.
teachings.quote: Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
teachings.title: Follow Me and Become Fishers of Men

teachings.text: Jesus warns a would-be follower that the foxes have holes and the birds of the air have nests but the Son of man has nowhere to lay his head, and tells another to follow him and let the dead bury their dead.
teachings.quote: The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man hath not where to lay his head. Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.
teachings.title: No Place to Lay His Head

teachings.text: Jesus calls Matthew the tax collector from his tax booth with the words, follow me.
teachings.quote: Follow me.
teachings.title: Matthew Called from the Tax Booth

teachings.text: Jesus asks who is his mother and brothers, and pointing to his disciples says those who do his Father's will are his family.
teachings.quote: Who is my mother? and who are my brethren? Behold my mother and my brethren!
teachings.title: Those Who Do God's Will Are His Family

teachings.text: Jesus calls Levi from his tax booth with the words, follow me.
teachings.quote: Follow me.
teachings.title: Levi Called to Follow

teachings.text: Jesus calls the returning apostles to come away with him to a deserted place and rest a while.
teachings.quote: Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while:
teachings.title: Come Apart and Rest a While

teachings.text: Jesus tells Peter to launch out into the deep and let down his nets for a catch.
teachings.quote: Launch out into the deep, and let down your nets for a draught.
teachings.title: Launch Out into the Deep

teachings.text: Jesus tells Peter not to fear, for from now on he will catch men.
teachings.quote: Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.
teachings.title: Fear Not — You Will Catch Men

teachings.text: Jesus calls Levi the tax collector from his tax booth with the words, follow me.
teachings.quote: Follow me.
teachings.title: The Tax Collector Called to Follow

teachings.text: Jesus declares that no one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.
teachings.quote: No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.
teachings.title: No One Who Looks Back Is Fit for the Kingdom

teachings.text: Jesus tells the anxious Martha that she is worried and troubled about many things, but one thing is needful, and Mary has chosen that good part which will not be taken from her.
teachings.quote: Martha, Martha, thou art careful and troubled about many things: But one thing is needful: and Mary hath chosen that good part, which shall not be taken away from her.
teachings.title: Mary Has Chosen the Better Part

teachings.text: Jesus asks the first disciples what they seek and invites them to come and see where he dwells.
teachings.quote: What seek ye? Come and see.
teachings.title: Come and See Where Jesus Dwells

teachings.text: Jesus names Simon son of Jonah and declares that he will be called Cephas.
teachings.quote: Thou art Simon the son of Jona: thou shalt be called Cephas,
teachings.title: Simon Renamed Cephas

teachings.text: Jesus reminds the twelve that he has chosen them, and yet one of them is a devil.
teachings.quote: Have not I chosen you twelve, and one of you is a devil?
teachings.title: Chosen by Christ, Yet One Is a Devil

teachings.text: Jesus calls his disciples to go with him into Judea again.
teachings.quote: Let us go into Judæa again.
teachings.title: Called to Go Into Judea Again

teachings.text: Jesus tells Peter that where he goes he cannot follow him now, but he will follow him afterward.
teachings.quote: Whither I go, thou canst not follow me now; but thou shalt follow me afterwards.
teachings.title: You Cannot Follow Now But Will Later

teachings.text: Jesus three times asks Simon son of Jonah if he loves him, charging him to feed his lambs and feed his sheep. He foretells that when Peter is old another will gird him and carry him where he would not, and calls him to follow.
teachings.quote: Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? Feed my lambs... Feed my sheep. Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself... but when thou shalt be old... another shall gird thee... Follow me.
teachings.title: Feed My Sheep: Peter's Threefold Restoration

teachings.text: Jesus declares that if anyone will come after him, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow him.
teachings.quote: If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
teachings.title: Deny Yourself, Take Up Your Cross

teachings.text: Jesus says whoever will save his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for his sake will find it. He asks what a man is profited if he gains the whole world and loses his own soul.
teachings.quote: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it. For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?
teachings.title: Lose Your Life to Find It

teachings.text: Jesus declares that everyone who has forsaken houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or lands for his name's sake will receive a hundredfold and will inherit everlasting life.
teachings.quote: And every one that hath forsaken houses, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or lands, for my name’s sake, shall receive an hundredfold, and shall inherit everlasting life.
teachings.title: A Hundredfold Reward for Those Who Forsake All

teachings.text: Jesus asks why his hearers call him Lord, Lord, and do not do the things he says.
teachings.quote: ¶ And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?
teachings.title: Why Call Me Lord and Not Obey?

teachings.text: Jesus rebukes James and John, saying the Son of man came not to destroy lives but to save them.
teachings.quote: Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of. For the Son of man is not come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them.
teachings.title: The Son of Man Came to Save, Not Destroy

teachings.text: Jesus declares that whoever does not hate his own family and life, and forsake all he has, cannot be his disciple.
teachings.quote: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple. So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.
teachings.title: Count the Cost of Following Jesus

teachings.text: Jesus likens the would-be disciple to a man building a tower who first counts the cost, and to a king going to war who first weighs whether he can win or must sue for peace. Whoever does not forsake all cannot be his disciple.
teachings.quote: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it? Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him, Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish. Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand? Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace. So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.
teachings.title: The Tower Builder and King at War

teachings.text: Jesus asks the twelve whether they also will go away.
teachings.quote: Will ye also go away?
teachings.title: Will You Also Go Away?

teachings.text: Jesus declares that if his hearers continue in his word, then they are his disciples indeed.
teachings.quote: If ye continue in my word, then are ye my disciples indeed;
teachings.title: Continuing in His Word Proves True Discipleship

teachings.text: Jesus teaches that a good tree brings forth good fruit and a corrupt tree evil fruit. Every tree that does not bring forth good fruit is hewn down and cast into the fire, and by their fruits they will be known.
teachings.quote: Even so every good tree bringeth forth good fruit; but a corrupt tree bringeth forth evil fruit. A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit. Every tree that bringeth not forth good fruit is hewn down, and cast into the fire. Wherefore by their fruits ye shall know them.
teachings.title: Good Trees Bear Good Fruit

teachings.text: Jesus declares that whoever loves his life will lose it, and whoever hates his life in this world keeps it for life eternal. He prays that though his soul is troubled, the Father glorify his name, for this cause he came to this hour.
teachings.quote: He that loveth his life shall lose it; and he that hateth his life in this world shall keep it unto life eternal. If any man serve me, let him follow me; and where I am, there shall also my servant be: if any man serve me, him will my Father honour. Now is my soul troubled; and what shall I say? Father, save me from this hour: but for this cause came I unto this hour. Father, glorify thy name.
teachings.title: Hating Your Life in This World to Keep It

teachings.text: Jesus declares he is the vine and his hearers the branches. Whoever abides in him bears much fruit, for without him they can do nothing.
teachings.quote: I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing. Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; so shall ye be my disciples.
teachings.title: Abide in the Vine and Bear Much Fruit

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples he has chosen them to bear fruit that remains, and whatever they ask the Father in his name will be given.
teachings.quote: If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you. Ye have not chosen me, but I have chosen you, and ordained you, that ye should go and bring forth fruit, and that your fruit should remain: that whatsoever ye shall ask of the Father in my name, he may give it you.
teachings.title: Chosen to Bear Fruit That Remains

teachings.text: Jesus answers the tempter that man will not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God.
teachings.quote: It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
teachings.title: Man Shall Not Live by Bread Alone

teachings.text: Jesus answers the tempter, declaring it is written: you will not tempt the Lord your God.
teachings.quote: It is written again, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.
teachings.title: You Shall Not Tempt the Lord Your God

teachings.text: Jesus commands Satan to depart, declaring it is written: you will worship the Lord your God, and him only will you serve.
teachings.quote: Get thee hence, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
teachings.title: Worship God Alone — Satan Rebuked

teachings.text: Jesus answers in Luke's account that man will not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.
teachings.quote: It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.
teachings.title: Man Lives by Every Word of God

teachings.text: Jesus rebukes Satan, declaring it is written: you will worship the Lord your God, and him only will you serve.
teachings.quote: Get thee behind me, Satan: for it is written, Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only shalt thou serve.
teachings.title: Worship the Lord Your God Only

teachings.text: Jesus answers that it is said: you will not tempt the Lord your God.
teachings.quote: It is said, Thou shalt not tempt the Lord thy God.
teachings.title: Do Not Tempt the Lord

teachings.text: Jesus blesses those persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven, and calls his hearers blessed when men revile them falsely for his sake. He charges them to rejoice, for great is their reward, as they persecuted the prophets before them.
teachings.quote: Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven. Blessed are ye, when men shall revile you, and persecute you, and shall say all manner of evil against you falsely, for my sake. Rejoice, and be exceeding glad: for great is your reward in heaven: for so persecuted they the prophets which were before you.
teachings.title: Blessed Are the Persecuted — Rejoice and Be Glad

teachings.text: Jesus says a prophet is not without honor, except in his own country and in his own house.
teachings.quote: A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and in his own house.
teachings.title: A Prophet Without Honor in His Hometown

teachings.text: Jesus says a prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, among his own kin, and in his own house.
teachings.quote: A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.
teachings.title: No Honor Among His Own Kin

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples if the world hates them, it hated him first, for they are not of the world but chosen out of it.
teachings.quote: If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you. If ye were of the world, the world would love his own: but because ye are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you.
teachings.title: The World Hated Him First

teachings.text: Jesus charges the disciples to remember his word: the servant is not greater than his lord. If they have persecuted him they will also persecute them, and if they have kept his saying they will keep theirs also.
teachings.quote: Remember the word that I said unto you, The servant is not greater than his lord. If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you; if they have kept my saying, they will keep yours also.
teachings.title: The Servant Is Not Greater Than the Master

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples the world hates them because it does not know the Father. Had he not come and done such works, they had no sin; now they have seen and hated both, fulfilling the word: they hated me without a cause.
teachings.quote: But all these things will they do unto you for my name’s sake, because they know not him that sent me. If I had not come and spoken unto them, they had not had sin: but now they have no cloke for their sin. He that hateth me hateth my Father also. If I had not done among them the works which none other man did, they had not had sin: but now have they both seen and hated both me and my Father. But this cometh to pass, that the word might be fulfilled that is written in their law, They hated me without a cause.
teachings.title: They Hated Me Without a Cause

teachings.text: Jesus warns that they will put his disciples out of the synagogues, and the time comes when whoever kills them will think he serves God.
teachings.quote: They shall put you out of the synagogues: yea, the time cometh, that whosoever killeth you will think that he doeth God service.
teachings.title: The Hour Comes When Killing Seems Like Service

teachings.text: Jesus charges the disciples not to fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul, but rather to fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
teachings.quote: And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
teachings.title: Fear God, Not Those Who Kill the Body

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples he has spoken these things to them so they will not stumble.
teachings.quote: These things have I spoken unto you, that ye should not be offended.
teachings.title: These Things Spoken So You Will Not Stumble

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples the world acts so because it does not know the Father, and warns them now so they will remember. He kept silent before since he was with them; now he goes to him who sent him, and sorrow fills their heart.
teachings.quote: And these things will they do unto you, because they have not known the Father, nor me. But these things have I told you, that when the time shall come, ye may remember that I told you of them. And these things I said not unto you at the beginning, because I was with you. But now I go my way to him that sent me; and none of you asketh me, Whither goest thou? But because I have said these things unto you, sorrow hath filled your heart.
teachings.title: Sorrow Fills Your Heart Because I Go Away

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples they will weep while the world rejoices, but their sorrow will turn to joy as a woman forgets her travail for joy a child is born. He will see them again, and their joy no one will take from them.
teachings.quote: Do ye enquire among yourselves of that I said, A little while, and ye shall not see me: and again, a little while, and ye shall see me? Verily, verily, I say unto you, That ye shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice: and ye shall be sorrowful, but your sorrow shall be turned into joy. A woman when she is in travail hath sorrow, because her hour is come: but as soon as she is delivered of the child, she remembereth no more the anguish, for joy that a man is born into the world. And ye now therefore have sorrow: but I will see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and your joy no man taketh from you.
teachings.title: Sorrow Turned to Joy Like a Mother's Travail

teachings.text: Jesus declares the hour has come when they will scatter and leave him alone, yet he is not alone because the Father is with him.
teachings.quote: Do ye now believe? Behold, the hour cometh, yea, is now come, that ye shall be scattered, every man to his own, and shall leave me alone: and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
teachings.title: He Is Not Alone — the Father Is With Him

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples in him they have peace; in the world they will have tribulation, but take heart, for he has overcome the world.
teachings.quote: These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace. In the world ye shall have tribulation: but be of good cheer; I have overcome the world.
teachings.title: In Him Peace, in the World Tribulation

teachings.text: Jesus answers that his grace is sufficient for him, for his strength is made perfect in weakness.
teachings.quote: My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness.
teachings.title: My Grace Is Sufficient for You

teachings.text: Jesus says that if anyone will come after him, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow him, for whoever will save his life will lose it and whoever will lose his life for his sake will find it. He declares some standing there will not taste death till they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.
teachings.quote: If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me. For whosoever will save his life shall lose it: and whosoever will lose his life for my sake shall find it. Verily I say unto you, There be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the Son of man coming in his kingdom.
teachings.title: Take Up the Cross and Follow

teachings.text: Jesus asks what a man is profited if he gains the whole world and loses his own soul, or what a man will give in exchange for his soul.
teachings.quote: For what is a man profited, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?
teachings.title: What Profits a Man Who Gains the World?

subcategories.title: The Seven Woes to Scribes and Pharisees (Matthew 23)

teachings.text: Jesus pronounces woe upon the scribes and Pharisees who shut up the kingdom of heaven against men, neither entering themselves nor letting others in.
teachings.quote: ¶ But woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye shut up the kingdom of heaven against men: for ye neither go in yourselves, neither suffer ye them that are entering to go in.
teachings.title: Woe for Shutting the Kingdom of Heaven

teachings.text: Jesus pronounces woe upon the scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, for devouring widows' houses and for a pretence making long prayer, declaring that they will receive the greater damnation.
teachings.quote: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye devour widows’ houses, and for a pretence make long prayer: therefore ye shall receive the greater damnation.
teachings.title: Woe for Devouring Widows' Houses

teachings.text: Jesus pronounces woe upon the scribes and Pharisees who travel sea and land to make one convert, then make him twice the child of hell.
teachings.quote: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.
teachings.title: Woe for Making Converts Twice as Wicked

teachings.text: Jesus pronounces woe upon blind guides who swear by the temple's gold but not the temple. They tithe mint and dill yet neglect judgment, mercy, and faith. They strain at a gnat and swallow a camel.
teachings.quote: Woe unto you, ye blind guides, which say, Whosoever shall swear by the temple, it is nothing; but whosoever shall swear by the gold of the temple, he is a debtor! Ye fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gold, or the temple that sanctifieth the gold? And, Whosoever shall swear by the altar, it is nothing; but whosoever sweareth by the gift that is upon it, he is guilty. Ye fools and blind: for whether is greater, the gift, or the altar that sanctifieth the gift? Whoso therefore shall swear by the altar, sweareth by it, and by all things thereon. And whoso shall swear by the temple, sweareth by it, and by him that dwelleth therein. And he that shall swear by heaven, sweareth by the throne of God, and by him that sitteth thereon. Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone. Ye blind guides, which strain at a gnat, and swallow a camel.
teachings.title: Woe to Blind Guides Who Neglect Justice

teachings.text: Jesus pronounces woe upon the scribes and Pharisees who tithe mint and dill yet neglect judgment, mercy, and faith.
teachings.quote: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye pay tithe of mint and anise and cummin, and have omitted the weightier matters of the law, judgment, mercy, and faith: these ought ye to have done, and not to leave the other undone.
teachings.title: Woe for Tithing but Neglecting Mercy

teachings.text: Jesus pronounces woe upon the scribes and Pharisees who clean the outside of the cup but inside are full of greed, charging them to cleanse the inside first so the outside also may be clean.
teachings.quote: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye make clean the outside of the cup and of the platter, but within they are full of extortion and excess. Thou blind Pharisee, cleanse first that which is within the cup and platter, that the outside of them may be clean also.
teachings.title: Woe for Cleansing Only the Outside

teachings.text: Jesus pronounces woe upon the scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, likening them to whited sepulchres which appear beautiful outward but within are full of dead men's bones and all uncleanness, so that they outwardly appear righteous unto men while within being full of hypocrisy and iniquity.
teachings.quote: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye are like unto whited sepulchres, which indeed appear beautiful outward, but are within full of dead men’s bones, and of all uncleanness. Even so ye also outwardly appear righteous unto men, but within ye are full of hypocrisy and iniquity.
teachings.title: Woe for Outward Piety and Inner Corruption

teachings.text: Jesus pronounces woe upon the scribes and Pharisees who build the prophets' tombs while saying they would not have shared in their fathers' bloodshed, calling them children of those who killed the prophets and asking how they can escape hell.
teachings.quote: Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because ye build the tombs of the prophets, and garnish the sepulchres of the righteous, And say, If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partakers with them in the blood of the prophets. Wherefore ye be witnesses unto yourselves, that ye are the children of them which killed the prophets. Fill ye up then the measure of your fathers. Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?
teachings.title: Woe for Honoring Prophets You Would Have Killed

teachings.text: Jesus pronounces woe upon the Pharisees, for they love the uppermost seats in the synagogues and greetings in the markets.
teachings.quote: Woe unto you, Pharisees! for ye love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and greetings in the markets.
teachings.title: Woe for Loving the Seats of Honor

teachings.text: Jesus pronounces woe upon the lawyers who load men with grievous burdens yet will not lift them with one finger.
teachings.quote: Woe unto you also, ye lawyers! for ye lade men with burdens grievous to be borne, and ye yourselves touch not the burdens with one of your fingers.
teachings.title: Woe to Lawyers Who Burden Others

teachings.text: Jesus declares that this generation will be held to account for the blood of all the prophets from Abel to Zacharias, and pronounces woe upon the lawyers who have taken away the key of knowledge.
teachings.quote: Therefore also said the wisdom of God, I will send them prophets and apostles, and some of them they shall slay and persecute: That the blood of all the prophets, which was shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation; From the blood of Abel unto the blood of Zacharias, which perished between the altar and the temple: verily I say unto you, It shall be required of this generation. Woe unto you, lawyers! for ye have taken away the key of knowledge: ye entered not in yourselves, and them that were entering in ye hindered.
teachings.title: Woe — This Generation Accountable for the Prophets

teachings.text: Jesus likens this generation to children in the markets who would neither dance nor mourn, for John came neither eating nor drinking and they called him possessed, and the Son of Man comes eating and drinking and they call him a glutton.
teachings.quote: ¶ But whereunto shall I liken this generation? It is like unto children sitting in the markets, and calling unto their fellows, And saying, We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned unto you, and ye have not lamented. For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, He hath a devil. The Son of man came eating and drinking, and they say, Behold a man gluttonous, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified of her children.
teachings.title: This Generation Rejects Both John and the Son

teachings.text: Jesus declares that an evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and that none will be given but the sign of the prophet Jonah.
teachings.quote: An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas:
teachings.title: No Sign Given Except the Sign of Jonah

teachings.text: Jesus says of the people that they draw near to him with their mouth and honor him with their lips while their heart is far from him, and that in vain they worship him, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.
teachings.quote: This people draweth nigh unto me with their mouth, and honoureth me with their lips; but their heart is far from me. But in vain they do worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.
teachings.title: Lips Near but Heart Far from God

teachings.text: Jesus teaches that what enters the mouth does not defile a man, but what comes from the heart defiles him: evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, thefts, false witness, and blasphemies.
teachings.quote: Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man. But those things which proceed out of the mouth come forth from the heart; and they defile the man. For out of the heart proceed evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, blasphemies:
teachings.title: What Comes from the Heart Defiles a Man

teachings.text: Jesus declares that a wicked and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and none will be given but the sign of the prophet Jonah.
teachings.quote: A wicked and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign; and there shall no sign be given unto it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas.
teachings.title: An Adulterous Generation Demands a Sign

teachings.text: Jesus speaks to the fruitless fig tree, charging that no fruit grow on it henceforward for ever.
teachings.quote: Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever.
teachings.title: The Fruitless Fig Tree Cursed

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Syrophoenician woman the children must first be filled — it is not right to give their bread to the dogs.
teachings.quote: Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it unto the dogs.
teachings.title: Children's Bread Not Given to the Dogs

teachings.text: Jesus tells of a Pharisee who boasts to God of his fasts and tithes and a publican who beats his breast pleading mercy. He declares the publican goes home justified — whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
teachings.quote: Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican. The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican. I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess. And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner. I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
teachings.title: The Pharisee and the Tax Collector

subcategories.title: Traditions of Men Versus God's Commands

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Pharisees that they have made the commandment of God of none effect by their tradition, calling them hypocrites of whom Esaias well prophesied.
teachings.quote: And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free. Thus have ye made the commandment of God of none effect by your tradition. Ye hypocrites, well did Esaias prophesy of you, saying,
teachings.title: Human Tradition Makes God's Commandment Void

teachings.text: Jesus charges the Pharisees with setting aside the commandment of God to keep the tradition of men, such as the washing of pots and cups.
teachings.quote: For laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men, as the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things ye do.
teachings.title: Setting Aside God's Word for Men's Traditions

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Pharisees they reject God's commandment to keep their own tradition: Moses commanded honoring father and mother, but they say a son who declares his support Corban is freed from helping them, making the word of God void.
teachings.quote: Full well ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your own tradition. For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death: But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free. And ye suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother; Making the word of God of none effect through your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things do ye.
teachings.title: Corban: Tradition Used to Dishonor Parents

teachings.text: Jesus calls the multitude to hearken to him every one and to understand.
teachings.quote: Hearken unto me every one of you, and understand:
teachings.title: Called to Hear and Understand

teachings.text: Jesus explains to the disciples that whatever enters from outside cannot defile, for it goes to the belly and out, but what comes from within — that defiles the man.
teachings.quote: Are ye so without understanding also? Do ye not perceive, that whatsoever thing from without entereth into the man, it cannot defile him; Because it entereth not into his heart, but into the belly, and goeth out into the draught, purging all meats? That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man.
teachings.title: External Things Cannot Defile — What Comes Out Does

teachings.text: Jesus declares that all these evil things come from within and defile the man.
teachings.quote: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.
teachings.title: Evil Things from Within Defile the Man

teachings.text: Jesus asks what man among them would not lift his sheep from a pit on the sabbath, and reasons that since a man is much better than a sheep, it is lawful to do good on the sabbath.
teachings.quote: What man shall there be among you, that shall have one sheep, and if it fall into a pit on the sabbath day, will he not lay hold on it, and lift it out? How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.
teachings.title: Is It Lawful to Do Good on the Sabbath?

teachings.text: Jesus declares that the sabbath was made for man and not man for the sabbath, and that therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
teachings.quote: The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
teachings.title: The Sabbath Was Made for Man

teachings.text: Jesus asks the Pharisees whether they have not read what David did when he was hungry, eating the showbread which was lawful only for priests.
teachings.quote: Have ye not read so much as this, what David did, when himself was an hungred, and they which were with him; How he went into the house of God, and did take and eat the shewbread, and gave also to them that were with him; which it is not lawful to eat but for the priests alone?
teachings.title: David Ate the Showbread on the Sabbath

teachings.text: Jesus calls the man with the withered hand to stand forth and asks whether it is lawful on the sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it.
teachings.quote: Rise up, and stand forth in the midst. I will ask you one thing; Is it lawful on the sabbath days to do good, or to do evil? to save life, or to destroy it? Stretch forth thy hand.
teachings.title: Do Good or Do Evil on the Sabbath?

teachings.text: Jesus says to the bent-over woman in the synagogue, Woman, you are loosed from yours infirmity.
teachings.quote: Woman, thou art loosed from thine infirmity.
teachings.title: Woman, You Are Loosed from Your Infirmity

teachings.text: Jesus calls the synagogue ruler a hypocrite, asking does not each untie his ox on the sabbath to lead him to water.
teachings.quote: Thou hypocrite, doth not each one of you on the sabbath loose his ox or his ass from the stall, and lead him away to watering?
teachings.title: Hypocrites Water Their Cattle on the Sabbath

teachings.text: Jesus asks the lawyers and Pharisees whether it is lawful to heal on the sabbath day.
teachings.quote: Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day?
teachings.title: Is It Lawful to Heal on the Sabbath?

teachings.text: Jesus reasons that since Moses gave them circumcision and they circumcise on the sabbath so the law not be broken, they should not be angry that he has made a man whole on the sabbath.
teachings.quote: I have done one work, and ye all marvel. Moses therefore gave unto you circumcision; (not because it is of Moses, but of the fathers;) and ye on the sabbath day circumcise a man. If a man on the sabbath day receive circumcision, that the law of Moses should not be broken; are ye angry at me, because I have made a man every whit whole on the sabbath day?
teachings.title: Circumcision on the Sabbath — Why Not Healing?

teachings.text: Jesus warns that every plant which his heavenly Father has not planted will be rooted up.
teachings.quote: Every plant, which my heavenly Father hath not planted, shall be rooted up.
teachings.title: Every Plant Not of God Will Be Uprooted

teachings.text: Jesus concludes that these are the things which defile a man, but to eat with unwashen hands defiles not a man.
teachings.quote: These are the things which defile a man: but to eat with unwashen hands defileth not a man.
teachings.title: Eating with Unwashed Hands Does Not Defile

teachings.text: Jesus cleanses the temple by driving out merchants and money changers, declaring that his Father’s house is not to be a house of merchandise or a den of thieves, but shall be a house of prayer.
teachings.quote: It is written, My house shall be called the house of prayer; but ye have made it a den of thieves.
teachings.title: Cleansing the Temple — My House Shall Be a House of Prayer

teachings.text: Jesus says the scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses' seat, charging his hearers to do whatever they bid but not to follow their works, for they bind heavy burdens on others' shoulders that they themselves will not lift.
teachings.quote: The scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses’ seat: All therefore whatsoever they bid you observe, that observe and do; but do not ye after their works: for they say, and do not. For they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne, and lay them on men’s shoulders; but they themselves will not move them with one of their fingers.
teachings.title: Pharisees Bind Burdens They Will Not Lift

teachings.text: Jesus says the scribes and Pharisees do their works to be seen, loving the chief seats in synagogues, greetings in markets, and the title Rabbi, and charges his disciples not to be called Rabbi, for one is their Master.
teachings.quote: But all their works they do for to be seen of men: they make broad their phylacteries, and enlarge the borders of their garments, And love the uppermost rooms at feasts, and the chief seats in the synagogues, And greetings in the markets, and to be called of men, Rabbi, Rabbi. But be not ye called Rabbi: for one is your Master, even Christ; and all ye are brethren.
