Neither be ye called masters: for one is your Master, even Christ. ¶ Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify; and some of them shall ye scourge in your synagogues, and persecute them from city to city: That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar. Verily I say unto you, All these things shall come upon this generation. O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not! Behold, your house is left unto you desolate. For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.
teachings.title: Leaders Who Love Titles and Chief Seats

teachings.text: Jesus declares he sends prophets, of whom they will kill and persecute, so all righteous blood from Abel to Zacharias will come upon this generation; he laments how often he would have gathered Jerusalem's children as a hen gathers her brood, but they would not.
teachings.quote: Wherefore, behold, I send unto you prophets, and wise men, and scribes: and some of them ye shall kill and crucify... O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!
teachings.title: Prophets Sent and Killed — Jerusalem's Lament

teachings.text: Jesus speaks to the unfruitful fig tree, charging that no man eat fruit of it from now on for ever.
teachings.quote: No man eat fruit of thee hereafter for ever.
teachings.title: The Barren Fig Tree Cursed Forever

teachings.text: Jesus answers the chief priests with a question of his own: was John's baptism from heaven or from men?
teachings.quote: I will also ask of you one question, and answer me, and I will tell you by what authority I do these things. The baptism of John, was it from heaven, or of men? answer me.
teachings.title: Was John's Baptism from Heaven or Men?

teachings.text: Jesus tells the chief priests, neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
teachings.quote: Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
teachings.title: I Will Not Tell You My Authority

teachings.text: Jesus tells the Pharisees they justify themselves before men, but God knows their hearts, for what men esteem highly is abomination before God.
teachings.quote: Ye are they which justify yourselves before men; but God knoweth your hearts: for that which is highly esteemed among men is abomination in the sight of God.
teachings.title: Men Esteem What God Counts Abomination

teachings.text: Jesus tells the leaders he receives no honor from men but knows they have not the love of God in them, for they receive him not though he comes in his Father's name; he declares that Moses, in whom they trust, accuses them.
teachings.quote: I receive not honour from men. But I know you, that ye have not the love of God in you. I am come in my Father’s name, and ye receive me not: if another shall come in his own name, him ye will receive. How can ye believe, which receive honour one of another, and seek not the honour that cometh from God only? Do not think that I will accuse you to the Father: there is one that accuseth you, even Moses, in whom ye trust.
teachings.title: They Do Not Have the Love of God

teachings.text: Jesus tells the religious leaders that though they are Abraham's seed, they seek to kill him because his word has no place in them, and that they do the deeds of their father the devil — a murderer from the beginning, the father of lies; because Jesus tells them the truth they do not believe him, for he that is of God hears God's words.
teachings.quote: I know that ye are Abraham’s seed; but ye seek to kill me, because my word hath no place in you. I speak that which I have seen with my Father: and ye do that which ye have seen with your father. If ye were Abraham’s children, ye would do the works of Abraham. But now ye seek to kill me, a man that hath told you the truth, which I have heard of God: this did not Abraham. Ye do the deeds of your father. If God were your Father, ye would love me: for I proceeded forth and came from God; neither came I of myself, but he sent me. Why do ye not understand my speech? even because ye cannot hear my word. Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and abode not in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it. And because I tell you the truth, ye believe me not. Which of you convinceth me of sin? And if I say the truth, why do ye not believe me? He that is of God heareth God’s words: ye therefore hear them not, because ye are not of God.
teachings.title: Children of the Devil Who Reject the Truth

teachings.text: Jesus tells Peter that on this rock he will build his church and the gates of hell will not prevail. He gives him the keys of the kingdom of heaven — whatever he binds or looses on earth is bound or loosed in heaven.
teachings.quote: And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.
teachings.title: On This Rock I Will Build My Church

teachings.text: Jesus grants the disciples authority to bind and loose: whatever they bind or loose on earth will be bound or loosed in heaven.
teachings.quote: And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.
teachings.title: Authority to Bind and Loose on Earth

teachings.text: Jesus says where two or three gather in his name he is among them, and what two agree to ask his Father will do.
teachings.quote: Again I say unto you, That if two of you shall agree on earth as touching any thing that they shall ask, it shall be done for them of my Father which is in heaven. For where two or three are gathered together in my name, there am I in the midst of them.
teachings.title: Where Two or Three Gather in My Name

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples not to forbid the unknown man working a miracle in his name, for no one who does so can lightly speak evil of him, and whoever is not against them is for them.
teachings.quote: Forbid him not: for there is no man which shall do a miracle in my name, that can lightly speak evil of me. For he that is not against us is on our part.
teachings.title: Whoever Is Not Against Us Is for Us

teachings.text: Jesus declares all power in heaven and earth has been given him, charges the eleven to make disciples of all nations, baptizing in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and promises he is with them to the end of the world.
teachings.quote: All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth. ¶ Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world.
teachings.title: Go and Make Disciples of All Nations

teachings.text: Jesus tells the apostles they will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon them, and be his witnesses to the ends of the earth.
teachings.quote: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.
teachings.title: You Will Receive Power to Be My Witnesses

subcategories.title: Instructions for the Twelve and the Seventy

teachings.text: Jesus charges the twelve to go to the lost sheep of Israel, taking neither gold nor extra clothing for the worker is worthy of his wages, lodging where they are received and shaking off the dust where they are not, warning them of councils and synagogues; whoever loses his life for his sake will find it, and whoever receives them receives him.
teachings.quote: Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not: But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel. Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass in your purses, Nor scrip for your journey, neither two coats, neither shoes, nor yet staves: for the workman is worthy of his meat. And into whatsoever city or town ye shall enter, enquire who in it is worthy; and there abide till ye go thence. And when ye come into an house, salute it. And if the house be worthy, let your peace come upon it: but if it be not worthy, let your peace return to you. And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet. But beware of men: for they will deliver you up to the councils, and they will scourge you in their synagogues; It is enough for the disciple that he be as his master, and the servant as his lord. If they have called the master of the house Beelzebub, how much more shall they call them of his household? He that findeth his life shall lose it: and he that loseth his life for my sake shall find it. ¶ He that receiveth you receiveth me, and he that receiveth me receiveth him that sent me. He that receiveth a prophet in the name of a prophet shall receive a prophet’s reward; and he that receiveth a righteous man in the name of a righteous man shall receive a righteous man’s reward. And whosoever shall give to drink unto one of these little ones a cup of cold water only in the name of a disciple, verily I say unto you, he shall in no wise lose his reward.
teachings.title: Instructions for the Mission to Israel

teachings.text: Jesus sends the twelve forth to preach that the kingdom of heaven is at hand, to heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, and cast out devils, charging them that as they have freely received they will freely give.
teachings.quote: And as ye go, preach, saying, The kingdom of heaven is at hand. Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely ye have received, freely give.
teachings.title: Preach the Kingdom, Heal the Sick

teachings.text: Jesus tells the twelve he sends them as sheep among wolves, and charges them therefore to be wise as serpents and harmless as doves.
teachings.quote: ¶ Behold, I send you forth as sheep in the midst of wolves: be ye therefore wise as serpents, and harmless as doves.
teachings.title: Wise as Serpents, Harmless as Doves

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples they must go to the next towns so he may preach there also, for that is why he came forth.
teachings.quote: Let us go into the next towns, that I may preach there also: for therefore came I forth.
teachings.title: Preach the Kingdom in Every Town

teachings.text: Jesus tells the returning seventy he beheld Satan fall as lightning from heaven, and gives them power to tread on serpents and over the enemy, charging them not to rejoice that the spirits are subject but that their names are written in heaven.
teachings.quote: I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven. Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you. Notwithstanding in this rejoice not, that the spirits are subject unto you; but rather rejoice, because your names are written in heaven. I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes: even so, Father; for so it seemed good in thy sight.
teachings.title: Satan Falls — Power Over the Enemy Given

subcategories.title: Visions and Commissions to the Apostles

teachings.text: Jesus calls out to Saul on the Damascus road, asking why he persecutes him and declaring himself to be Jesus whom Saul persecutes, and tells him it is hard to kick against the pricks and to arise and go into the city where he will be told what he must do.
teachings.quote: Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me? I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks. Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do.
teachings.title: Saul, Why Do You Persecute Me?

teachings.text: Jesus calls Ananias in a vision and sends him to lay hands on Saul of Tarsus, declaring Saul is a chosen vessel to bear his name before Gentiles, kings, and Israel, and that he will show him how much he must suffer for his name.
teachings.quote: Ananias. Arise, and go into the street which is called Straight, and enquire in the house of Judas for one called Saul, of Tarsus: for, behold, he prayeth, And hath seen in a vision a man named Ananias coming in, and putting his hand on him, that he might receive his sight. Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel: For I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name’s sake.
teachings.title: Saul Chosen to Carry the Name to Nations

teachings.text: Jesus tells Peter in a vision to rise, kill, and eat from the creatures let down before him, and when Peter refuses what is common or unclean, declares that what God has cleansed Peter must not call common.
teachings.title: What God Has Cleansed Do Not Call Common

teachings.text: Jesus tells Paul in a vision at Corinth not to fear but to speak, for he is with him and has people in that city.
teachings.quote: Be not afraid, but speak, and hold not thy peace: For I am with thee, and no man shall set on thee to hurt thee: for I have much people in this city.
teachings.title: Do Not Fear — I Have People in This City

teachings.text: Jesus tells Paul in a trance at the temple to make haste and depart quickly from Jerusalem, for they will not receive his testimony concerning him, and declares that he will send him far hence to the Gentiles.
teachings.quote: Make haste, and get thee quickly out of Jerusalem: for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me. Depart: for I will send thee far hence unto the Gentiles.
teachings.title: Depart Quickly — Go Far to the Gentiles

teachings.text: Jesus stands by Paul and bids him be of good cheer, for as he has testified in Jerusalem so must he also testify at Rome.
teachings.quote: Be of good cheer, Paul: for as thou hast testified of me in Jerusalem, so must thou bear witness also at Rome.
teachings.title: As You Have Testified Here, So Also at Rome

teachings.text: Jesus says that the harvest truly is plenteous but the labourers are few, and charges his disciples to pray the Lord of the harvest to send forth labourers into his harvest.
teachings.quote: The harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few; Pray ye therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he will send forth labourers into his harvest.
teachings.title: The Harvest Is Plentiful, Workers Are Few

teachings.text: Jesus declares in the Nazareth synagogue that no prophet is accepted in his own country, recalling that in Elijah's time he was sent to a widow in Sidon and in Elisha's time only Naaman the Syrian was cleansed.
teachings.quote: Ye will surely say unto me this proverb, Physician, heal thyself: whatsoever we have heard done in Capernaum, do also here in thy country. Verily I say unto you, No prophet is accepted in his own country. But I tell you of a truth, many widows were in Israel in the days of Elias, when the heaven was shut up three years and six months, when great famine was throughout all the land; But unto none of them was Elias sent, save unto Sarepta, a city of Sidon, unto a woman that was a widow. And many lepers were in Israel in the time of Eliseus the prophet; and none of them was cleansed, saving Naaman the Syrian.
teachings.title: No Prophet Accepted in His Own Country

teachings.text: Jesus tells the crowd at Capernaum that he must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also, for to that end he was sent.
teachings.quote: I must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also: for therefore am I sent.
teachings.title: I Must Preach the Kingdom to Other Cities

teachings.text: Jesus likens this generation to children who neither danced nor wept: John came neither eating nor drinking and they said he had a devil, and the Son of Man comes eating and drinking and they call him a glutton.
teachings.quote: Whereunto then shall I liken the men of this generation? and to what are they like? They are like unto children sitting in the marketplace, and calling one to another, and saying, We have piped unto you, and ye have not danced; we have mourned to you, and ye have not wept. For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine; and ye say, He hath a devil. The Son of man is come eating and drinking; and ye say, Behold a gluttonous man, and a winebibber, a friend of publicans and sinners! But wisdom is justified of all her children.
teachings.title: A Generation That Rejects John and the Son

teachings.text: Jesus sends the healed Gerasene demoniac back to his own house to show how great things God has done for him.
teachings.quote: Return to thine own house, and shew how great things God hath done unto thee.
teachings.title: Tell What Great Things God Has Done

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples his food is to do the will of him who sent him, bidding them look on the fields white for harvest, where reaper and sower rejoice together, for he sent them to reap what others have labored.
teachings.quote: My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work. Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest. And he that reapeth receiveth wages, and gathereth fruit unto life eternal: that both he that soweth and he that reapeth may rejoice together. And herein is that saying true, One soweth, and another reapeth. I sent you to reap that whereon ye bestowed no labour: other men laboured, and ye are entered into their labours.
teachings.title: The Fields Are White for Harvest

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples that they also will bear witness, because they have been with him from the beginning.
teachings.quote: And ye also shall bear witness, because ye have been with me from the beginning.
teachings.title: You Also Bear Witness — You Were There

teachings.text: Jesus charges the disciples to preach on the housetops what they hear in the ear, and to fear not those who kill the body but him who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
teachings.quote: What I tell you in darkness, that speak ye in light: and what ye hear in the ear, that preach ye upon the housetops. And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
teachings.title: Proclaim from the Rooftops Without Fear

teachings.text: Jesus declares that whoever confesses him before men, he will also confess before his Father in heaven, but whoever denies him before men, he will also deny before his Father in heaven.
teachings.quote: Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven. But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.
teachings.title: Confess Me Before Men and I Will Confess You

teachings.text: Jesus warns the disciples that they will be brought before governors and kings for his sake as a testimony against them and the Gentiles.
teachings.quote: And ye shall be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony against them and the Gentiles.
teachings.title: Brought Before Kings as a Testimony

teachings.text: Jesus warns that brother will betray brother, parents will be put to death by their children, and his disciples will be hated by all for his name's sake — but he that endures to the end will be saved.
teachings.quote: And the brother shall deliver up the brother to death, and the father the child: and the children shall rise up against their parents, and cause them to be put to death. And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.
teachings.title: Hated by All, But Endure to the End

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples that not a hair of their head will perish, and that in their patience they will possess their souls.
teachings.quote: But there shall not an hair of your head perish. In your patience possess ye your souls.
teachings.title: Not a Hair of Your Head Will Perish

categories.title: The Passion Narrative
categories.description: The words of Jesus during his final hours — the Last Supper, Gethsemane, his trial, and crucifixion.

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples that after two days is the feast of the passover, and the Son of man is betrayed to be crucified.
teachings.quote: Ye know that after two days is the feast of the passover, and the Son of man is betrayed to be crucified.
teachings.title: After Two Days the Son of Man Is Betrayed

teachings.text: Jesus defends the woman who poured ointment on him, saying she has wrought a good work upon him for his burial, and declares that wherever this gospel is preached in the whole world what she has done will be told for a memorial of her.
teachings.quote: Why trouble ye the woman? for she hath wrought a good work upon me. For ye have the poor always with you; but me ye have not always. For in that she hath poured this ointment on my body, she did it for my burial. Verily I say unto you, Wheresoever this gospel shall be preached in the whole world, there shall also this, that this woman hath done, be told for a memorial of her.
teachings.title: She Has Done a Good Work for My Burial

teachings.text: Jesus sends his disciples into the city to a certain man with the message that the Master's time is at hand and he will keep the passover at his house with his disciples.
teachings.quote: Go into the city to such a man, and say unto him, The Master saith, My time is at hand; I will keep the passover at thy house with my disciples.
teachings.title: Preparing the Passover for the Master

teachings.text: Jesus declares to the Twelve at table that one of them will betray him.
teachings.quote: Verily I say unto you, that one of you shall betray me.
teachings.title: One of You Will Betray Me

teachings.text: Jesus says the one who dips his hand with him will betray him; the Son of Man goes as it is written, but woe to that man — it would have been good for him not to have been born.
teachings.quote: He that dippeth his hand with me in the dish, the same shall betray me. The Son of man goeth as it is written of him: but woe unto that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! it had been good for that man if he had not been born. Thou hast said.
teachings.title: Woe to the Man Who Betrays the Son of Man

teachings.text: Jesus takes the bread and cup at the supper, telling the disciples to take and eat for this is his body, and to drink for this is his blood of the new testament shed for many for the remission of sins, and declares he will not drink of the vine again until that day in his Father's kingdom.
teachings.quote: Take, eat; this is my body. Drink ye all of it; For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins. But I say unto you, I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.
teachings.title: This Is My Body and Blood of the New Covenant

teachings.text: Jesus institutes the Lord's Supper, bidding the disciples to take and eat his body and to drink of the cup which is his blood of the new testament shed for many for the remission of sins, and pledges he will not drink of the fruit of the vine again until that day when he drinks it new with them in his Father's kingdom.
teachings.quote: Take, eat; this is my body. Drink ye all of it; For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins. But I say unto you, I will not drink henceforth of this fruit of the vine, until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.
teachings.title: The Lord's Supper Instituted

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples that all of them will be offended because of him this night — the shepherd will be smitten and the sheep scattered — but pledges that after he is risen he will go before them into Galilee.
teachings.quote: All ye shall be offended because of me this night: for it is written, I will smite the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered abroad. But after I am risen again, I will go before you into Galilee.
teachings.title: All Will Fall Away — But I Go Before You

teachings.text: Jesus tells Peter that this very night, before the cock crows, he will deny him three times.
teachings.quote: Verily I say unto thee, That this night, before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.
teachings.title: Before the Cock Crows You Will Deny Me

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples he has longed to eat this Passover before he suffers, and will not eat it again until God's kingdom comes.
teachings.quote: With desire I have desired to eat this passover with you before I suffer: For I say unto you, I will not any more eat thereof, until it be fulfilled in the kingdom of God.
teachings.title: He Longed to Eat This Passover Before Suffering

teachings.text: Jesus charges his disciples that the greatest among them must be as the youngest and the leader as one who serves.
teachings.quote: And he said unto them, The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and they that exercise authority upon them are called benefactors. But ye shall not be so: but he that is greatest among you, let him be as the younger; and he that is chief, as he that doth serve.
teachings.title: The Greatest Must Serve Like the Youngest

teachings.text: Jesus asks which is greater, he who sits at table or he who serves, and declares he is among them as one who serves.
teachings.quote: For whether is greater, he that sitteth at meat, or he that serveth? is not he that sitteth at meat? but I am among you as he that serveth.
teachings.title: I Am Among You as One Who Serves

teachings.text: Jesus commends his disciples for continuing with him in his trials and appoints them a kingdom to eat at his table and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes; he warns Peter Satan has desired to sift him, but has prayed for him.
teachings.quote: Ye are they which have continued with me in my temptations. And I appoint unto you a kingdom, as my Father hath appointed unto me; That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel. And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren.
teachings.title: Peter, Satan Has Asked to Sift You

teachings.text: Jesus bids the disciples to watch with him, telling them his soul is exceeding sorrowful unto death, and prays that if possible the cup might pass yet not as he wills but the Father's; he rebukes them for not watching one hour, charging them to pray that they enter not into temptation, and at last tells them the hour is at hand.
teachings.quote: Sit ye here, while I go and pray yonder. My soul is exceeding sorrowful, even unto death: tarry ye here, and watch with me. O my Father, if it be possible, let this cup pass from me: nevertheless not as I will, but as thou wilt. What, could ye not watch with me one hour? Watch and pray, that ye enter not into temptation: the spirit indeed is willing, but the flesh is weak. O my Father, if this cup may not pass away from me, except I drink it, thy will be done. Sleep on now, and take your rest: behold, the hour is at hand, and the Son of man is betrayed into the hands of sinners. Rise, let us be going: behold, he is at hand that doth betray me.
teachings.title: Gethsemane: Not My Will but Yours

teachings.text: Jesus greets Judas at the betrayal, asking, Friend, wherefore art you come?
teachings.quote: Friend, wherefore art thou come?
teachings.title: Friend, Why Have You Come?

teachings.text: Jesus charges Peter to put up his sword, for all who take the sword will perish; he could pray for twelve legions of angels but asks how then the scriptures should be fulfilled, and asks the arresting party why they come as against a thief.
teachings.quote: Put up again thy sword into his place: for all they that take the sword shall perish with the sword. Thinkest thou that I cannot now pray to my Father, and he shall presently give me more than twelve legions of angels? But how then shall the scriptures be fulfilled, that thus it must be? Are ye come out as against a thief with swords and staves for to take me? I sat daily with you teaching in the temple, and ye laid no hold on me. But all this was done, that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.
teachings.title: Put Up Your Sword — Scripture Must Be Fulfilled

teachings.text: Jesus asks the arresting party whether they have come out as against a thief with swords and staves to take him, noting that he was daily with them in the temple teaching and they took him not, but the scriptures must be fulfilled.
teachings.quote: Are ye come out, as against a thief, with swords and with staves to take me? I was daily with you in the temple teaching, and ye took me not: but the scriptures must be fulfilled.
teachings.title: You Come as Against a Thief in the Night

teachings.text: Jesus asks Judas whether he betrays the Son of man with a kiss.
teachings.quote: Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?
teachings.title: Judas, Do You Betray Me with a Kiss?

teachings.text: Jesus goes forth to those who came to arrest him and asks, Whom seek you?
teachings.quote: Whom seek ye?
teachings.title: Whom Do You Seek?

teachings.text: Jesus declares I am he to those who came to arrest him, asks again whom they seek, and tells them that since he has said he is the one, they should let his disciples go their way.
teachings.quote: I am he. Whom seek ye? I have told you that I am he: if therefore ye seek me, let these go their way:
teachings.title: I Am He — Let My Disciples Go Free

teachings.text: Jesus answers the high priest, you have said, and declares that from now on they will see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power and coming in the clouds of heaven.
teachings.quote: Thou hast said: nevertheless I say unto you, Hereafter shall ye see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.
teachings.title: The Son of Man Coming on the Clouds of Heaven

teachings.text: Jesus answers Pilate's question whether he is the King of the Jews with the words, you sayest.
teachings.quote: Thou sayest.
teachings.title: You Sayest — Jesus Before Pilate

teachings.text: Jesus tells the daughters of Jerusalem not to weep for him but for themselves and their children, for the days are coming when the barren will be called blessed and men will say to the mountains, fall on us.
teachings.quote: Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me, but weep for yourselves, and for your children. For, behold, the days are coming, in the which they shall say, Blessed are the barren, and the wombs that never bare, and the paps which never gave suck. Then shall they begin to say to the mountains, Fall on us; and to the hills, Cover us. For if they do these things in a green tree, what shall be done in the dry?
teachings.title: Weep Not for Me but for Yourselves

teachings.text: Jesus tells the high priest he spoke openly in the synagogue and temple, said nothing in secret, and asks why he is questioned.
teachings.quote: I spake openly to the world; I ever taught in the synagogue, and in the temple, whither the Jews always resort; and in secret have I said nothing. Why askest thou me? ask them which heard me, what I have said unto them: behold, they know what I said.
teachings.title: I Spoke Openly in the Temple

teachings.text: Jesus answers the officer who struck him: if he has spoken evil, bear witness of it; but if well, why is he smitten?
teachings.quote: If I have spoken evil, bear witness of the evil: but if well, why smitest thou me?
teachings.title: If I Spoke Evil, Bear Witness of It

teachings.text: Jesus asks Pilate whether he says this thing of himself or whether others have told it him concerning Jesus.
teachings.quote: Sayest thou this thing of thyself, or did others tell it thee of me?
teachings.title: Do You Ask This of Yourself or Were You Told?

teachings.text: Jesus tells Pilate his kingdom is not of this world; if it were, his servants would fight that he should not be delivered.
teachings.quote: My kingdom is not of this world: if my kingdom were of this world, then would my servants fight, that I should not be delivered to the Jews: but now is my kingdom not from hence.
teachings.title: My Kingdom Is Not of This World

teachings.text: Jesus tells Pilate he came into the world to bear witness to the truth, and everyone who is of the truth hears his voice.
teachings.quote: Thou sayest that I am a king. To this end was I born, and for this cause came I into the world, that I should bear witness unto the truth. Every one that is of the truth heareth my voice.
teachings.title: I Came to Bear Witness to the Truth

teachings.text: Jesus tells Pilate he could have no power against him unless given from above, and therefore the one who delivered him has the greater sin.
teachings.quote: Thou couldest have no power at all against me, except it were given thee from above: therefore he that delivered me unto thee hath the greater sin.
teachings.title: No Power Unless Given from Above

teachings.text: At the ninth hour Jesus cries out with a loud voice, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani — My God, my God, why hast you forsaken me?
teachings.quote: Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani?
teachings.title: My God, Why Have You Forsaken Me?

teachings.text: From the cross Jesus prays, Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.
teachings.quote: Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do.
teachings.title: Father, Forgive Them — They Know Not What They Do

teachings.text: Jesus tells the repentant criminal crucified beside him, truly I say to you, today will you be with me in paradise.
teachings.quote: Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
teachings.title: Today You Will Be with Me in Paradise

teachings.text: With a loud voice Jesus cries, Father, into your hands I commend my spirit.
teachings.quote: Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit:
teachings.title: Father, Into Your Hands I Commend My Spirit

teachings.text: From the cross Jesus says to his mother, Woman, your son, and to the beloved disciple, your mother.
teachings.quote: Woman, behold thy son! Behold thy mother!
teachings.title: Woman, Behold Your Son — Behold Your Mother

teachings.text: Jesus says from the cross, I thirst.
teachings.quote: I thirst.
teachings.title: I Thirst

teachings.text: Jesus cries out from the cross, It is finished.
teachings.quote: It is finished:
teachings.title: It Is Finished

teachings.text: Jesus joins the two disciples on the Emmaus road and asks what they are discussing as they walk so sadly.
teachings.quote: What manner of communications are these that ye have one to another, as ye walk, and are sad?
teachings.title: The Risen Christ Joins the Emmaus Travelers

teachings.text: Jesus walks with the Emmaus disciples and asks what things, drawing out their account of Jesus of Nazareth.
teachings.quote: What things?
teachings.title: What Things? Drawing Out the Emmaus Account

teachings.text: Jesus calls the two disciples fools and slow of heart to believe the prophets, asking whether the Christ had to suffer to enter his glory.
teachings.quote: O fools, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken: Ought not Christ to have suffered these things, and to enter into his glory?
teachings.title: Slow of Heart to Believe the Prophets

teachings.text: Jesus appears among the gathered disciples on the resurrection evening and greets them, saying peace to you.
teachings.quote: Peace be unto you.
teachings.title: Peace Be to You — First Easter Greeting

teachings.text: Jesus asks why they are troubled and why doubts arise in their hearts. He bids them handle his hands and feet, for a spirit has no flesh and bones. He reminds them that Moses, the prophets, and the psalms all speak of him.
teachings.quote: Why are ye troubled? and why do thoughts arise in your hearts? Behold my hands and my feet, that it is I myself: handle me, and see; for a spirit hath not flesh and bones, as ye see me have. These are the words which I spake unto you, while I was yet with you, that all things must be fulfilled, which were written in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the psalms, concerning me.
teachings.title: Handle Me and See — I Am No Spirit

teachings.text: Jesus asks the disciples whether they have any food there.
teachings.quote: Have ye here any meat?
teachings.title: Do You Have Any Food Here?

teachings.text: Jesus tells the disciples it is written that the Christ would suffer and rise the third day, that repentance and forgiveness of sins would be preached in his name to all nations beginning at Jerusalem, and that they are witnesses of these things.
teachings.quote: Thus it is written, and thus it behoved Christ to suffer, and to rise from the dead the third day: And that repentance and remission of sins should be preached in his name among all nations, beginning at Jerusalem. And ye are witnesses of these things.
teachings.title: Repentance and Forgiveness Preached to All Nations

teachings.text: Jesus asks Mary why she weeps and calls her by name, sending her to tell his brethren he ascends to his Father. He gives the disciples peace, sends them as he was sent with the Holy Spirit, and grants authority to remit or retain sins.
teachings.quote: Woman, why weepest thou? whom seekest thou? Mary. Touch me not; for I am not yet ascended to my Father: but go to my brethren, and say unto them, I ascend unto my Father, and your Father; and to my God, and your God. Peace be unto you. Peace be unto you: as my Father hath sent me, even so send I you. Receive ye the Holy Ghost: Whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them; and whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained.
teachings.title: Mary, Go Tell My Brethren I Ascend

teachings.text: From the shore Jesus asks if they have food and tells them to cast the net on the right side and they will find.
teachings.quote: Children, have ye any meat? Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find.
teachings.title: Cast the Net on the Right Side

teachings.text: Jesus instructs the disciples to bring of the fish they have just caught.
teachings.quote: Bring of the fish which ye have now caught.
teachings.title: Bring the Fish You Have Just Caught

teachings.text: Jesus invites the disciples to come and dine.
teachings.quote: Come and dine.
teachings.title: Come and Dine

teachings.text: Jesus returns eight days later with Thomas present and greets the disciples, saying peace to you.
teachings.quote: Peace be unto you.
teachings.title: Peace to You — Jesus Returns to the Disciples

teachings.text: Jesus tells Thomas to reach his finger and see his hands, and to thrust his hand into his side, charging him not to be faithless but believing. He declares blessed are those who have not seen and yet believed.
teachings.quote: Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing. Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.
teachings.title: Thomas, Reach Here Your Hand — Stop Doubting

categories.title: Eschatology and the End Times
categories.description: The Olivet Discourse (Matthew 24–25, Mark 13, Luke 21) is the primary source for this category.

teachings.text: Jesus foretells the destruction of the temple, declaring that there will not be left one stone upon another that will not be thrown down.
teachings.quote: See ye not all these things? verily I say unto you, There shall not be left here one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down.
teachings.title: Not One Stone Left Upon Another

teachings.text: Jesus warns his disciples to take heed that no one deceive them, for many will come in his name claiming to be Christ; iniquity will abound and the love of many will grow cold.
teachings.quote: Take heed that no man deceive you. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many. And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another. And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many. And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold.
teachings.title: Beware of False Christs and Deception

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples they will hear of wars and rumors of wars but not be troubled, for nation will rise against nation and there will be famines and earthquakes — these are the beginning of sorrows.
teachings.quote: And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet. For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places. All these are the beginning of sorrows.
teachings.title: Wars, Famines, and Earthquakes: Beginning of Sorrows

teachings.text: Jesus declares that this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world for a witness, and then the end will come.
teachings.quote: And this gospel of the kingdom shall be preached in all the world for a witness unto all nations; and then shall the end come.
teachings.title: Gospel Preached to All Nations, Then the End

teachings.text: Jesus warns that when his hearers see the abomination of desolation standing in the holy place, those in Judea must flee to the mountains without turning back, for then will be great tribulation such as has not been since the beginning of the world; for the elect's sake those days will be shortened.
teachings.quote: When ye therefore shall see the abomination of desolation, spoken of by Daniel the prophet, stand in the holy place, (whoso readeth, let him understand:) Then let them which be in Judaea flee into the mountains: Let him which is on the housetop not come down to take any thing out of his house: Neither let him which is in the field return back to take his clothes. And woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck in those days! But pray ye that your flight be not in the winter, neither on the sabbath day: For then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be. And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect’s sake those days shall be shortened.
teachings.title: The Abomination of Desolation and Great Tribulation

teachings.text: Jesus warns that false christs and false prophets will arise and show great signs, so that, if possible, even the elect will be deceived.
teachings.quote: For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect.
teachings.title: False Prophets Who Could Deceive the Elect

teachings.text: Jesus says after that tribulation the sun will be darkened and the stars will fall; then the sign of the Son of Man will appear, and the tribes of the earth will mourn at his coming in the clouds with power and great glory.
teachings.quote: ¶ Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
teachings.title: The Sun Darkened and the Son of Man's Sign

teachings.text: Jesus weeps over Jerusalem, lamenting that she did not know the things that belong to her peace; the days will come when her enemies will lay her with the ground and not leave one stone upon another, because she knew not her visitation.
teachings.quote: If thou hadst known, even thou, at least in this thy day, the things which belong unto thy peace! but now they are hid from thine eyes. For the days shall come upon thee, that thine enemies shall cast a trench about thee, and compass thee round, and keep thee in on every side, And shall lay thee even with the ground, and thy children within thee; and they shall not leave in thee one stone upon another; because thou knewest not the time of thy visitation.
teachings.title: Jerusalem Weeps over Her Missed Visitation

subcategories.title: The Return of the Son of Man

teachings.text: Jesus declares that his disciples will be hated of all men for his name's sake, but he that endures to the end will be saved.
teachings.quote: And ye shall be hated of all men for my name’s sake: but he that endureth to the end shall be saved.
teachings.title: Endure to the End and Be Saved

teachings.text: Jesus promises his followers that when the Son of Man sits on his throne of glory, they will sit on twelve thrones judging Israel's tribes.
teachings.quote: Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of man shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
teachings.title: Twelve Thrones Judging Israel at the Renewal

teachings.text: Jesus declares the Son of Man's coming will be like lightning from east to west, and as in Noah's days they ate and married till the flood came, so will his coming be; he says heaven and earth will pass away but his words will not, and that of that day no one knows — not the angels, but the Father only.
teachings.quote: For as the lightning cometh out of the east, and shineth even unto the west; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be. For wheresoever the carcase is, there will the eagles be gathered together. ¶ Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other. Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh: So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors. Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass, till all these things be fulfilled. Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away. ¶ But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only. But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be. For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.
teachings.title: The Son of Man's Coming Like Lightning

teachings.text: Jesus declares that the sign of the Son of Man will appear and the tribes of the earth will mourn at his coming in the clouds with power, and he will send his angels with a trumpet to gather his elect from the four winds.
teachings.quote: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.
teachings.title: Angels Sent to Gather the Elect at His Coming

teachings.text: Jesus says that two will be in the field, the one taken and the other left, and two women will be grinding at the mill, the one taken and the other left.
teachings.quote: Then shall two be in the field; the one shall be taken, and the other left. Two women shall be grinding at the mill; the one shall be taken, and the other left.
teachings.title: One Taken, One Left — the Day of the Lord

teachings.text: Jesus warns his disciples they will long for the days of the Son of Man unseen, and not to chase rumors of his coming.
teachings.quote: The days will come, when ye shall desire to see one of the days of the Son of man, and ye shall not see it. And they shall say to you, See here; or, see there: go not after them, nor follow them.
teachings.title: Do Not Chase Rumors of the Son of Man's Coming

teachings.text: Jesus declares from the throne that he makes all things new, promising the water of life to the thirsty and warning the unfaithful of the lake of fire.
teachings.title: All Things New: Water of Life or Lake of Fire

teachings.text: Jesus charges his hearers to watch, for they know not what hour their Lord does come.
teachings.quote: ¶ Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.
teachings.title: Watch — You Do Not Know the Hour

teachings.text: Jesus tells of a faithful and wise servant whom his lord makes ruler over his household; when his lord finds him so doing he will set him over all his goods, but if that evil servant says his lord delays his coming and beats his fellows, his lord will come at an unexpected hour and appoint him with the hypocrites where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
teachings.quote: Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord hath made ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season? Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing. Verily I say unto you, That he shall make him ruler over all his goods. But and if that evil servant shall say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; And shall begin to smite his fellowservants, and to eat and drink with the drunken; The lord of that servant shall come in a day when he looketh not for him, and in an hour that he is not aware of, And shall cut him asunder, and appoint him his portion with the hypocrites: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
teachings.title: The Faithful and Unfaithful Servant

teachings.text: Jesus charges his disciples to keep their lamps burning like men waiting for their lord's return; blessed are those he finds watching, for he will gird himself and serve them — and the Son of Man comes at an unexpected hour.
teachings.quote: Let your loins be girded about, and your lights burning; And ye yourselves like unto men that wait for their lord, when he will return from the wedding; that when he cometh and knocketh, they may open unto him immediately. Blessed are those servants, whom the lord when he cometh shall find watching: verily I say unto you, that he shall gird himself, and make them to sit down to meat, and will come forth and serve them. And if he shall come in the second watch, or come in the third watch, and find them so, blessed are those servants. And this know, that if the goodman of the house had known what hour the thief would come, he would have watched, and not have suffered his house to be broken through. Be ye therefore ready also: for the Son of man cometh at an hour when ye think not.
teachings.title: The Servants with Lamps Lit

teachings.text: Jesus interrupts the bowl-judgment vision to declare he comes as a thief, and blessed is he who watches and keeps his garments.
teachings.title: I Come as a Thief — Blessed Are the Watchful

teachings.text: Jesus declares I come quickly — blessed is he that keeps the sayings of the prophecy of this book — and that his reward is with him to give every man according as his work will be, affirming surely I come quickly.
teachings.quote: Behold, I come quickly: blessed is he that keepeth the sayings of the prophecy of this book. And, behold, I come quickly; and my reward is with me, to give every man according as his work shall be. Surely I come quickly.
teachings.title: Behold, I Come Quickly with My Reward

subcategories.title: The Fig Tree and the Unknown Hour

teachings.text: Jesus draws a parable from the fig tree: as its branch becoming tender and putting forth leaves shows that summer is near, so when his hearers see all these things they may know that it is near, even at the doors.
teachings.quote: Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh: So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.
teachings.title: The Fig Tree

teachings.text: Jesus declares that heaven and earth will pass away but his words will not pass away, says that of that day and hour knows no man — not the angels of heaven, but the Father only — and likens his coming to a thief whose hour the householder does not know, charging his hearers therefore to be ready.
teachings.quote: Heaven and earth shall pass away, but my words shall not pass away. ¶ But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only. But know this, that if the goodman of the house had known in what watch the thief would come, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be broken up. Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh.
teachings.title: Heaven and Earth Will Pass — His Words Will Not

subcategories.title: The Certainty and Scope of Judgment

teachings.text: Jesus declares it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah at the judgment than for cities that reject his messengers, and says the hour comes when all in the graves will hear his voice and come forth to life or damnation.
teachings.quote: Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.
teachings.title: All in the Graves Will Hear His Voice

teachings.text: Jesus says men will give account for every idle word, and his word will judge those who reject him on the last day.
teachings.quote: But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.
teachings.title: Every Idle Word Will Face Judgment

teachings.text: Jesus declares that Nineveh and the queen of the South will condemn this generation, for one greater than Jonah and Solomon is here.
teachings.quote: The men of Nineveh shall rise in judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: because they repented at the preaching of Jonas; and, behold, a greater than Jonas is here. The queen of the south shall rise up in the judgment with this generation, and shall condemn it: for she came from the uttermost parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon; and, behold, a greater than Solomon is here.
teachings.title: Nineveh and the Queen of the South Will Condemn

teachings.text: Jesus says the Son of Man will come in the glory of his Father with his angels and reward every man according to his works, for the Father has committed all judgment to the Son.
teachings.quote: For the Son of man shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.
teachings.title: The Father Has Given All Judgment to the Son

teachings.text: Jesus says he goes his way and his hearers will seek him and die in their sins, for where he goes they cannot come.
teachings.quote: I go my way, and ye shall seek me, and shall die in your sins: whither I go, ye cannot come.
teachings.title: Where I Go You Cannot Come

teachings.text: Jesus tells the crowd the voice came for their sakes; now is the judgment of this world, and its prince will be cast out.
teachings.quote: This voice came not because of me, but for your sakes. Now is the judgment of this world: now shall the prince of this world be cast out.
teachings.title: Now Is the Judgment of This World

teachings.text: Jesus warns that anger with a brother brings danger of judgment, calling him Raca brings the council, and saying You fool brings hell fire.
teachings.quote: But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment... but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.
teachings.title: Anger, Contempt, and the Danger of Hell

teachings.text: Jesus charges that if eye or hand offends, cut it off — better to lose one member than have the whole body cast into hell.
teachings.quote: And if thy right eye offend thee, pluck it out, and cast it from thee: for it is profitable for thee that one of thy members should perish, and not that thy whole body should be cast into hell.
teachings.title: Cut Off What Offends Rather Than Face Hell

teachings.text: Jesus declares that the children of the kingdom will be cast out into outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
teachings.quote: But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
teachings.title: Cast Into Outer Darkness with Weeping and Gnashing

teachings.text: Jesus tells his disciples to fear not the killers of the body but him who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
teachings.quote: And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
teachings.title: Fear God Who Can Destroy Soul and Body

teachings.text: Jesus declares that at the end of the age angels will cast the wicked into the furnace of fire, with wailing and gnashing of teeth.
teachings.quote: And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.
teachings.title: The Wicked Cast Into the Furnace of Fire

teachings.text: Jesus says if a hand or foot offends, cut it off — better to enter life maimed than with two hands or two feet to be cast into everlasting fire, into hell, where the worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.
teachings.quote: Wherefore if thy hand or thy foot offend thee, cut them off, and cast them from thee: it is better for thee to enter into life halt or maimed, rather than having two hands or two feet to be cast into everlasting fire.
teachings.title: Everlasting Fire Where the Worm Does Not Die

teachings.text: Jesus tells how the king binds the man hand and foot and casts him into outer darkness, with weeping and gnashing of teeth.
teachings.quote: Bind him hand and foot, and take him away, and cast him into outer darkness; there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
teachings.title: Cast Into Outer Darkness at the King's Judgment

teachings.text: Jesus cries out to the scribes and Pharisees as serpents and a brood of vipers, asking how they will escape the damnation of hell.
teachings.quote: Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?
teachings.title: Serpents — How Will You Escape Damnation?

teachings.text: Jesus declares those on his left will go into everlasting fire prepared for the devil — to everlasting punishment, the righteous to life eternal.
teachings.quote: Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels: And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal.
teachings.title: Everlasting Punishment or Eternal Life

teachings.text: Jesus declares that many will come from the east and west and will sit down with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.quote: And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.
teachings.title: Many Will Feast with Abraham in the Kingdom

teachings.text: Jesus declares the hour is coming when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God and live, says he is the resurrection and the life, and promises to raise up at the last day all the Father has given him.
teachings.quote: Verily, verily, I say unto you, The hour is coming, and now is, when the dead shall hear the voice of the Son of God: and they that hear shall live.
teachings.title: I Am the Resurrection and the Life

teachings.text: Jesus tells of a rich man clothed in purple who fared sumptuously, and a beggar named Lazarus laid at his gate full of sores. When both died, Lazarus was carried into Abraham's bosom while the rich man in hell lifted his eyes in torment. Abraham tells him he received good things in life and Lazarus evil; now Lazarus is comforted, he tormented, and a great gulf is fixed between them.
teachings.quote: ¶ There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores, And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores. And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried; And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom. And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame. But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented. And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence. Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house: For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment. Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them. And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent. And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.
teachings.title: The Rich Man and Lazarus — A Great Gulf Fixed

teachings.text: Jesus, in Abraham's words, declares if they do not hear Moses and the prophets, they will not be persuaded though one rose from the dead.
teachings.quote: And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.
teachings.title: If They Reject Moses They Will Not Believe

categories.title: The Seven Churches
categories.description: Spoken directly by the risen Christ. Each letter follows a pattern: what he knows about the church, what concerns he raises, a call to repentance or faithfulness, and a promise to the one who overcomes.

subcategories.title: Introduction to the Seven Churches — The Vision of Christ

teachings.text: Jesus declares that he is Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, the Lord who is and was and is to come, the Almighty.
teachings.quote: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending,
teachings.title: I Am Alpha and Omega, Who Was and Is

teachings.text: Jesus, the first and the last, charges John to write what he sees and send it to the seven churches in Asia.
teachings.quote: I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last: What thou seest, write in a book, and send it unto the seven churches which are in Asia; unto Ephesus, and unto Smyrna, and unto Pergamos, and unto Thyatira, and unto Sardis, and unto Philadelphia, and unto Laodicea.
teachings.title: Write What You See to the Seven Churches

teachings.text: Jesus tells John not to fear, for he is the first and the last, alive forevermore, holding the keys of hell and death.
teachings.quote: Fear not; I am the first and the last: I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death.
teachings.title: Fear Not — I Hold the Keys of Death

teachings.text: Jesus charges John to write what is and what will be — the stars are the church angels and the candlesticks are the churches.
teachings.quote: Write the things which thou hast seen, and the things which are, and the things which shall be hereafter; The mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches.
teachings.title: The Stars Are Angels, Candlesticks Are Churches

teachings.text: Jesus closes each of the seven letters with the same summons, charging him that has an ear to hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
teachings.quote: He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches.
teachings.title: Let Him Who Has an Ear Hear the Spirit

subcategories.title: Ephesus — The Church That Left Its First Love

teachings.text: Jesus addresses the angel of the church of Ephesus as the one who holds the seven stars and walks among the seven golden candlesticks.
teachings.quote: Unto the angel of the church of Ephesus write; These things saith he that holdeth the seven stars in his right hand, who walketh in the midst of the seven golden candlesticks;
teachings.title: Jesus Addresses the Church at Ephesus

teachings.text: Jesus commends Ephesus for their works and patience and testing of false apostles, but holds against them that they have left their first love, charging them to remember from where they have fallen, repent, and do the first works, or he will remove their candlestick.
teachings.quote: I know thy works, and thy labour, and thy patience, and how thou canst not bear them which are evil: and thou hast tried them which say they are apostles, and are not, and hast found them liars: And hast borne, and hast patience, and for my name’s sake hast laboured, and hast not fainted. Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love. Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick out of his place, except thou repent.
teachings.title: You Have Left Your First Love — Repent

teachings.text: Jesus commends Ephesus that they hate the deeds of the Nicolaitans, which he also hates.
teachings.quote: But this thou hast, that thou hatest the deeds of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.
teachings.title: Ephesus Rightly Hates the Nicolaitan Deeds

teachings.text: Jesus promises that to him who overcomes he will give to eat of the tree of life in the paradise of God.
teachings.quote: He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of God.
teachings.title: To the Overcomer: The Tree of Life in Paradise

teachings.text: Jesus addresses the angel of the church in Smyrna as the first and the last, who was dead and is alive.
teachings.quote: And unto the angel of the church in Smyrna write; These things saith the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive;
teachings.title: Jesus Addresses the Suffering Church at Smyrna

teachings.text: Jesus tells Smyrna not to fear what they will suffer but to be faithful unto death, and he will give them a crown of life.
teachings.quote: I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan. Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.
teachings.title: Fear Not Suffering — Be Faithful unto Death

teachings.text: Jesus charges Smyrna to be faithful unto death for the crown of life; he who overcomes will not be hurt of the second death.
teachings.quote: Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life. He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death.
teachings.title: Faithful unto Death — Spared the Second Death

teachings.text: Jesus addresses the angel of the church in Pergamos as the one who has the sharp sword with two edges.
teachings.quote: And to the angel of the church in Pergamos write; These things saith he which hath the sharp sword with two edges;
teachings.title: Jesus Addresses Pergamum with the Two-Edged Sword

teachings.text: Jesus commends Pergamos for holding fast his name even where Satan dwells, but holds against them that some hold the doctrines of Balaam and the Nicolaitans, charging them to repent or he will fight against them with the sword of his mouth.
teachings.quote: I know thy works, and where thou dwellest, even where Satan’s seat is: and thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied my faith, even in those days wherein Antipas was my faithful martyr, who was slain among you, where Satan dwelleth. But I have a few things against thee, because thou hast there them that hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed unto idols, and to commit fornication. So hast thou also them that hold the doctrine of the Nicolaitans, which thing I hate. Repent; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will fight against them with the sword of my mouth.
teachings.title: Pergamum Holds Fast but Tolerates False Teaching

teachings.text: Jesus promises that to him who overcomes he will give the hidden manna and a white stone with a new name written on it.
teachings.quote: He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the hidden manna, and will give him a white stone, and in the stone a new name written, which no man knoweth saving he that receiveth it.
teachings.title: To the Overcomer: Hidden Manna and a White Stone

subcategories.title: Thyatira — The Church Tolerating False Teaching

teachings.text: Jesus addresses Thyatira as the Son of God, whose eyes are like a flame of fire and whose feet are like fine brass.
teachings.quote: And unto the angel of the church in Thyatira write; These things saith the Son of God, who hath his eyes like unto a flame of fire, and his feet are like fine brass;
teachings.title: Jesus Addresses Thyatira — Eyes of Fire, Feet of Brass

teachings.text: Jesus commends Thyatira's works but holds against them that they suffer Jezebel, who seduces his servants to fornication and idolatry, and declares he will cast her into a bed and her children into death, that all may know he searches hearts.
teachings.quote: I know thy works, and charity, and service, and faith, and thy patience, and thy works; and the last to be more than the first. Notwithstanding I have a few things against thee, because thou sufferest that woman Jezebel, which calleth herself a prophetess, to teach and to seduce my servants to commit fornication, and to eat things sacrificed unto idols. And I gave her space to repent of her fornication; and she repented not. Behold, I will cast her into a bed, and them that commit adultery with her into great tribulation, except they repent of their deeds. And I will kill her children with death; and all the churches shall know that I am he which searcheth the reins and hearts: and I will give unto every one of you according to your works.
teachings.title: Thyatira Tolerates Jezebel — Judgment Pronounced

teachings.text: Jesus tells the rest in Thyatira who have not held this doctrine that he will put on them no other burden.
teachings.quote: But unto you I say, and unto the rest in Thyatira, as many as have not this doctrine, and which have not known the depths of Satan, as they speak; I will put upon you none other burden.
teachings.title: No Extra Burden on Those Who Reject Jezebel

teachings.text: Jesus charges Thyatira to hold fast what they have until he comes, and promises that to him who overcomes he will give power over the nations and the morning star.
teachings.quote: But that which ye have already hold fast till I come. And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron; as the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers: even as I received of my Father. And I will give him the morning star.
teachings.title: Hold Fast Until I Come — Power Over Nations

teachings.text: Jesus tells Sardis that they have a name that they live but are dead, charging them to be watchful, strengthen what remains, and repent, or he will come on them as a thief at an hour they do not know.
teachings.quote: And unto the angel of the church in Sardis write; These things saith he that hath the seven Spirits of God, and the seven stars; I know thy works, that thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead. Be watchful, and strengthen the things which remain, that are ready to die: for I have not found thy works perfect before God. Remember therefore how thou hast received and heard, and hold fast, and repent. If therefore thou shalt not watch, I will come on thee as a thief, and thou shalt not know what hour I will come upon thee.
teachings.title: Sardis Has a Name but Is Dead — Repent

teachings.text: Jesus says a few in Sardis have not defiled their garments, and they will walk with him in white, for they are worthy.
teachings.quote: Thou hast a few names even in Sardis which have not defiled their garments; and they shall walk with me in white: for they are worthy.
teachings.title: A Few in Sardis Walk Undefiled

teachings.text: Jesus promises he who overcomes will wear white, with his name kept in the book of life and confessed before the Father.
teachings.quote: He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.
teachings.title: Overcomers in White with Names in the Book of Life

teachings.text: Jesus addresses Philadelphia as the holy and true one with the key of David — opens what none can shut, shuts what none can open.
teachings.quote: And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia write; These things saith he that is holy, he that is true, he that hath the key of David, he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth;
teachings.title: Philadelphia: He Holds the Key of David

teachings.text: Jesus tells Philadelphia he has set before them an open door no one can shut, for they have a little strength and have kept his word, and promises to keep them from the hour of trial that comes upon all the world.
teachings.quote: I know thy works: behold, I have set before thee an open door, and no man can shut it: for thou hast a little strength, and hast kept my word, and hast not denied my name. Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet, and to know that I have loved thee. Because thou hast kept the word of my patience, I also will keep thee from the hour of temptation, which shall come upon all the world, to try them that dwell upon the earth.
teachings.title: An Open Door No One Can Shut

teachings.text: Jesus comes quickly and charges Philadelphia to hold fast their crown, and promises him who overcomes a pillar in the temple of his God.
teachings.quote: Behold, I come quickly: hold that fast which thou hast, that no man take thy crown. Him that overcometh will I make a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall go no more out: and I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, which is new Jerusalem, which cometh down out of heaven from my God: and I will write upon him my new name.
teachings.title: Hold Fast Your Crown — I Come Quickly

teachings.text: Jesus addresses the angel of the church of the Laodiceans as the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God.
teachings.quote: And unto the angel of the church of the Laodiceans write; These things saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God;
teachings.title: Jesus Addresses Laodicea — the Faithful Witness

teachings.text: Jesus rebukes Laodicea for being lukewarm and declares he will spit them out, telling them that though they say they are rich they are wretched and naked, counseling them to buy gold, white raiment, and eyesalve, and charging them to be zealous and repent.
teachings.quote: I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot: I would thou wert cold or hot. So then because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spue thee out of my mouth. Because thou sayest, I am rich, and increased with goods, and have need of nothing; and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked: I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich; and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear; and anoint thine eyes with eyesalve, that thou mayest see. As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten: be zealous therefore, and repent.
teachings.title: Lukewarm Laodicea — Repent or Be Spat Out

teachings.text: Jesus stands at the door and knocks; if any opens he will come in. He who overcomes will sit with him on his throne.
teachings.quote: Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me. To him that overcometh will I grant to sit with me in my throne, even as I also overcame, and am set down with my Father in his throne.
teachings.title: I Stand at the Door and Knock
